\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
py3plex provides scalable analysis and visualization of multilayer and multiplex networks in Python.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Key Features:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Multiplex and multilayer network structures

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{SQL\sphinxhyphen{}like DSL for network queries} — first\sphinxhyphen{}class feature

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
17+ multilayer statistics and centrality measures

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Community detection (Louvain, Infomap, multilayer modularity)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Random walk algorithms (Node2Vec, DeepWalk) for embeddings

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Publication\sphinxhyphen{}ready visualizations

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
High\sphinxhyphen{}performance I/O with Arrow/Parquet support

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Full NetworkX compatibility

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{DSL: Query Networks Like SQL}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The py3plex DSL lets you query networks using intuitive SQL\sphinxhyphen{}like syntax or a type\sphinxhyphen{}safe Python builder API:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{dsl}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{execute\PYGZus{}query}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{L}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} String DSL: Simple and readable}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{execute\PYGZus{}query}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{SELECT nodes WHERE layer=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{social}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{ AND degree \PYGZgt{} 5 }\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{COMPUTE betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Builder API: Type\PYGZhy{}safe with autocompletion}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{from\PYGZus{}layers}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{L}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{social}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{where}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{degree\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}gt}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{compute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{order\PYGZus{}by}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZhy{}betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{limit}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The DSL is \sphinxstylestrong{perfect for}:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Interactive network exploration

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Rapid prototyping

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Educational purposes

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Production pipelines

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the complete {\hyperref[\detokenize{user_guide/dsl::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{SQL\sphinxhyphen{}like DSL for Multilayer Networks}}}} guide for all features!
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\chapter{Quick Start}
\label{\detokenize{index:quick-start}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Install:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Create a multilayer network:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{core}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{multinet}

\PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}edges}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}
    \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Alice}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Carol}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Alice}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{colleagues}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{colleagues}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{list}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{basic\PYGZus{}stats}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{visualize\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{show}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{True}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See {\hyperref[\detokenize{getting_started/quickstart_5min::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{5\sphinxhyphen{}Minute Quickstart}}}} (5 min) or {\hyperref[\detokenize{getting_started/tutorial_10min::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{10\sphinxhyphen{}Minute Tutorial}}}} (10 min) for complete introductions.

\subsubsection{Basic Installation}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/installation:basic-installation}}

\paragraph{Install from GitHub (Recommended)}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/installation:install-from-github-recommended}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The latest version is always available on GitHub:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This installs the core py3plex library with all required dependencies.


\paragraph{Install from Source}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/installation:install-from-source}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For development or to access the latest features:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
git\PYG{+w}{ }clone\PYG{+w}{ }https://github.com/SkBlaz/py3plex.git
\PYG{n+nb}{cd}\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex
pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}e\PYG{+w}{ }.
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}e}} flag installs in editable mode, so changes to the source code are immediately available.


\paragraph{Docker Installation (Alternative)}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/installation:docker-installation-alternative}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For a containerized environment with all dependencies pre\sphinxhyphen{}installed, use Docker:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Clone the repository}
git\PYG{+w}{ }clone\PYG{+w}{ }https://github.com/SkBlaz/py3plex.git
\PYG{n+nb}{cd}\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Build the Docker image}
docker\PYG{+w}{ }build\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}t\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex:latest\PYG{+w}{ }.

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Run py3plex commands}
docker\PYG{+w}{ }run\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}rm\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex:latest\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}version
docker\PYG{+w}{ }run\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}rm\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex:latest\PYG{+w}{ }selftest
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Benefits of Docker installation:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
No Python environment setup required

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
All dependencies pre\sphinxhyphen{}installed and tested

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Consistent environment across different systems

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Isolated from system Python installation

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See {\hyperref[\detokenize{deployment/cli_and_docker::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Docker Usage Guide}}}} for complete Docker documentation including:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Building and running the container

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Working with data files via volume mounts

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Docker Compose usage

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Helper scripts (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{py3plex\sphinxhyphen{}docker.sh}})

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Batch processing and CI/CD integration

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Optional Dependencies}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/installation:optional-dependencies}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
py3plex offers several optional feature sets that can be installed separately:


\paragraph{Advanced Community Detection}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/installation:advanced-community-detection}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Install Infomap for advanced overlapping community detection:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex\PYG{o}{[}infomap\PYG{o}{]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Additional Algorithms}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/installation:additional-algorithms}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Install extra community detection algorithms (Louvain, cdlib):

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex\PYG{o}{[}algos\PYG{o}{]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Advanced Visualization}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/installation:advanced-visualization}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Install Plotly and igraph for interactive and advanced visualizations:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex\PYG{o}{[}viz\PYG{o}{]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Apache Arrow Support}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/installation:apache-arrow-support}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Install pyarrow for high\sphinxhyphen{}performance I/O with Arrow/Parquet formats:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex\PYG{o}{[}arrow\PYG{o}{]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Arrow format provides 2\sphinxhyphen{}3x faster read/write operations and better compression compared to JSON.
See {\hyperref[\detokenize{user_guide/io_and_formats::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{I/O and Serialization}}}} for details on using Arrow format.


\paragraph{Multiple Extras}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/installation:multiple-extras}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Install multiple feature sets at once:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex\PYG{o}{[}infomap,viz,algos,arrow\PYG{o}{]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Development Installation}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/installation:development-installation}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For contributors, install with development tools (testing, linting):

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Recommended (Makefile\sphinxhyphen{}based):}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
git\PYG{+w}{ }clone\PYG{+w}{ }https://github.com/SkBlaz/py3plex.git
\PYG{n+nb}{cd}\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex
make\PYG{+w}{ }setup\PYG{+w}{        }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Create virtual environment}
make\PYG{+w}{ }dev\PYGZhy{}install\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Install with dev dependencies}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Alternative (manual):}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
git\PYG{+w}{ }clone\PYG{+w}{ }https://github.com/SkBlaz/py3plex.git
\PYG{n+nb}{cd}\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex
pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}e\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}.[dev]\PYGZdq{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Both methods install:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
pytest and coverage tools

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
black, ruff, isort for code formatting

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
mypy for type checking

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
sphinx for documentation building

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{System Requirements}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/installation:system-requirements}}

\paragraph{Python Version}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/installation:python-version}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
py3plex requires Python 3.8 or higher. We test on:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Python 3.8

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Python 3.9

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Python 3.10

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Python 3.11

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Python 3.12

\end{itemize}


\paragraph{Platform Support}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/installation:platform-support}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
py3plex is cross\sphinxhyphen{}platform and tested on:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\paragraph{Infomap Community Detection}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/installation:infomap-community-detection}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For advanced community detection using Infomap:

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Option 1:} Use the bundled Python implementation (recommended):

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex\PYG{o}{[}infomap\PYG{o}{]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Option 2:} Download the C++ binary from the official source:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Website: \sphinxurl{https://www.mapequation.org/infomap/}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Follow platform\sphinxhyphen{}specific installation instructions

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Alternative:} Use the built\sphinxhyphen{}in Louvain algorithm (no binary needed):

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{algorithms}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{community\PYGZus{}detection}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{community\PYGZus{}louvain}
\PYG{n}{communities} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{community\PYGZus{}louvain}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{best\PYGZus{}partition}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{core\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Node2Vec Embeddings}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/installation:node2vec-embeddings}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For Node2Vec node embeddings, use pure Python alternatives:

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Option 1:} Use pecanpy (fast parallel implementation):

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }pecanpy
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Option 2:} Use node2vec package:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }node2vec
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Option 3:} Use py3plex’s built\sphinxhyphen{}in random walk implementation:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{algorithms}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{general}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{walkers}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{node2vec\PYGZus{}walk}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{generate\PYGZus{}walks}
\PYG{n}{walks} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{generate\PYGZus{}walks}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{core\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{num\PYGZus{}walks}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{walk\PYGZus{}length}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{80}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\subsubsection{Common Installation Issues}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/installation:common-installation-issues}}

\paragraph{Issue: “No module named ‘numpy’”}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/installation:issue-no-module-named-numpy}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Solution:} Install numpy first:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }numpy
pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Issue: Compilation errors on Windows}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/installation:issue-compilation-errors-on-windows}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Solution:} Install Visual C++ Build Tools:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Download from: \sphinxurl{https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/visual-cpp-build-tools/}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Install “Desktop development with C++”

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Retry installation

\end{enumerate}


\paragraph{Issue: “Permission denied” on Linux/macOS}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/installation:issue-permission-denied-on-linux-macos}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Solution:} Use pip install with \textendash{}user flag:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}user\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Or use a virtual environment (recommended).


\paragraph{Issue: Old version installed}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/installation:issue-old-version-installed}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Solution:} Upgrade to latest version:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}upgrade\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\subsection{5\sphinxhyphen{}Minute Quickstart}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/quickstart_5min:minute-quickstart}}\label{\detokenize{getting_started/quickstart_5min::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Create a multilayer network, compute statistics, and visualize—all in 5 minutes.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{You will learn:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Create a multilayer network with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add\_edges()}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Display network statistics with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{basic\_stats()}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute layer\sphinxhyphen{}specific metrics

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Visualize your network

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Query with the SQL\sphinxhyphen{}like DSL

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Installation}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/quickstart_5min:installation}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For Docker setup, see {\hyperref[\detokenize{getting_started/installation::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Installation and Setup}}}}.


\subsubsection{Create Your First Network}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/quickstart_5min:create-your-first-network}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{core}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{multinet}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Format: [source\PYGZus{}node, source\PYGZus{}layer, target\PYGZus{}node, target\PYGZus{}layer, weight]}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}edges}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}
    \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Alice}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Carol}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Alice}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{colleagues}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{colleagues}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{colleagues}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Dave}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{colleagues}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}
\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{list}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{basic\PYGZus{}stats}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Output:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

Number of edges: 4
Number of unique nodes (as node\PYGZhy{}layer tuples): 6
Number of unique node IDs (across all layers): 4
Nodes per layer:
  Layer \PYGZsq{}friends\PYGZsq{}: 3 nodes

\subsubsection{Visualize}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/quickstart_5min:visualize}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{visualization}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{multilayer}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{draw\PYGZus{}multilayer\PYGZus{}default}

\PYG{n}{draw\PYGZus{}multilayer\PYGZus{}default}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{display}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{True}\PYG{p}{)}

\subsubsection{Basic Analysis}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/quickstart_5min:basic-analysis}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{algorithms}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{statistics}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{multilayer\PYGZus{}statistics} \PYG{k}{as} \PYG{n}{mls}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Layer density: how connected is each layer?}

\subsubsection{Query with DSL}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/quickstart_5min:query-with-dsl}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Py3plex features a powerful SQL\sphinxhyphen{}like DSL for querying networks!

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{DSL Example: Network Queries}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use SQL\sphinxhyphen{}like queries for network exploration:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{dsl}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{execute\PYGZus{}query}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{L}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} String DSL syntax}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{execute\PYGZus{}query}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{SELECT nodes WHERE degree \PYGZgt{} 1}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Found }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{result}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{count}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ high\PYGZhy{}degree nodes}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Builder API (recommended for production)}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{from\PYGZus{}layers}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{L}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{where}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{degree\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}gt}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{compute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The DSL makes complex network analysis intuitive and concise!
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See {\hyperref[\detokenize{user_guide/dsl::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{SQL\sphinxhyphen{}like DSL for Multilayer Networks}}}} for complete DSL documentation.


\subsubsection{Key Concepts}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/quickstart_5min:key-concepts}}\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Node\sphinxhyphen{}layer pairs:} Nodes are \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(node\_id, layer\_id)}} tuples. Alice in friends is different from Alice in colleagues.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Layers preserve context:} Each layer represents a different relationship type. Statistics and algorithms respect layer boundaries.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{NetworkX compatible:} py3plex uses NetworkX internally. All NetworkX algorithms work.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Multilayer statistics:} Metrics like node activity and edge overlap reveal cross\sphinxhyphen{}layer patterns invisible to single\sphinxhyphen{}layer tools.

\end{enumerate}

\PYG{n}{plt}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{savefig}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{analysis.png}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{dpi}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{150}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{bbox\PYGZus{}inches}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{tight}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{plt}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{close}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

\subsubsection{Bonus: Using the DSL (1 min)}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/tutorial_10min:bonus-using-the-dsl-1-min}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The SQL\sphinxhyphen{}like DSL makes many analysis tasks even simpler:

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{DSL Example: Quick Analysis}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{dsl}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{L}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Find top influential nodes}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{where}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{degree\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}gt}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{3}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{compute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{pagerank}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{order\PYGZus{}by}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZhy{}betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{limit}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Display as DataFrame}
\PYG{n}{df} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}pandas}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Compare layers}
\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{layer\PYGZus{}id} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{1}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{2}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n}{layer\PYGZus{}result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
        \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
         \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{from\PYGZus{}layers}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{L}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{layer\PYGZus{}id}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
         \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{compute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
         \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Layer }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{layer\PYGZus{}id}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{layer\PYGZus{}result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{count}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ nodes}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\subsection{Common Issues and Troubleshooting}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/common_issues:common-issues-and-troubleshooting}}\label{\detokenize{getting_started/common_issues::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This guide helps you troubleshoot common problems when getting started with py3plex.


\subsubsection{Installation Issues}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/common_issues:installation-issues}}

\paragraph{“No module named ‘numpy’”}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/common_issues:no-module-named-numpy}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Problem:} Import error when trying to use py3plex.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Solution:} Install numpy first:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }numpy
pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Compilation Errors on Windows}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/common_issues:compilation-errors-on-windows}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Problem:} C++ compilation errors during installation on Windows.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Solution:} Install Visual C++ Build Tools:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Download from: \sphinxurl{https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/visual-cpp-build-tools/}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Install “Desktop development with C++”

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Retry installation

\end{enumerate}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{“Permission denied” on Linux/macOS}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/common_issues:permission-denied-on-linux-macos}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Problem:} Permission errors during pip install.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Solution 1:} Use pip install with \textendash{}user flag:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}user\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Solution 2:} Use a virtual environment (recommended):

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
python3\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}m\PYG{+w}{ }venv\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex\PYGZhy{}env
\PYG{n+nb}{source}\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex\PYGZhy{}env/bin/activate\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} On Windows: py3plex\PYGZhy{}env\PYGZbs{}Scripts\PYGZbs{}activate}
pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Old Version Installed}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/common_issues:old-version-installed}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Problem:} Changes not reflecting or documentation mentions newer features.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Solution:} Upgrade to the latest version:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}upgrade\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{Data Loading Issues}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/common_issues:data-loading-issues}}

\paragraph{File Not Found Errors}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/common_issues:file-not-found-errors}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Problem:} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{FileNotFoundError}} when loading networks.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Solution 1:} Use absolute paths:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{os}

\PYG{n}{network\PYGZus{}path} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{/absolute/path/to/data.edgelist}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{load\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{network\PYGZus{}path}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{edgelist}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{directed}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{False}
\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Solution 2:} Ensure you’re running from the correct directory:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{os}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Check current directory}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Current directory:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{os}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{getcwd}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} List files}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Files:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{os}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{listdir}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{.}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Solution 3:} Use paths relative to script location:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{os}

\PYG{n}{script\PYGZus{}dir} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{os}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{path}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{dirname}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{os}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{path}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{abspath}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n+nv+vm}{\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}file\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{data\PYGZus{}path} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{os}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{path}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{join}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{script\PYGZus{}dir}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{data}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{network.edgelist}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Empty or Malformed Networks}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/common_issues:empty-or-malformed-networks}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Problem:} Network loads but has no nodes or edges.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Solution:} Check file format matches input\_type:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} For simple edge lists (source target)}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{load\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{data.txt}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{edgelist}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} For multilayer edge lists (source target layer)}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{load\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{data.txt}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{multiedgelist}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Always verify after loading}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{basic\PYGZus{}stats}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{Visualization Issues}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/common_issues:visualization-issues}}

\paragraph{Visualization Not Showing}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/common_issues:visualization-not-showing}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Problem:} No window appears when calling visualization functions.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Solution 1:} For Jupyter notebooks, add at the top:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{o}{\PYGZpc{}}\PYG{n}{matplotlib} \PYG{n}{inline}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Solution 2:} For scripts, explicitly show the plot:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{matplotlib}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{pyplot}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{as}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{plt}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Your visualization code}
\PYG{n}{draw\PYGZus{}multilayer\PYGZus{}default}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{display}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{False}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Explicitly show}
\PYG{n}{plt}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{show}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Solution 3:} Save to file instead of displaying:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{visualization}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{multilayer}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{hairball\PYGZus{}plot}
\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{matplotlib}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{pyplot}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{as}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{plt}

\PYG{n}{plt}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{figure}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{figsize}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{hairball\PYGZus{}plot}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{core\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{layout\PYGZus{}algorithm}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{force}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{plt}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{savefig}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{network.png}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{dpi}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{150}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{bbox\PYGZus{}inches}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{tight}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{plt}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{close}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{“No Display Found” Error}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/common_issues:no-display-found-error}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Problem:} Error on headless servers or SSH sessions without X11.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Solution:} Use Agg backend for matplotlib:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{matplotlib}
\PYG{n}{matplotlib}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{use}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Agg}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Must be before importing pyplot}
\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{matplotlib}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{pyplot}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{as}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{plt}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Now visualization will save to file instead of displaying}
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{visualization}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{multilayer}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{draw\PYGZus{}multilayer\PYGZus{}default}
\PYG{n}{draw\PYGZus{}multilayer\PYGZus{}default}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{display}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{False}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{plt}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{savefig}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{output.png}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Blurry or Low\sphinxhyphen{}Quality Plots}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/common_issues:blurry-or-low-quality-plots}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Problem:} Plots look pixelated or blurry.

\subsubsection{Performance Issues}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/common_issues:performance-issues}}

\paragraph{Very Slow Loading}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/common_issues:very-slow-loading}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Problem:} Loading large networks takes too long.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Solution 1:} Use Arrow/Parquet format for large networks:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Install Arrow support}
pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex\PYG{o}{[}arrow\PYG{o}{]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{io}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{read}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{write}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Save in efficient format}
\PYG{n}{write}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{network.arrow}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Load much faster}
\PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{read}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{network.arrow}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Solution 2:} Process in chunks or use subnetworks:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Extract a single layer for testing}
\PYG{n}{layer\PYGZus{}1} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{subnetwork}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{layer1}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{subset\PYGZus{}by}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{layers}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Work with the smaller network}

\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\PYG{p}{)}

    \PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{key}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{)}

\subsubsection{What are Multilayer Networks?}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/multilayer_networks_101:what-are-multilayer-networks}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A \sphinxstylestrong{multilayer network} models systems with multiple types of relationships, node types, or interaction contexts.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Example:} A researcher’s social world includes coauthors, colleagues, students, and Twitter followers. These are different relationship types with different meanings. A multilayer network keeps them as separate \sphinxstylestrong{layers} rather than flattening into one graph.

\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}edges}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}
    \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{A}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{2020}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{B}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{2020}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{A}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{2021}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{B}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{2021}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Examples:} Communication over time, social dynamics, disease spread.


\paragraph{Interdependent Networks}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/multilayer_networks_101:interdependent-networks}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Multiple networks where nodes depend on each other.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Examples:} Power grid depends on communication network, supply chains, cyber\sphinxhyphen{}physical systems.


\subsubsection{When to Use Multilayer Networks}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/multilayer_networks_101:when-to-use-multilayer-networks}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use multilayer modeling when:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Multiple relationship types matter} — Friendship and professional connections behave differently

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Node roles vary by context} — A hub in work network may be peripheral in hobby network

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Layer interactions are important} — Transportation failures in one mode affect others

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Temporal evolution matters} — Relationships change over time

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{System\sphinxhyphen{}level properties emerge} — Cross\sphinxhyphen{}layer dependencies affect resilience

\end{enumerate}


\subsubsection{Choosing a Modeling Approach}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/multilayer_networks_101:choosing-a-modeling-approach}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Ask these questions:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Layers vs. attributes?} If relationships have different \sphinxstyleemphasis{types} \(\rightarrow\) use layers. If they vary only in \sphinxstyleemphasis{weight} \(\rightarrow\) use edge attributes.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Same or different nodes?} Same entities in all layers \(\rightarrow\) multiplex. Different entity types \(\rightarrow\) heterogeneous.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Coupling strength?} Identity coupling only \(\rightarrow\) \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{omega=1.0}}. Nodes can differ \(\rightarrow\) lower omega.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Temporal structure?} Yes \(\rightarrow\) time\sphinxhyphen{}sliced layers. No \(\rightarrow\) aggregate into static network.

\end{enumerate}


\subsubsection{What Goes Wrong When You Flatten}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/multilayer_networks_101:what-goes-wrong-when-you-flatten}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Community structure destroyed:} Flattening can create spurious bridges between groups that are distinct in the layer structure.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Centrality becomes misleading:} A researcher with 2 coauthors and 500 Twitter followers has degree 502 when flattened, but academic influence is only 2.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Path analysis fails:} Email \(\rightarrow\) meeting transitions matter for information flow but are invisible in a flattened network.


\subsubsection{Common Pitfalls}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/multilayer_networks_101:common-pitfalls}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Over\sphinxhyphen{}aggregating} — Combining layers that should stay separate

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Under\sphinxhyphen{}aggregating} — Too many sparse layers (use edge weights instead)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Ignoring coupling} — Treating layers as independent when nodes correspond

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Wrong coupling strength} — Too high forces artificial consistency; too low loses information

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Mismatched identifiers} — Same entity must have same ID across layers

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Key Terminology}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/multilayer_networks_101:key-terminology}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Intra\sphinxhyphen{}layer edges} — Within a single layer

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer edges} — Between layers (often identity edges connecting same node)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Node\sphinxhyphen{}layer pairs} — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(node\_id, layer\_id)}} tuples, the fundamental unit

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Supra\sphinxhyphen{}adjacency matrix} — Block matrix encoding both intra\sphinxhyphen{} and inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer connections

\end{itemize}

\subsection{Chapter 4: The py3plex Core Model}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/py3plex_core_model:chapter-4-the-py3plex-core-model}}\label{\detokenize{concepts/py3plex_core_model::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{In which we look under the hood at how py3plex represents multilayer networks, understand the node\sphinxhyphen{}layer pair representation, and learn to work with the supra\sphinxhyphen{}adjacency matrix.}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
In the previous chapter, you learned \sphinxstyleemphasis{what} multilayer networks are conceptually. Now we’ll see \sphinxstyleemphasis{how} py3plex represents them in code—and why these design choices matter for your analysis.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Understanding the internal representation will help you:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Debug unexpected behavior (why does my network have twice as many nodes as I expected?)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Integrate with NetworkX (how do I use existing algorithms on my multilayer network?)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Scale to large networks (when should I use sparse matrices? how much memory will this take?)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Extend py3plex (how do I add my own algorithms?)

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Network Types: Multilayer vs Multiplex}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/py3plex_core_model:network-types-multilayer-vs-multiplex}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
py3plex supports two network types that determine how layers and inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer connections are handled:

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Multilayer Networks} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{network\_type=\textquotesingle{}multilayer\textquotesingle{}}}, default)

\sphinxAtStartPar
General multilayer networks where each layer can have a different set of nodes. No automatic coupling edges are created.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use when layers represent different node types (e.g., authors, papers, venues)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use when nodes naturally appear in only some layers

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer edges must be explicitly added

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{core}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{multinet}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Heterogeneous network: authors and papers are different node types}
\PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{multilayer}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}edges}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}
    \PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{source}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{author1}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{target}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{paper1}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
     \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{source\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{authors}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{target\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{papers}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}
\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Multiplex Networks} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{network\_type=\textquotesingle{}multiplex\textquotesingle{}}})

\sphinxAtStartPar
Special case where all layers share the same set of nodes but with different relationship types. After loading, coupling edges are automatically created between each node and its counterparts in other layers.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use when the same entities (people, cities) are connected via multiple relationship types

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Coupling edges are auto\sphinxhyphen{}generated with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{type=\textquotesingle{}coupling\textquotesingle{}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Filter coupling edges using \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{get\_edges(multiplex\_edges=False)}}

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Social network: same people, different relationship types}
\PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{multiplex}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{load\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends\PYGZus{}and\PYGZus{}colleagues.edges}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{multiplex\PYGZus{}edges}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Coupling edges are auto\PYGZhy{}created between (Alice, friends) \PYGZlt{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZgt{} (Alice, colleagues)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Get only explicit edges (exclude auto\PYGZhy{}coupling)}
\PYG{n}{explicit\PYGZus{}edges} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n+nb}{list}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}edges}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{multiplex\PYGZus{}edges}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{False}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Get all edges including coupling}
\PYG{n}{all\PYGZus{}edges} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n+nb}{list}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}edges}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{multiplex\PYGZus{}edges}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{True}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\subsubsection{The \sphinxstyleliteralintitle{\sphinxupquote{multi\_layer\_network}} Class}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/py3plex_core_model:the-multi-layer-network-class}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The central data structure in py3plex is the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{multi\_layer\_network}} class, which provides a high\sphinxhyphen{}level API for working with multilayer networks while maintaining full compatibility with NetworkX.


\paragraph{Basic Structure}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/py3plex_core_model:basic-structure}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{core}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{multinet}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Create a multilayer network}
\PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} The underlying NetworkX graph}
\PYG{n}{nx\PYGZus{}graph} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{core\PYGZus{}network}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} MultiDiGraph or MultiGraph}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Layer management}
\PYG{n}{layers} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}layers}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} List of layer names}
\PYG{n}{layer\PYGZus{}map} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{layer\PYGZus{}name\PYGZus{}map}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Layer name to ID mapping}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Key Components}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/py3plex_core_model:key-components}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{1. Core NetworkX Graph}

\sphinxAtStartPar
At its heart, py3plex uses a NetworkX \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{MultiDiGraph}} (for directed networks) or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{MultiGraph}} (for undirected networks) to store all nodes and edges.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Access the underlying graph}
\PYG{n}{G} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{core\PYGZus{}network}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Use any NetworkX function}
\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{networkx}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{as}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{nx}
\PYG{n}{betweenness} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{nx}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{G}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{2. Layer Encoding}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Nodes are internally encoded as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(node\_id, layer\_id)}} tuples to distinguish the same logical node across different layers.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Node \PYGZsq{}Alice\PYGZsq{} in layer \PYGZsq{}friends\PYGZsq{} is stored as (\PYGZsq{}Alice\PYGZsq{}, \PYGZsq{}friends\PYGZsq{})}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Alice}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Access all node\PYGZhy{}layer pairs}
\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{node\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}pair} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{node\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}pair}\PYG{p}{)}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} (\PYGZsq{}Alice\PYGZsq{}, \PYGZsq{}friends\PYGZsq{}), (\PYGZsq{}Bob\PYGZsq{}, \PYGZsq{}friends\PYGZsq{}), ...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{3. Layer Mapping}

\sphinxAtStartPar
py3plex maintains bidirectional mappings between layer names and internal layer IDs for efficient lookups.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Get layer mapping}
\PYG{n}{layer\PYGZus{}map} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{layer\PYGZus{}name\PYGZus{}map}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} \PYGZob{}\PYGZsq{}friends\PYGZsq{}: 0, \PYGZsq{}colleagues\PYGZsq{}: 1, ...\PYGZcb{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{4. Attributes}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Node and edge attributes are stored directly in the underlying NetworkX graph and can be accessed and modified using standard NetworkX patterns.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Add node with attributes}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{core\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Alice}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{age}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{l+m+mi}{30}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Add edge with attributes}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}edges}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}

\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}

\subsubsection{Internal Representation}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/py3plex_core_model:internal-representation}}

\paragraph{Node\sphinxhyphen{}Layer Pairs}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/py3plex_core_model:node-layer-pairs}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The key concept in py3plex’s internal model is the \sphinxstylestrong{node\sphinxhyphen{}layer pair}: a tuple \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(node\_id, layer\_id)}} that uniquely identifies a node in a specific layer.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Same logical node, different layers}
\PYG{n}{alice\PYGZus{}friends} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Alice}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{alice\PYGZus{}colleagues} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Alice}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{colleagues}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} These are treated as different nodes internally}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{alice\PYGZus{}friends}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{alice\PYGZus{}colleagues}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This representation allows:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The same logical entity to appear in multiple layers

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Different attributes per node\sphinxhyphen{}layer pair

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Efficient layer\sphinxhyphen{}specific operations

\end{itemize}

\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}

\subsubsection{Supra\sphinxhyphen{}Adjacency Matrix}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/py3plex_core_model:supra-adjacency-matrix}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The supra\sphinxhyphen{}adjacency matrix is a block matrix representation that encodes the entire multilayer network structure.


\paragraph{Mathematical Definition}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/py3plex_core_model:mathematical-definition}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For a multilayer network with \(L\) layers, the supra\sphinxhyphen{}adjacency matrix \(\mathbf{S}\) is:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\mathbf{S} = \begin{bmatrix}
A_1 & C_{12} & \cdots & C_{1L} \\
C_{21} & A_2 & \cdots & C_{2L} \\
\vdots & \vdots & \ddots & \vdots \\
C_{L1} & C_{L2} & \cdots & A_L
\end{bmatrix}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Where:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(A_\alpha\) is the adjacency matrix of layer \(\alpha\) (intra\sphinxhyphen{}layer connections)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(C_{\alpha\beta}\) is the coupling matrix between layers \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) (inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer connections)

\end{itemize}


\paragraph{Numeric Example}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/py3plex_core_model:numeric-example}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Consider a simple multiplex network with 3 nodes (A, B, C) and 2 layers. In layer 1, A\sphinxhyphen{}B are connected. In layer 2, B\sphinxhyphen{}C are connected. The nodes are the same across layers (multiplex structure).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Network structure:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
Layer 1:        Layer 2:
A \PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{} B   C     A   B \PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{} C
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Node ordering:} We order nodes as (A,L1), (B,L1), (C,L1), (A,L2), (B,L2), (C,L2).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Intra\sphinxhyphen{}layer blocks:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Layer 1 adjacency matrix (A\(\sb{\text{1}}\)):

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
     A   B   C
A [  0   1   0 ]
B [  1   0   0 ]
C [  0   0   0 ]
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Layer 2 adjacency matrix (A\(\sb{\text{2}}\)):

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
     A   B   C
A [  0   0   0 ]
B [  0   0   1 ]
C [  0   1   0 ]
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer coupling blocks (C\(\sb{\text{1}}\)\(\sb{\text{2}}\) and C\(\sb{\text{2}}\)\(\sb{\text{1}}\)):}

\sphinxAtStartPar
In a multiplex network, we typically add identity coupling—each node connects to itself across layers:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
C\(\sb{\text{1}}\)\(\sb{\text{2}}\) = C\(\sb{\text{2}}\)\(\sb{\text{1}}\)ᵀ =
     A   B   C
A [  1   0   0 ]
B [  0   1   0 ]
C [  0   0   1 ]
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Full supra\sphinxhyphen{}adjacency matrix (6×6):}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
          Layer 1        |     Layer 2
       A    B    C       |  A    B    C
L1  A [ 0    1    0      |  1    0    0 ]
    B [ 1    0    0      |  0    1    0 ]
    C [ 0    0    0      |  0    0    1 ]
   \PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}|\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}+\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}
L2  A [ 1    0    0      |  0    0    0 ]
    B [ 0    1    0      |  0    0    1 ]
    C [ 0    0    1      |  0    1    0 ]
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The diagonal 3×3 blocks are the within\sphinxhyphen{}layer adjacencies (A\(\sb{\text{1}}\) and A\(\sb{\text{2}}\)). The off\sphinxhyphen{}diagonal 3×3 blocks are the coupling matrices (C\(\sb{\text{1}}\)\(\sb{\text{2}}\) and C\(\sb{\text{2}}\)\(\sb{\text{1}}\)).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{What this enables:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Multilayer shortest paths:} A path from (A,L1) to (C,L2) must go through B: (A,L1)\(\rightarrow\)(B,L1)\(\rightarrow\)(B,L2)\(\rightarrow\)(C,L2)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Spectral methods:} Eigenvalues of S capture multilayer structure

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Matrix operations:} All linear algebra works on the full system

\end{itemize}


\paragraph{Construction}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/py3plex_core_model:construction}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{core}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{multinet}

\PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} ... add nodes and edges ...}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Get supra\PYGZhy{}adjacency matrix (sparse by default for efficiency)}
\PYG{n}{supra\PYGZus{}adj} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}supra\PYGZus{}adjacency\PYGZus{}matrix}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{sparse}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{True}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Dense version (for small networks only)}
\PYG{n}{supra\PYGZus{}adj\PYGZus{}dense} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}supra\PYGZus{}adjacency\PYGZus{}matrix}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{sparse}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{False}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Shape: (total\PYGZus{}nodes, total\PYGZus{}nodes)}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} where total\PYGZus{}nodes = sum of nodes across all layers}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Shape: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{supra\PYGZus{}adj}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{shape}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Memory Implications}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/py3plex_core_model:memory-implications}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The supra\sphinxhyphen{}adjacency matrix has size (N×L)\(\sp{\text{2}}\) where N is nodes per layer and L is layers:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Small network (100 nodes, 3 layers):} 300×300 = 90,000 entries \(\rightarrow\) \textasciitilde{}720 KB dense

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Medium network (1,000 nodes, 5 layers):} 5,000×5,000 = 25 million entries \(\rightarrow\) \textasciitilde{}200 MB dense

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Large network (10,000 nodes, 10 layers):} 100,000×100,000 = 10 billion entries \(\rightarrow\) impossible dense

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Always use sparse=True} for networks with more than \textasciitilde{}1,000 total node\sphinxhyphen{}layer pairs. Sparse matrices only store non\sphinxhyphen{}zero entries, reducing memory from O(N\(\sp{\text{2}}\)L\(\sp{\text{2}}\)) to O(edges + coupling).

\subsubsection{How py3plex Uses NetworkX Under the Hood}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/py3plex_core_model:how-py3plex-uses-networkx-under-the-hood}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
py3plex is built on top of NetworkX, using it as the storage and algorithm backend. Understanding this architecture helps you leverage the full NetworkX ecosystem.


\paragraph{The Role of MultiGraph/MultiDiGraph}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/py3plex_core_model:the-role-of-multigraph-multidigraph}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Internally, py3plex stores all nodes and edges in a single NetworkX \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{MultiGraph}} (for undirected) or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{MultiDiGraph}} (for directed networks). The multilayer structure is encoded through the node representation:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} What you write in py3plex:}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}edges}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}
    \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Alice}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Alice}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{colleagues}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{colleagues}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{list}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} What\PYGZsq{}s actually stored in NetworkX:}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Nodes: (\PYGZsq{}Alice\PYGZsq{}, \PYGZsq{}friends\PYGZsq{}), (\PYGZsq{}Bob\PYGZsq{}, \PYGZsq{}friends\PYGZsq{}),}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{}        (\PYGZsq{}Alice\PYGZsq{}, \PYGZsq{}colleagues\PYGZsq{}), (\PYGZsq{}Bob\PYGZsq{}, \PYGZsq{}colleagues\PYGZsq{})}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Edges: ((\PYGZsq{}Alice\PYGZsq{}, \PYGZsq{}friends\PYGZsq{}), (\PYGZsq{}Bob\PYGZsq{}, \PYGZsq{}friends\PYGZsq{})),}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{}        ((\PYGZsq{}Alice\PYGZsq{}, \PYGZsq{}colleagues\PYGZsq{}), (\PYGZsq{}Bob\PYGZsq{}, \PYGZsq{}colleagues\PYGZsq{}))}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This means:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{All NetworkX algorithms work directly} on the underlying graph

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Node\sphinxhyphen{}layer tuples are just nodes} to NetworkX—it doesn’t “know” about layers

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Attributes are stored as NetworkX attributes} and persist across operations

\end{enumerate}


\paragraph{Attribute Propagation}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/py3plex_core_model:attribute-propagation}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
When you add nodes or edges with attributes, they’re stored in the NetworkX graph:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Node attributes}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{core\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Alice}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{age}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{l+m+mi}{30}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{core\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Alice}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{role}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{admin}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Edge attributes}

\subsubsection{Design Trade\sphinxhyphen{}offs}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/py3plex_core_model:design-trade-offs}}

\paragraph{Node\sphinxhyphen{}Layer Pairs vs. Alternative Representations}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/py3plex_core_model:node-layer-pairs-vs-alternative-representations}}

py3plex’s node\sphinxhyphen{}layer pair representation is one of several possible designs. Here’s why it was chosen:

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Alternative 1: Separate graphs per layer}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Instead of py3plex:}

\PYG{n}{layer2} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{nx}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{Graph}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{layer1}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}edge}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Alice}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{layer2}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}edge}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Alice}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Pros:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Simple, familiar

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Easy layer\sphinxhyphen{}specific analysis

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cons:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
No representation of inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer edges

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Manual bookkeeping for cross\sphinxhyphen{}layer operations

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Can’t compute multilayer paths or centrality directly

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Alternative 2: Single graph with edge type attributes}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Instead of py3plex:}
\PYG{n}{G} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{nx}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{MultiGraph}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{G}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}edge}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Alice}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n+nb}{type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{G}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}edge}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Alice}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n+nb}{type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{colleagues}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Pros:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Single graph structure

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Edges carry type information

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cons:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Nodes can’t have layer\sphinxhyphen{}specific attributes

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Same node in different contexts is the same node (can’t have Alice be central in one layer and peripheral in another)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer edges to the same node are impossible

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{py3plex approach: Node\sphinxhyphen{}layer pairs}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} py3plex representation:}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}edges}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}
    \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Alice}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Alice}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{colleagues}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{colleagues}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{list}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Pros:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Preserves both intra\sphinxhyphen{}layer and inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer structure

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Allows layer\sphinxhyphen{}specific node attributes

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compatible with NetworkX algorithms

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Enables proper multilayer\sphinxhyphen{}specific operations

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Supports identity coupling and cross\sphinxhyphen{}layer edges

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cons:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Node names are tuples (less intuitive for simple cases)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Memory usage is multiplied by number of layers

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
NetworkX algorithms treat node\sphinxhyphen{}layer pairs as independent nodes (need py3plex wrappers for multilayer semantics)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{py3plex’s choice:} The node\sphinxhyphen{}layer pair approach was chosen because it correctly models multilayer semantics while maintaining NetworkX compatibility. The downsides (tuple names, memory) are acceptable trade\sphinxhyphen{}offs for the flexibility and correctness gained.


\paragraph{Consequences for Algorithm Implementation}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/py3plex_core_model:consequences-for-algorithm-implementation}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The node\sphinxhyphen{}layer pair design has implications:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Layer extraction is subsetting:} To get layer 1, you filter nodes where the layer component equals “layer1”

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Identity coupling is explicit:} Cross\sphinxhyphen{}layer edges between the same entity must be added explicitly (or automatically in multiplex mode)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Supra\sphinxhyphen{}matrix is derivable:} The supra\sphinxhyphen{}adjacency matrix can be computed from the graph structure

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{NetworkX algorithms work but need interpretation:} Betweenness on the full graph treats cross\sphinxhyphen{}layer edges as normal edges

\end{enumerate}


\paragraph{Consequences for I/O}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/py3plex_core_model:consequences-for-i-o}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The node\sphinxhyphen{}layer pair representation affects serialization:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Standard formats work:} GraphML, GML can store tuple nodes

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Human\sphinxhyphen{}readable formats need mapping:} Edgelists typically use separate columns for node and layer

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Arrow/Parquet are efficient:} Modern columnar formats handle the structure naturally

\end{enumerate}

\PYG{n}{nx}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{write\PYGZus{}gml}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{G\PYGZus{}export}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{output.gml}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\subsubsection{Performance Considerations}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/py3plex_core_model:performance-considerations}}

\paragraph{Sparse vs. Dense Matrices}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/py3plex_core_model:sparse-vs-dense-matrices}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For large networks, always use sparse matrix representations:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Good: Sparse matrix (efficient for large networks)}
\PYG{n}{supra\PYGZus{}adj} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}supra\PYGZus{}adjacency\PYGZus{}matrix}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{sparse}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{True}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Bad: Dense matrix (memory\PYGZhy{}intensive)}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Only use for small networks (\PYGZlt{} 1000 nodes)}
\PYG{n}{supra\PYGZus{}adj\PYGZus{}dense} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}supra\PYGZus{}adjacency\PYGZus{}matrix}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{sparse}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{False}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Memory Usage}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/py3plex_core_model:memory-usage}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Node\sphinxhyphen{}layer pairs mean that a node appearing in \(L\) layers occupies \(L\) times the memory of a single\sphinxhyphen{}layer network. For networks with many layers:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Consider layer\sphinxhyphen{}specific analysis when possible

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use subnetwork extraction to work with smaller portions

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
See {\hyperref[\detokenize{deployment/performance_scalability::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Performance and Scalability Best Practices}}}} for optimization strategies

\end{itemize}


\paragraph{Tensor\sphinxhyphen{}Like Indexing}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/py3plex_core_model:tensor-like-indexing}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
You can access nodes and edges using tensor\sphinxhyphen{}like notation:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{core}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{random\PYGZus{}generators}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Create a network}
\PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{random\PYGZus{}generators}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{random\PYGZus{}multilayer\PYGZus{}ER}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{100}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{3}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.05}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{directed}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{False}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Get some nodes and edges}
\PYG{n}{some\PYGZus{}nodes} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n+nb}{list}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{]}
\PYG{n}{some\PYGZus{}edges} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n+nb}{list}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}edges}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{]}

\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Node }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{some\PYGZus{}nodes}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ data: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{node\PYGZus{}data}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Edge data: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{edge\PYGZus{}data}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
