\subsubsection{Design Principles}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/py3plex_core_model:design-principles}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
py3plex follows several key design principles:

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{1. NetworkX Compatibility}

\sphinxAtStartPar
All operations maintain compatibility with NetworkX, allowing seamless use of the rich NetworkX ecosystem.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{2. Lazy Evaluation}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Expensive operations like supra\sphinxhyphen{}adjacency matrix construction are computed on demand and cached when appropriate.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{3. Graceful Degradation}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Optional features (like Infomap community detection or advanced visualizations) fail gracefully with informative error messages if dependencies are missing.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{4. Extensibility}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The modular design makes it easy to extend py3plex with custom algorithms and visualizations.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{5. Flexibility}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Multiple ways to construct and manipulate networks to suit different workflows and use cases.


\subsubsection{Comparison with Other Representations}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/py3plex_core_model:comparison-with-other-representations}}

\paragraph{Why Node\sphinxhyphen{}Layer Pairs?}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/py3plex_core_model:why-node-layer-pairs}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Alternative representations exist, but py3plex’s node\sphinxhyphen{}layer pair approach offers key advantages:

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Alternative: Separate graphs per layer}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Drawback:} Loses inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer information, requires manual bookkeeping for cross\sphinxhyphen{}layer operations.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Alternative: Single graph with edge type attributes}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Drawback:} Cannot distinguish node context across layers, loses layer\sphinxhyphen{}specific node attributes.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{py3plex approach: Node\sphinxhyphen{}layer pairs}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Advantages:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Preserves both intra\sphinxhyphen{}layer and inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer structure

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Allows layer\sphinxhyphen{}specific node attributes

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compatible with NetworkX algorithms

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Efficient for multilayer\sphinxhyphen{}specific operations

\end{itemize}

\sphinxstylestrong{Rationale:} NetworkX is the de facto standard for network analysis in Python. By building on it, py3plex:

\paragraph{Lazy Evaluation}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/design_principles:lazy-evaluation}}

\sphinxstylestrong{In practice:}

\label{\detokenize{concepts/design_principles:py3plex-vs-other-multilayer-tools}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Other tools (e.g., muxViz, pymnet):}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Often specialized or platform\sphinxhyphen{}specific

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
May have steep learning curves

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Limited algorithm libraries

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{py3plex:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Pure Python (easy installation)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Comprehensive algorithm library

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
NetworkX integration

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Active development

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Research\sphinxhyphen{}backed

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{What You Learned}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/design_principles:what-you-learned}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This chapter covered the design philosophy behind py3plex:

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Core principles:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Simple, off\sphinxhyphen{}the\sphinxhyphen{}shelf functionality} — work out of the box with minimal configuration

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{NetworkX compatibility} — leverage the entire NetworkX ecosystem

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Modular architecture} — import only what you need

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Implementation principles:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Flexibility} — multiple ways to accomplish tasks

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Lazy evaluation} — expensive operations computed on demand

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Graceful degradation} — optional features fail with helpful messages

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Explicit over implicit} — clear, predictable behavior

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Performance principles:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Sparse representations} — efficient for large networks

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Sensible defaults} — good starting parameters based on research

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Quality principles:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Comprehensive documentation} — every feature has examples

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Extensive testing} — validated against published results

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Reproducibility} — seed parameters for deterministic results

\end{itemize}

\subsection{Algorithm Landscape}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/algorithm_landscape:algorithm-landscape}}\label{\detokenize{concepts/algorithm_landscape::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This guide provides a narrative overview of the algorithm families available in py3plex, helping you understand when to use each type of algorithm for multilayer network analysis.


\subsubsection{Overview}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/algorithm_landscape:overview}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
py3plex provides algorithms in seven main categories:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Community Detection} \sphinxhyphen{} Finding groups of densely connected nodes

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Centrality \& Importance} \sphinxhyphen{} Measuring node and edge importance

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Network Statistics} \sphinxhyphen{} Computing network\sphinxhyphen{}level and layer\sphinxhyphen{}specific metrics

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Random Walks \& Embeddings} \sphinxhyphen{} Node representations and sampling

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Node Ranking \& Classification} \sphinxhyphen{} Ordering and classifying nodes

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Visualization \& Layout} \sphinxhyphen{} Rendering and spatial arrangement

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Benchmarking \& Generation} \sphinxhyphen{} Testing and synthetic network creation

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For detailed parameter lists and API reference, see {\hyperref[\detokenize{reference/algorithm_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Algorithm Roadmap}}}}.


\subsubsection{Community Detection}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/algorithm_landscape:community-detection}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Goal:} Identify groups of nodes that are more densely connected to each other than to the rest of the network.


\paragraph{When to Use}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/algorithm_landscape:when-to-use}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use community detection when you want to:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Discover functional modules in biological networks

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Find social groups in multilayer social networks

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Identify topical clusters in citation networks

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Understand organizational structure

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Detect anomalies (nodes that don’t fit any community)

\end{itemize}


\paragraph{Algorithm Families}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/algorithm_landscape:algorithm-families}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Modularity\sphinxhyphen{}Based Methods}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Best for:} Fast community detection on large networks

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Examples:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Louvain} \sphinxhyphen{} Fast, greedy modularity optimization

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Leiden} \sphinxhyphen{} Improved version of Louvain with better stability

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Multilayer Louvain} \sphinxhyphen{} Extends Louvain to multiple layers with inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer coupling

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Trade\sphinxhyphen{}offs:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\checkmark\) Fast (scales to millions of nodes)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\checkmark\) Easy to use (minimal parameters)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
✗ Resolution limit (may miss small communities)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
✗ Stochastic (different runs give different results)

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{algorithms}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{community\PYGZus{}detection}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{community\PYGZus{}louvain}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Single\PYGZhy{}layer Louvain}
\PYG{n}{partition} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{community\PYGZus{}louvain}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{best\PYGZus{}partition}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{core\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Multilayer Louvain}
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{algorithms}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{community\PYGZus{}detection}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{multilayer\PYGZus{}modularity}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{louvain\PYGZus{}multilayer}
\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{partition} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{louvain\PYGZus{}multilayer}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{gamma}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{omega}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Flow\sphinxhyphen{}Based Methods}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Best for:} Finding communities based on information flow

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Examples:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Infomap} \sphinxhyphen{} Minimizes description length of random walks

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Walktrap} \sphinxhyphen{} Based on random walk distances

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Trade\sphinxhyphen{}offs:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\checkmark\) Theoretically grounded (information theory)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\checkmark\) Finds hierarchical structure

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
✗ Slower than modularity methods

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
✗ May require external binaries

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{algorithms}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{community\PYGZus{}detection}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{community\PYGZus{}wrapper}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Infomap (requires binary)}
\PYG{n}{partition} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{community\PYGZus{}wrapper}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{infomap\PYGZus{}communities}\PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{core\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{n}{binary\PYGZus{}path}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{/path/to/infomap}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Overlapping Community Detection}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Best for:} Networks where nodes belong to multiple communities

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Examples:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{NoRC} \sphinxhyphen{} Network of Ranked Communities

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Clique Percolation} \sphinxhyphen{} Based on overlapping cliques

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Trade\sphinxhyphen{}offs:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\checkmark\) More realistic for many real networks

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\checkmark\) Captures multi\sphinxhyphen{}role nodes

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
✗ More complex to interpret

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
✗ Computationally expensive

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{algorithms}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{community\PYGZus{}detection}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{community\PYGZus{}wrapper}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} NoRC overlapping communities}
\PYG{n}{partition} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{community\PYGZus{}wrapper}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{NoRC\PYGZus{}communities}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{alpha}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.5}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Choosing a Community Detection Method}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/algorithm_landscape:choosing-a-community-detection-method}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use this decision tree:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
Do you need overlapping communities?
├─ Yes \(\rightarrow\) NoRC or Clique Percolation
└─ No
   └─ Is your network multilayer?
      ├─ Yes \(\rightarrow\) Multilayer Louvain or Leiden
      └─ No
         └─ What\PYGZsq{}s most important?
            ├─ Speed \(\rightarrow\) Louvain
            ├─ Stability \(\rightarrow\) Leiden
            └─ Theory \(\rightarrow\) Infomap
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{Centrality \& Importance}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/algorithm_landscape:centrality-importance}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Goal:} Quantify the importance of nodes or edges in the network.


\paragraph{When to Use}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/algorithm_landscape:id1}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use centrality measures when you want to:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Identify influential nodes (e.g., key proteins, opinion leaders)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Find bottlenecks in flow networks

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Prioritize nodes for intervention or study

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Understand network vulnerability

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Analyze node roles across layers

\end{itemize}


\paragraph{Algorithm Families}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/algorithm_landscape:id2}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Degree\sphinxhyphen{}Based Centrality}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Measures:} Local connectivity

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Examples:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Degree Centrality} \sphinxhyphen{} Number of connections

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Multilayer Degree} \sphinxhyphen{} Degree summed across layers

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Versatility} \sphinxhyphen{} Participation across layers

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{When to use:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Quick assessment of connectivity

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Identifying hubs

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Local importance measures

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{networkx}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{as}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{nx}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Single\PYGZhy{}layer degree centrality}
\PYG{n}{degree\PYGZus{}cent} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{nx}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{degree\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{core\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Multilayer versatility}
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{algorithms}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{statistics}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{multilayer\PYGZus{}statistics} \PYG{k}{as} \PYG{n}{mls}
\PYG{n}{versatility} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{mls}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{versatility\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{centrality\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Distance\sphinxhyphen{}Based Centrality}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Measures:} Global position in network

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Examples:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Closeness Centrality} \sphinxhyphen{} Average distance to all other nodes

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Betweenness Centrality} \sphinxhyphen{} Fraction of shortest paths through node

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Harmonic Centrality} \sphinxhyphen{} Harmonic mean of distances

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{When to use:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Identifying central nodes

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Finding information brokers

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Understanding information flow

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Betweenness centrality}
\PYG{n}{betweenness} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{nx}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{core\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Closeness centrality}
\PYG{n}{closeness} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{nx}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{closeness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{core\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Eigenvector\sphinxhyphen{}Based Centrality}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Measures:} Importance based on connections to important nodes

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Examples:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Eigenvector Centrality} \sphinxhyphen{} First eigenvector of adjacency matrix

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{PageRank} \sphinxhyphen{} Google’s ranking algorithm

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{HITS} \sphinxhyphen{} Hubs and authorities

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{When to use:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Ranking web pages or citations

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Finding influential nodes in social networks

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Authority/hub analysis

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} PageRank}
\PYG{n}{pagerank} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{nx}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{pagerank}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{core\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Eigenvector centrality}
\PYG{n}{eigenvector} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{nx}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{eigenvector\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{core\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Choosing a Centrality Measure}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/algorithm_landscape:choosing-a-centrality-measure}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Consider these questions:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Local vs. Global?}
\sphinxhyphen{} Local \(\rightarrow\) Degree centrality
\sphinxhyphen{} Global \(\rightarrow\) Closeness or betweenness

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Direct connections or influence?}
\sphinxhyphen{} Direct \(\rightarrow\) Degree
\sphinxhyphen{} Influence \(\rightarrow\) PageRank or eigenvector

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Network type?}
\sphinxhyphen{} Directed \(\rightarrow\) PageRank or HITS
\sphinxhyphen{} Undirected \(\rightarrow\) Any method
\sphinxhyphen{} Weighted \(\rightarrow\) Use weight\sphinxhyphen{}aware versions

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Computational cost?}
\sphinxhyphen{} Large network \(\rightarrow\) Degree or PageRank (fast)
\sphinxhyphen{} Small network \(\rightarrow\) Betweenness (expensive but informative)

\end{enumerate}


\subsubsection{Network Statistics}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/algorithm_landscape:network-statistics}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Goal:} Characterize network structure at the global, layer, or node level.


\paragraph{When to Use}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/algorithm_landscape:id3}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use network statistics when you want to:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compare networks quantitatively

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Understand structural properties

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Validate network models

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Monitor network evolution

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Detect anomalies

\end{itemize}


\paragraph{Statistic Families}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/algorithm_landscape:statistic-families}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Global Statistics}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Examples:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Number of nodes, edges, layers

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Density, clustering coefficient

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Average path length

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Degree distribution

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{When to use:} Basic network characterization

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Basic stats}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{basic\PYGZus{}stats}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Clustering}
\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{networkx}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{as}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{nx}
\PYG{n}{clustering} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{nx}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{average\PYGZus{}clustering}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{core\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{)}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{from\PYGZus{}layers}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{L}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{social}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{+} \PYG{n}{L}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{work}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}

     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{order\PYGZus{}by}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZhy{}betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{limit}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Find high\PYGZhy{}degree nodes}
\PYG{n}{hubs} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}

     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{order\PYGZus{}by}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZhy{}degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}

\label{\detokenize{user_guide/networks:method-1-add-edges-directly}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The simplest way to create a network is to add edges directly. Nodes are created automatically.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{core}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{multinet}

\PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Add edges in list format}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Format: [source\PYGZus{}node, source\PYGZus{}layer, target\PYGZus{}node, target\PYGZus{}layer, weight]}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}edges}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}
    \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Alice}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Carol}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Alice}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{colleagues}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{colleagues}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{colleagues}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Dave}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{colleagues}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{]}
\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{list}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Verify}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For more control, add nodes explicitly before adding edges:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

    \PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Alice}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Carol}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Alice}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{colleagues}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{colleagues}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Dave}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{colleagues}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}

\subsubsection{NetworkX Integration}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/networks:networkx-integration}}

\paragraph{Direct Access}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/networks:direct-access}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{core\_network}} attribute gives you direct access to the NetworkX graph:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{networkx}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{as}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{nx}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Use any NetworkX function}
\PYG{n}{degree} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n+nb}{dict}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{G}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{degree}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{betweenness} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{nx}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{G}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{clustering} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{nx}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{clustering}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{G}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Average clustering: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{nx}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{average\PYGZus{}clustering}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{G}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{.3f}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{NetworkX Wrappers}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/networks:networkx-wrappers}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
py3plex provides convenience wrappers for common NetworkX functions:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Extract a layer first}
\PYG{n}{friends\PYGZus{}layer} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{subnetwork}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{subset\PYGZus{}by}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{layers}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Apply NetworkX algorithms via wrapper}
\PYG{n}{degree\PYGZus{}centrality} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{friends\PYGZus{}layer}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{monoplex\PYGZus{}nx\PYGZus{}wrapper}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{betweenness} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{friends\PYGZus{}layer}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{monoplex\PYGZus{}nx\PYGZus{}wrapper}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{pagerank} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{friends\PYGZus{}layer}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{monoplex\PYGZus{}nx\PYGZus{}wrapper}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{pagerank}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Results are dictionaries}
\PYG{n}{top\PYGZus{}degree} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n+nb}{sorted}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{degree\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{items}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{key}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k}{lambda} \PYG{n}{x}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{x}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{reverse}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{True}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{]}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Top 5 by degree:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{top\PYGZus{}degree}\PYG{p}{)}

\paragraph{Converting to NetworkX}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/networks:converting-to-networkx}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Since py3plex networks ARE NetworkX graphs, conversion is trivial:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Save as GML}
\PYG{n}{nx}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{write\PYGZus{}gml}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{G}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{output.gml}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Save as pickle}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Verify it matches expectations}
\PYG{k}{assert} \PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}layers}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{o}{==} \PYG{l+m+mi}{3}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Expected 3 layers}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{k}{assert} \PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n+nb}{list}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Network is empty!}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Use Appropriate Data Structures}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/networks:use-appropriate-data-structures}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} For large networks, use sparse matrices}
\PYG{n}{supra\PYGZus{}adj} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}supra\PYGZus{}adjacency\PYGZus{}matrix}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{sparse}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{True}\PYG{p}{)}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Good}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Avoid dense matrices for large networks}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} supra\PYGZus{}adj = network.get\PYGZus{}supra\PYGZus{}adjacency\PYGZus{}matrix(sparse=False)  \PYGZsh{} Bad for n \PYGZgt{} 1000}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{Common Patterns}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/networks:common-patterns}}

\paragraph{Pattern 1: Load, Analyze, Visualize}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/networks:pattern-1-load-analyze-visualize}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{core}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{multinet}
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{visualization}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{multilayer}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{draw\PYGZus{}multilayer\PYGZus{}default}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Load}
\PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{load\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{data.multiedgelist}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{multiedgelist}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Analyze}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{basic\PYGZus{}stats}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Visualize}
\PYG{n}{draw\PYGZus{}multilayer\PYGZus{}default}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{display}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{True}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Pattern 2: Create from Multiple Sources}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/networks:pattern-2-create-from-multiple-sources}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Combine data from multiple files}
\PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Load friends from file}
\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pandas}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{as}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pd}
\PYG{n}{friends\PYGZus{}df} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{pd}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{read\PYGZus{}csv}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{friends.csv}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{\PYGZus{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{row} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{friends\PYGZus{}df}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{iterrows}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}edges}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{row}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{source}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{row}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{target}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
                     \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{list}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Load colleagues from database (pseudocode)}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} colleagues = query\PYGZus{}database(\PYGZdq{}SELECT * FROM colleagues\PYGZdq{})}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} for source, target in colleagues:}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{}     network.add\PYGZus{}edges([[source, \PYGZsq{}colleagues\PYGZsq{}, target, \PYGZsq{}colleagues\PYGZsq{}, 1]],}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{}                      input\PYGZus{}type=\PYGZdq{}list\PYGZdq{})}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Pattern 3: Layer\sphinxhyphen{}by\sphinxhyphen{}Layer Analysis}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/networks:pattern-3-layer-by-layer-analysis}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Analyze each layer separately}
\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{layer\PYGZus{}name} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}layers}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}n}\PYG{l+s+s2}{=== Layer: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{layer\PYGZus{}name}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ ===}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Extract layer}
    \PYG{n}{layer\PYGZus{}subnet} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{subnetwork}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{layer\PYGZus{}name}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{subset\PYGZus{}by}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{layers}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Compute metrics}
    \PYG{n}{layer\PYGZus{}subnet}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{basic\PYGZus{}stats}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Optional: visualize}
    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} draw\PYGZus{}multilayer\PYGZus{}default([layer\PYGZus{}subnet], display=True)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\subsection{Network Statistics}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/statistics:network-statistics}}\label{\detokenize{user_guide/statistics::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{How to measure and compare the structure of your multilayer network.}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{DSL for Quick Statistics}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute statistics efficiently with the DSL:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{dsl}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{L}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Compute degree and clustering for all nodes}
\PYG{n}{stats} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{compute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{clustering}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Compare layers}
\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{layer} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{layer1}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{layer2}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{layer3}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
        \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
         \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{from\PYGZus{}layers}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{L}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{layer}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
         \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{compute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
         \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{n}{df} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}pandas}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{layer}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{: avg degree = }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{mean}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{.2f}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
DSL makes comparative analysis straightforward!
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Once you’ve loaded a multilayer network, the next question is: \sphinxstyleemphasis{what does it look like?} This chapter shows you how to compute statistics that answer fundamental questions about your network’s structure:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{How dense is each layer?} Sparse layers may indicate missing data or genuine sparsity.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Who participates in multiple contexts?} High\sphinxhyphen{}activity nodes may be bridges or hubs.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{How similar are your layers?} Similar layers might be redundant; dissimilar layers reveal complementary information.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{What patterns emerge across layers?} Metrics like edge overlap and inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer degree correlation reveal cross\sphinxhyphen{}layer structure.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
py3plex provides three levels of network statistics:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Global Statistics} — Whole network properties (density, clustering, etc.)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Layer\sphinxhyphen{}Specific Statistics} — Per\sphinxhyphen{}layer measures and comparisons

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Node\sphinxhyphen{}Level Statistics} — Node activity and participation across layers

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For centrality measures (degree, betweenness, PageRank, etc.), see {\hyperref[\detokenize{concepts/algorithm_landscape::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Algorithm Landscape}}}}.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsubsection{Basic Network Statistics}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/statistics:basic-network-statistics}}

\paragraph{Quick Stats}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/statistics:quick-stats}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The fastest way to get basic information:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{core}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{multinet}

\PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{load\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{data.multiedgelist}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{multiedgelist}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Display comprehensive stats}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{basic\PYGZus{}stats}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Output:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
Number of nodes: 184
Number of edges: 1691
Number of unique nodes (as node\PYGZhy{}layer tuples): 184
Number of unique node IDs (across all layers): 46
Nodes per layer:
  Layer \PYGZsq{}1\PYGZsq{}: 46 nodes
  Layer \PYGZsq{}2\PYGZsq{}: 46 nodes
  Layer \PYGZsq{}3\PYGZsq{}: 46 nodes
  Layer \PYGZsq{}4\PYGZsq{}: 46 nodes
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Manual Counting}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/statistics:manual-counting}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Count elements}
\PYG{n}{num\PYGZus{}nodes} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n+nb}{list}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{num\PYGZus{}edges} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n+nb}{list}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}edges}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{num\PYGZus{}layers} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}layers}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Unique node IDs (across all layers)}
\PYG{n}{unique\PYGZus{}nodes} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n+nb}{set}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{layer} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n}{unique\PYGZus{}nodes}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{num\PYGZus{}unique\PYGZus{}nodes} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{unique\PYGZus{}nodes}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Nodes (node\PYGZhy{}layer pairs): }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{num\PYGZus{}nodes}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Edges: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{num\PYGZus{}edges}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Layers: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{num\PYGZus{}layers}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Unique node IDs: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{num\PYGZus{}unique\PYGZus{}nodes}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{Layer\sphinxhyphen{}Specific Statistics}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/statistics:layer-specific-statistics}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{multilayer\_statistics}} module provides comprehensive statistics:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{algorithms}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{statistics}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{multilayer\PYGZus{}statistics} \PYG{k}{as} \PYG{n}{mls}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Layer Density}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/statistics:layer-density}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Definition:} Fraction of possible edges that exist in a layer.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Formula:} \(density = \frac{2m}{n(n-1)}\) for undirected graphs

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Use case:} Measure how connected a layer is.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Density of individual layers}

\subsection{Community Detection}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/community_detection:community-detection}}\label{\detokenize{user_guide/community_detection::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Finding groups that span multiple layers of interaction.}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{DSL Tip: Filter by Communities}

\sphinxAtStartPar
After detecting communities, use DSL to analyze them:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{dsl}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{L}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Find high\PYGZhy{}degree nodes in specific community}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} (assuming you stored community IDs as node attributes)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Get all nodes and their properties}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{compute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{order\PYGZus{}by}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZhy{}degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{limit}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{20}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Export for further analysis}
\PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}pandas}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}csv}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{community\PYGZus{}hubs.csv}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Combine traditional algorithms with DSL queries for powerful workflows!
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip


\sphinxAtStartPar
Networks are rarely homogeneous. People cluster into social groups. Proteins form functional modules. Cities organize into regional hubs. \sphinxstylestrong{Community detection} finds these natural groupings—but in multilayer networks, the question is more subtle: \sphinxstyleemphasis{do communities exist within layers, across layers, or both?}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This chapter shows you how to detect communities in multilayer networks, how to tune algorithm parameters for your specific domain, and how to interpret results that may differ from single\sphinxhyphen{}layer community detection.


\subsubsection{Overview}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/community_detection:overview}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Community detection identifies \sphinxstylestrong{groups of nodes} that are more \sphinxstylestrong{densely connected} to each other than to the rest of the network. For \sphinxstylestrong{multilayer networks}, communities can \sphinxstylestrong{span multiple layers}, accounting for both \sphinxstylestrong{intra\sphinxhyphen{}layer} and \sphinxstylestrong{inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer} structure.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Key insight:} A person who is moderately connected across multiple social platforms (layers) may be more central to a cross\sphinxhyphen{}platform community than someone who is highly connected on just one platform. Multilayer community detection captures this.


\subsubsection{Supported Algorithms}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/community_detection:supported-algorithms}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
py3plex provides \sphinxstylestrong{several community detection algorithms}:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Louvain} — \sphinxstylestrong{Fast modularity optimization} (recommended for most use cases)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Infomap} — \sphinxstylestrong{Flow\sphinxhyphen{}based} community detection (requires external binary)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Label Propagation} — \sphinxstylestrong{Semi\sphinxhyphen{}supervised} approach with known seed communities

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Multilayer Modularity} — \sphinxstylestrong{True multilayer} community detection (Mucha et al. 2010)

\end{itemize}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsubsection{Louvain Algorithm}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/community_detection:louvain-algorithm}}

\paragraph{Basic Usage}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/community_detection:basic-usage}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Fastest algorithm} for large networks:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{core}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{multinet}
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{algorithms}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{community\PYGZus{}detection}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{community\PYGZus{}louvain}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Create or load network}
\PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{load\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{data.graphml}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{graphml}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Detect communities using Louvain}
\PYG{n}{communities} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{community\PYGZus{}louvain}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{best\PYGZus{}partition}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{core\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Print results}
\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{community\PYGZus{}id} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{communities}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{items}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}

\subsubsection{Multilayer Modularity}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/community_detection:multilayer-modularity}}

\paragraph{True Multilayer Detection}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/community_detection:true-multilayer-detection}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Accounts for multilayer structure following Mucha et al. (2010):

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{algorithms}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{community\PYGZus{}detection}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{multilayer\PYGZus{}modularity} \PYG{k}{as} \PYG{n}{mlm}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Get supra\PYGZhy{}adjacency matrix}
\PYG{n}{supra\PYGZus{}adj} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}supra\PYGZus{}adjacency\PYGZus{}matrix}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{sparse}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{True}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Detect communities with multilayer modularity}
\PYG{n}{communities} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{mlm}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multilayer\PYGZus{}louvain}\PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{supra\PYGZus{}adj}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{n}{gamma}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{,}      \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Resolution parameter}
    \PYG{n}{omega}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}       \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Inter\PYGZhy{}layer coupling strength}
\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Parameter Tuning}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/community_detection:parameter-tuning}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Emphasize layer\PYGZhy{}specific structure}
\PYG{n}{communities} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{mlm}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multilayer\PYGZus{}louvain}\PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{supra\PYGZus{}adj}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{n}{gamma}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{n}{omega}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.1}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Low coupling = layer\PYGZhy{}specific communities}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Emphasize cross\PYGZhy{}layer structure}
\PYG{n}{communities} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{mlm}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multilayer\PYGZus{}louvain}\PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{supra\PYGZus{}adj}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{n}{gamma}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{n}{omega}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{10.0}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} High coupling = cross\PYGZhy{}layer communities}
\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Mathematical Formulation}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/community_detection:mathematical-formulation}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Multilayer modularity is defined as:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}Q^{ML} = \frac{1}{2\mu} \sum_{ij\alpha\beta} \left[ (A_{ij}^{[\alpha]} - \gamma_{\alpha} P_{ij}^{[\alpha]})\delta_{\alpha\beta} + \omega_{\alpha\beta}\delta_{ij} \right] \delta(g_{i}^{[\alpha]}, g_{j}^{[\beta]})\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Where:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(A_{ij}^{[\alpha]}\) is the adjacency matrix of layer \(\alpha\)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(P_{ij}^{[\alpha]}\) is the null model (e.g., configuration model)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\gamma_{\alpha}\) is the resolution parameter for layer \(\alpha\)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\omega_{\alpha\beta}\) is the coupling strength between layers

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\delta(g_{i}^{[\alpha]}, g_{j}^{[\beta]})\) is 1 if nodes are in the same community, 0 otherwise

\end{itemize}


\paragraph{Advantages}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/community_detection:id6}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Accounts for multilayer structure

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Implements state\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}the\sphinxhyphen{}art algorithm

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Configurable inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer coupling

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Published in Science (Mucha et al. 2010)

\end{itemize}


\paragraph{Disadvantages}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/community_detection:id7}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
More computationally expensive

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Requires parameter tuning

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
May not scale to very large networks (\textgreater{}100k nodes)

\end{itemize}

\subsubsection{Understanding Single\sphinxhyphen{}Layer vs. Multilayer Community Detection}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/community_detection:understanding-single-layer-vs-multilayer-community-detection}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Before diving into algorithm specifics, it’s important to understand the conceptual differences between approaches.


\paragraph{Single\sphinxhyphen{}Layer Community Detection}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/community_detection:single-layer-community-detection}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Traditional community detection finds groups in a single graph. Applied to a multilayer network, you have two options:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Flatten and detect:} Aggregate all layers into one graph, then find communities. This loses layer information.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Detect per layer:} Find communities independently in each layer. This ignores cross\sphinxhyphen{}layer structure.

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Neither captures the full multilayer picture.


\paragraph{Multilayer Community Detection}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/community_detection:multilayer-community-detection}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Multilayer algorithms find communities that are consistent across layers while respecting layer\sphinxhyphen{}specific structure. They ask: “Which nodes cluster together across multiple contexts?”

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Key insight:} A node that is moderately connected in many layers may be more “community\sphinxhyphen{}central” than a node highly connected in just one layer.


\paragraph{Overlapping vs. Non\sphinxhyphen{}Overlapping Communities}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/community_detection:overlapping-vs-non-overlapping-communities}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Non\sphinxhyphen{}overlapping:} Each node belongs to exactly one community. Algorithms like Louvain and Leiden produce non\sphinxhyphen{}overlapping partitions.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Overlapping:} Nodes can belong to multiple communities. Algorithms like NoRC and clique percolation find overlapping structure.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{When to use overlapping:} When nodes naturally belong to multiple groups (e.g., a person in both a work community and a hobby community).


\paragraph{Flow\sphinxhyphen{}Based vs. Modularity\sphinxhyphen{}Based Views}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/community_detection:flow-based-vs-modularity-based-views}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Modularity\sphinxhyphen{}based (Louvain, Leiden):} Optimize a quality function that compares edge density within communities to expected density. Fast, widely used, but has resolution limit issues.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Flow\sphinxhyphen{}based (Infomap):} Model random walks on the network and find community structure that minimizes description length of those walks. Theoretically grounded, finds hierarchical structure, but slower.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{When to use which:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use \sphinxstylestrong{modularity\sphinxhyphen{}based} for speed and when you don’t need hierarchical structure

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use \sphinxstylestrong{flow\sphinxhyphen{}based} when you care about information flow or want to find nested communities

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Parameter Tuning Cookbook}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/community_detection:parameter-tuning-cookbook}}

\paragraph{Tuning Resolution (Gamma)}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/community_detection:tuning-resolution-gamma}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The resolution parameter γ controls community size:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{algorithms}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{community\PYGZus{}detection}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{multilayer\PYGZus{}modularity}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{louvain\PYGZus{}multilayer}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Experiment with different resolution values}
\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{gamma} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.5}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{1.5}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{2.0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n}{partition} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{louvain\PYGZus{}multilayer}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{gamma}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{gamma}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{omega}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{random\PYGZus{}state}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{42}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{n}{num\PYGZus{}comms} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n+nb}{set}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{partition}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{gamma=}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{gamma}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{num\PYGZus{}comms}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ communities}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Interpretation guide:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Very few communities (2\sphinxhyphen{}5) when you expect more:} γ is too low \(\rightarrow\) increase γ

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Many singleton communities:} γ is too high \(\rightarrow\) decrease γ

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{One giant community + many tiny ones:} Resolution limit problem \(\rightarrow\) try γ \textgreater{} 1 or use Leiden

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Recommended starting procedure:}
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Start with γ=1.0 (standard modularity)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Look at community size distribution

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
If too coarse, try γ=1.5, 2.0

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
If too fine, try γ=0.5, 0.25

\end{enumerate}


\paragraph{Tuning Inter\sphinxhyphen{}Layer Coupling (Omega)}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/community_detection:tuning-inter-layer-coupling-omega}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The coupling parameter ω controls how much layers influence each other:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Experiment with different coupling values}
\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{omega} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.5}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{2.0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{5.0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n}{partition} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{louvain\PYGZus{}multilayer}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{gamma}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{omega}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{omega}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{random\PYGZus{}state}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{42}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{n}{num\PYGZus{}comms} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n+nb}{set}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{partition}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}

    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Check cross\PYGZhy{}layer consistency}
    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} (how often does the same node get same community across layers?)}
    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} ... (compute consistency metric)}
    \PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{omega=}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{omega}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{num\PYGZus{}comms}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ communities}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Interpretation guide:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{ω = 0:} Layers are independent (equivalent to detecting per\sphinxhyphen{}layer, then combining)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{ω = 1:} Balanced coupling (default, usually good)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{ω \textgreater{} 1:} Strong coupling (forces cross\sphinxhyphen{}layer consistency)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{ω \(\rightarrow\) \(\infty\):} All layers must have identical community structure

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Domain\sphinxhyphen{}specific guidance:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Multiplex social networks:} Start with ω=1.0 (people are the same across platforms)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Temporal networks:} ω=0.5 to 1.0 (communities can evolve but not too fast)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Heterogeneous networks:} ω=0.1 to 0.5 (different node types may have different community structure)

\end{itemize}


\paragraph{Diagnosing Bad Partitions}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/community_detection:diagnosing-bad-partitions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Problem: All nodes in one community}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{if} \PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n+nb}{set}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{partition}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{o}{==} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{All nodes in single community \PYGZhy{} try increasing gamma}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Causes:} Network is too dense, γ too low, or network genuinely has no community structure.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Problem: Each node is its own community}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{if} \PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n+nb}{set}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{partition}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{o}{==} \PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{partition}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{All singletons \PYGZhy{} try decreasing gamma or increasing omega}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Causes:} Network is too sparse, γ too high, ω too low.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Problem: Communities don’t match domain expectations}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Actions:}
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Visualize communities and examine specific nodes

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Check if high\sphinxhyphen{}degree nodes are correctly assigned

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Verify that known groups (e.g., departments) are recovered

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Consider using ground\sphinxhyphen{}truth labels for NMI comparison

\end{enumerate}

\paragraph{Case Study 1: Biological Network Communities}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/community_detection:case-study-1-biological-network-communities}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Scenario:} A protein\sphinxhyphen{}protein interaction network with 3 layers representing different experimental evidence types (yeast two\sphinxhyphen{}hybrid, co\sphinxhyphen{}immunoprecipitation, affinity purification).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Goal:} Find functional modules (groups of proteins with shared biological function).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Approach:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{core}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{multinet}
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{algorithms}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{community\PYGZus{}detection}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{multilayer\PYGZus{}modularity}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{louvain\PYGZus{}multilayer}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Load network}
\PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{load\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ppi\PYGZus{}multilayer.txt}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{multiedgelist}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{directed}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{False}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Use moderate coupling \PYGZhy{} different evidence types should}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} contribute to same modules, but we don\PYGZsq{}t require perfect consistency}
\PYG{n}{partition} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{louvain\PYGZus{}multilayer}\PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{n}{gamma}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{,}     \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Standard resolution}
    \PYG{n}{omega}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.5}\PYG{p}{,}     \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Moderate coupling}
    \PYG{n}{random\PYGZus{}state}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{42}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Validate: Do communities correspond to GO biological process terms?}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Compare community assignments to known functional annotations}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Expected outcome:} Communities should correspond to functional modules like “cell cycle,” “DNA repair,” “metabolic pathways.” Proteins appearing in multiple layers with high connectivity should be community hubs.


\paragraph{Case Study 2: Transportation Network Communities}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/community_detection:case-study-2-transportation-network-communities}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Scenario:} A multi\sphinxhyphen{}modal transportation network with layers for metro, bus, and bike\sphinxhyphen{}share in a city.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Goal:} Find “travel basins”—regions where people travel together within a mode and switch between modes at hubs.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Approach:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Load network}
\PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{load\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{transport\PYGZus{}network.txt}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{multiedgelist}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{directed}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{False}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Higher coupling \PYGZhy{} the same station serves multiple modes}

    \PYG{n}{gamma}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{1.2}\PYG{p}{,}     \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Slightly higher to find smaller regions}
    \PYG{n}{omega}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{1.5}\PYG{p}{,}     \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Strong coupling at multimodal hubs}
    \PYG{n}{random\PYGZus{}state}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{42}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Validate: Do communities correspond to geographic regions?}

\paragraph{Normalized Mutual Information}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/community_detection:normalized-mutual-information}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compare similarity between community structures:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{sklearn}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{metrics}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{normalized\PYGZus{}mutual\PYGZus{}info\PYGZus{}score}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Convert to lists}
\PYG{n}{louvain\PYGZus{}list} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{louvain\PYGZus{}comms}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{node} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{core\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{]}
\PYG{n}{label\PYGZus{}list} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{label\PYGZus{}prop\PYGZus{}comms}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{node} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{core\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{]}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Compute NMI}
\PYG{n}{nmi} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{normalized\PYGZus{}mutual\PYGZus{}info\PYGZus{}score}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{louvain\PYGZus{}list}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{label\PYGZus{}list}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{NMI between Louvain and Label Prop: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{nmi}\PYG{l+s+si}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{.3f}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Interpretation:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
NMI = 1.0: Identical community structures

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
NMI = 0.0: Completely different structures

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
NMI \textgreater{} 0.5: Similar structures

\end{itemize}

\paragraph{Parameter Guidelines}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/community_detection:parameter-guidelines}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Louvain resolution:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Start with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{resolution=1.0}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Increase if communities are too large

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Decrease if communities are too fragmented

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Multilayer coupling (omega):}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{omega=1.0}} \sphinxhyphen{} Default, balanced

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{omega\textless{}1.0}} \sphinxhyphen{} Emphasize layer\sphinxhyphen{}specific structure

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{omega\textgreater{}1.0}} \sphinxhyphen{} Emphasize cross\sphinxhyphen{}layer structure

\end{itemize}


\paragraph{Validation}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/community_detection:validation}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Always validate community detection results:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Visual inspection} — Plot and examine communities

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Modularity} — Check modularity score (\textgreater{}0.3 is good)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Size distribution} — Check for giant communities or singletons

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Domain knowledge} — Do communities make sense for your application?

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Ground truth comparison} — If you have labels, compute NMI or Adjusted Rand Index

\end{enumerate}


\paragraph{Common Failure Modes}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/community_detection:common-failure-modes}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Trivial partitions:} All\sphinxhyphen{}in\sphinxhyphen{}one or all\sphinxhyphen{}singletons \(\rightarrow\) tune γ and ω

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Unstable results:} Different runs give very different partitions \(\rightarrow\) use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{random\_state}} and run multiple times

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Over\sphinxhyphen{}fragmentation:} Too many small communities \(\rightarrow\) decrease γ or try Leiden

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Resolution limit:} Can’t find small communities in large networks \(\rightarrow\) increase γ or use hierarchical methods

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{What You Learned}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/community_detection:what-you-learned}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This chapter covered community detection in multilayer networks:

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Algorithms:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Louvain} — Fast, O(n log n), BSD license, good for most use cases

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Infomap} — Flow\sphinxhyphen{}based, finds hierarchical structure, AGPLv3 license

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Label Propagation} — Very fast, linear in edges, supports semi\sphinxhyphen{}supervised detection

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Multilayer Modularity} — True multilayer detection with inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer coupling

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Parameter tuning:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Resolution γ} — Higher = more, smaller communities; lower = fewer, larger

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Coupling ω} — Higher = cross\sphinxhyphen{}layer consistency; lower = layer\sphinxhyphen{}specific structure

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Start with γ=1.0, ω=1.0 and adjust based on results

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Interpretation:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Trivial partitions (all\sphinxhyphen{}in\sphinxhyphen{}one or all\sphinxhyphen{}singletons) indicate parameter tuning needed

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
High modularity (\textgreater{}0.3) suggests good community structure

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Validate with visualization, domain knowledge, and ground truth if available

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Conceptual differences:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Single\sphinxhyphen{}layer detection treats node\sphinxhyphen{}layer pairs independently

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Multilayer detection finds communities consistent across layers

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Overlapping vs. non\sphinxhyphen{}overlapping communities serve different use cases

\end{itemize}
