\paragraph{EXPLAIN Mode}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/dsl:explain-mode}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Get a query execution plan without actually running the query:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{dsl}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{Q}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Build a query}
\PYG{n}{q} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{where}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{layer}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{social}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{compute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Get execution plan}
\PYG{n}{plan} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{explain}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Inspect the plan}
\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{step} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{plan}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{steps}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{step}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{description}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ (}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{step}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{estimated\PYGZus{}complexity}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{)}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Check for warnings}
\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{warning} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{plan}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{warnings}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Warning: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{warning}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The execution plan includes:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Step\sphinxhyphen{}by\sphinxhyphen{}step breakdown of query execution

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Estimated time complexity for each step

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Warnings for expensive operations (e.g., betweenness centrality on large graphs)

\end{itemize}


\paragraph{Parameterized Queries}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/dsl:parameterized-queries}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Param}} to create queries with placeholders that are bound at execution time:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{dsl}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{Param}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Create a reusable query template}
\PYG{n}{q} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{where}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{layer}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{social}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{degree\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}gt}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{Param}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{int}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{min\PYGZus{}degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Execute with different parameters}
\PYG{n}{result1} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{min\PYGZus{}degree}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{result2} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{min\PYGZus{}degree}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Parameter types:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Param.int("name")}} \sphinxhyphen{} Integer parameter

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Param.float("name")}} \sphinxhyphen{} Float parameter

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Param.str("name")}} \sphinxhyphen{} String parameter

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Param.ref("name")}} \sphinxhyphen{} Untyped parameter

\end{itemize}


\paragraph{Convert Builder to DSL String}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/dsl:convert-builder-to-dsl-string}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Convert a builder query back to DSL string format:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{q} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{where}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{layer}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{social}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{degree\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}gt}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{compute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{limit}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Get DSL string}
\PYG{n}{dsl\PYGZus{}string} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}dsl}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{dsl\PYGZus{}string}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Output: SELECT nodes WHERE layer = \PYGZdq{}social\PYGZdq{} AND degree \PYGZgt{} 5 COMPUTE degree LIMIT 10}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is useful for:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Debugging queries

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Logging and auditing

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Serializing queries for later use

\end{itemize}


\paragraph{Error Handling with Suggestions}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/dsl:error-handling-with-suggestions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
DSL v2 provides helpful error messages with “Did you mean?” suggestions:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{dsl}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{UnknownMeasureError}

\PYG{k}{try}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Typo in measure name}
    \PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{compute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{betweenes}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{k}{except} \PYG{n}{UnknownMeasureError} \PYG{k}{as} \PYG{n}{e}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{e}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Output: Unknown measure \PYGZsq{}betweenes\PYGZsq{}. Did you mean \PYGZsq{}betweenness\PYGZsq{}?}
    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{}         Known measures: betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality, closeness\PYGZus{}centrality, ...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Measure Registry}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/dsl:measure-registry}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
DSL v2 includes a centralized registry for network measures. View available measures:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{dsl}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{measure\PYGZus{}registry}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} List all measures}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{measure\PYGZus{}registry}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{list\PYGZus{}measures}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Check if a measure exists}
\PYG{k}{if} \PYG{n}{measure\PYGZus{}registry}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{has}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree is available}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Get measure description}
\PYG{n}{desc} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{measure\PYGZus{}registry}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}description}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{desc}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{Example Queries}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/dsl:example-queries}}

\paragraph{Basic Queries}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/dsl:basic-queries}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Select all nodes in a layer:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{execute\PYGZus{}query}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{SELECT nodes WHERE layer=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{social}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Select high\sphinxhyphen{}degree nodes:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{execute\PYGZus{}query}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{SELECT nodes WHERE degree \PYGZgt{} 5}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Select all nodes (no filter):

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{execute\PYGZus{}query}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{SELECT nodes}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Complex Queries}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/dsl:complex-queries}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Combine multiple conditions:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Nodes in transport layer with high degree}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{execute\PYGZus{}query}\PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{SELECT nodes WHERE layer=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{transport}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{ AND degree \PYGZgt{} 5}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}
\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use OR operator:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Nodes in either social or work layer}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{execute\PYGZus{}query}\PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{SELECT nodes WHERE layer=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{social}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{ OR layer=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{work}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}
\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Degree range filtering:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Nodes with moderate degree}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{execute\PYGZus{}query}\PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{SELECT nodes WHERE degree \PYGZgt{}= 2 AND degree \PYGZlt{}= 5}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}
\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Analytical Queries}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/dsl:analytical-queries}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute centrality for a layer:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{execute\PYGZus{}query}\PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{SELECT nodes WHERE layer=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{transport}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{ COMPUTE betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Access computed values}
\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{centrality} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{result}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{computed}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{items}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{centrality}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Multiple measures for filtered nodes:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{SELECT nodes WHERE degree \PYGZgt{} 3 COMPUTE degree\PYGZus{}centrality closeness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}
\PYG{p}{)}

\subsubsection{Working with Results}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/dsl:working-with-results}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{execute\_query}} function returns a dictionary containing:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{query}}: Original query string

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{target}}: Query target (nodes or edges)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{nodes}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{edges}}: List of selected items

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{count}}: Number of items returned

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{computed}}: Dictionary of computed measures (if COMPUTE used)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{execute\PYGZus{}query}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{SELECT nodes WHERE layer=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{social}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Access results}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Found }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{result}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{count}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ nodes}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{node} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{result}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{nodes}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} If COMPUTE was used}
\PYG{k}{if} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{computed}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{result}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{measure}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{values} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{result}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{computed}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{items}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
        \PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{measure}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
        \PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{value} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{values}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{items}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
            \PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{  }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{value}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\paragraph{DSL v2 Error Types}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/dsl:dsl-v2-error-types}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For builder API queries, more specific error types are available:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{dsl}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{p}{(}

\PYG{p}{)}

\paragraph{Common DSL Errors}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/dsl:common-dsl-errors}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Here’s an example of a common error and how to fix it:

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Malformed Query (missing quotes around layer name):}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Wrong \PYGZhy{} missing quotes around layer name}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{execute\PYGZus{}query}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{SELECT nodes WHERE layer=social}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Error:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

Hint: Use layer=\PYGZdq{}social\PYGZdq{} instead of layer=social
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Fix:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Correct \PYGZhy{} layer name is quoted}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{execute\PYGZus{}query}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{SELECT nodes WHERE layer=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{social}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} UnknownMeasureError: Unknown measure \PYGZsq{}betweenes\PYGZsq{}. Did you mean \PYGZsq{}betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality\PYGZsq{}?}

\paragraph{Example 2: Multilayer Network Analysis}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{core}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{multinet}

\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{person} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Alice}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Charlie}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{:}

        \PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{append}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{source}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{person}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{type}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{layer}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Add edges in different layers}

    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Social connections}

    \PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{source}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{target}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Charlie}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{source\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{social}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{target\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{social}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}

\subsubsection{DSL\sphinxhyphen{}Based Dynamics Simulation}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/dsl:dsl-based-dynamics-simulation}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The py3plex DSL extends beyond network queries to support declarative dynamics
simulation on multilayer networks. This section demonstrates how to use the
dynamics DSL for epidemic modeling and other dynamical processes.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For detailed documentation and formalism, see \DUrole{xref}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{../../../book/part3\_dsl/chapter10\_advanced\_queries\_workflows}}}.


\paragraph{Quick Start}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/dsl:quick-start}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The dynamics DSL uses a builder API similar to the query DSL:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{dynamics}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{D}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{SIS}
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{core}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{multinet}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Create network}
\PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} ... add nodes and edges ...}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Define SIS simulation}
\PYG{n}{sim} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{D}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{process}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{SIS}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{beta}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.3}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{mu}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.1}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Transmission and recovery rates}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{initial}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{infected}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.05}\PYG{p}{)}           \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} 5\PYGZpc{} initially infected}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{steps}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{100}\PYG{p}{)}                       \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Run for 100 time steps}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{measure}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{prevalence}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{incidence}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Track measures}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{replicates}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{)}                   \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Run 10 independent simulations}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{seed}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{42}\PYG{p}{)}                         \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} For reproducibility}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Execute simulation}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{sim}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{run}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Access results}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Mean final prevalence: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{data}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{prevalence}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{mean}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{.3f}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Convert to pandas for analysis}
\PYG{n}{df\PYGZus{}dict} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}pandas}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{prevalence\PYGZus{}df} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{df\PYGZus{}dict}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{prevalence}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Available Processes}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/dsl:available-processes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The dynamics module supports several built\sphinxhyphen{}in processes:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{SIS} \sphinxhyphen{} Susceptible\sphinxhyphen{}Infected\sphinxhyphen{}Susceptible (endemic diseases)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{SIR} \sphinxhyphen{} Susceptible\sphinxhyphen{}Infected\sphinxhyphen{}Recovered (epidemic diseases with immunity)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{RandomWalk} \sphinxhyphen{} Random walk dynamics on networks

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Each process has configurable parameters:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{dynamics}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{SIS}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{SIR}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{RandomWalk}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} SIS with transmission rate β=0.3, recovery rate μ=0.1}
\PYG{n}{SIS}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{beta}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.3}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{mu}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.1}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} SIR with transmission rate β=0.4, recovery rate γ=0.15}
\PYG{n}{SIR}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{beta}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.4}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{gamma}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.15}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Random walk with teleportation probability}
\PYG{n}{RandomWalk}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{teleport}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.05}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Multilayer Dynamics}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/dsl:multilayer-dynamics}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The dynamics DSL seamlessly integrates with layer selection:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{dsl}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{L}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Simulate on specific layers}
\PYG{n}{sim} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{D}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{process}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{SIS}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{beta}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.25}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{mu}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.08}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{on\PYGZus{}layers}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{L}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{offline}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{+} \PYG{n}{L}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{online}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Select layers using layer algebra}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{coupling}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{node\PYGZus{}replicas}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{strong}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}       \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Nodes share states across layers}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{initial}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{infected}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.1}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{steps}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{120}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{measure}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{prevalence}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{prevalence\PYGZus{}by\PYGZus{}layer}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{replicates}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{15}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{sim}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{run}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{multilayer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Integration with Query DSL}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/dsl:integration-with-query-dsl}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use query DSL to specify targeted initial conditions:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{dsl}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{Q}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Start infection at high\PYGZhy{}degree nodes (hubs)}
\PYG{n}{sim} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{D}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{process}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{SIS}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{beta}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.35}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{mu}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.12}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{initial}\PYG{p}{(}
         \PYG{n}{infected}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{where}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{degree\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}gte}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{)}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Query selects hubs}
     \PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{steps}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{100}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{measure}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{prevalence}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{replicates}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{sim}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{run}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This powerful combination allows precise control over initial conditions based
on network structure, centrality, or any other computable property.


\paragraph{Result Analysis}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/dsl:result-analysis}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{SimulationResult}} object provides rich analysis capabilities:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Get summary statistics}
\PYG{n}{summary} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{summary}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{summary}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Plot time series with confidence intervals}
\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{matplotlib}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{pyplot}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{as}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{plt}
\PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{plot}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{prevalence}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{plt}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{show}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Export to pandas for custom analysis}
\PYG{n}{df\PYGZus{}dict} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}pandas}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{prevalence\PYGZus{}df} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{df\PYGZus{}dict}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{prevalence}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Compute mean trajectory across replicates}
\PYG{n}{mean\PYGZus{}trajectory} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{prevalence\PYGZus{}df}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{groupby}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{t}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{value}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{agg}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{mean}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{std}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\subsubsection{Limitations and Future Work}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/dsl:limitations-and-future-work}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Current limitations:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Edge queries are not yet fully supported

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Complex nested conditions require multiple queries

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Limited to NetworkX\sphinxhyphen{}based measures

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
No aggregation functions (SUM, AVG, etc.)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Planned enhancements:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Full edge query support

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Nested subqueries

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Aggregation operators

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Custom measure registration

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Query optimization

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Save/load query results

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Best Practices}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/dsl:best-practices}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{1. Choose the Right API}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Builder API (Q.nodes())}: Recommended for production code, complex queries, and when type hints are important

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{String DSL}: Good for simple queries, interactive exploration, and when learning the syntax

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{2. Start simple, build incrementally}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Begin with basic queries and add complexity step by step:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Start simple}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Add filtering}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{where}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{layer}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{social}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Add computation}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{where}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{layer}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{social}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{compute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Add ordering and limiting}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{where}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{layer}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{social}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{compute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{order\PYGZus{}by}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZhy{}degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{limit}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{3. Use parameterized queries for reusability}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Create reusable query templates with Param:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Define once}
\PYG{n}{top\PYGZus{}nodes\PYGZus{}query} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{where}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{layer}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{Param}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{str}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{layer\PYGZus{}name}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{degree\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}gt}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{Param}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{int}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{threshold}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{compute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{order\PYGZus{}by}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZhy{}betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{limit}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{Param}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{int}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{top\PYGZus{}n}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Execute many times with different parameters}
\PYG{n}{social\PYGZus{}hubs} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{top\PYGZus{}nodes\PYGZus{}query}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{layer\PYGZus{}name}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{social}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{threshold}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{top\PYGZus{}n}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{work\PYGZus{}hubs} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{top\PYGZus{}nodes\PYGZus{}query}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{layer\PYGZus{}name}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{work}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{threshold}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{3}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{top\PYGZus{}n}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{20}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{4. Use EXPLAIN for expensive queries}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Before running expensive queries on large networks, check the execution plan:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{q} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{compute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{plan} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{explain}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{step} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{plan}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{steps}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{step}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{description}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ \PYGZhy{} }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{step}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{estimated\PYGZus{}complexity}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{k}{if} \PYG{n}{plan}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{warnings}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Warnings:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{plan}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{warnings}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{5. Validate data and check results}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Always inspect result counts and samples before processing large result sets:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{where}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{degree\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}gt}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Found }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{count}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ nodes}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{k}{if} \PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{count} \PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Sample: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{items}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{l+m+mi}{3}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Process results...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{6. Choose appropriate export format}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{to\_pandas()}: Best for data analysis, statistical operations, and visualization

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{to\_networkx()}: Best for further NetworkX operations or subgraph analysis

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{to\_arrow()}: Best for large datasets, columnar operations, or data interchange

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{to\_dict()}: Best for serialization, API responses, or custom processing

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{7. Handle errors gracefully}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use try\sphinxhyphen{}except blocks and leverage error messages:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{dsl}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{UnknownMeasureError}

\PYG{k}{try}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{compute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{my\PYGZus{}measure}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{k}{except} \PYG{n}{UnknownMeasureError} \PYG{k}{as} \PYG{n}{e}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Measure not found: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{e}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Fallback logic or use suggested measure}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{8. Performance optimization}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For large networks, follow these guidelines:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Filter by layer first to reduce search space

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{limit()}} to restrict result size when you don’t need all results

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Cache computed measures if reusing them multiple times

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Consider using \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{degree}} instead of more expensive centrality measures for initial filtering

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Less efficient \PYGZhy{} computes centrality for all nodes}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{compute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{order\PYGZus{}by}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZhy{}betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{limit}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} More efficient \PYGZhy{} filter by degree first}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{where}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{degree\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}gt}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{compute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{order\PYGZus{}by}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZhy{}betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{limit}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{Performance Considerations}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/dsl:performance-considerations}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Computing centrality measures can be expensive on large networks

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Filter by layer first to reduce search space

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Cache computed measures if reusing them

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Consider using convenience functions for better performance

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Pre\sphinxhyphen{}compute measures and store in node attributes for repeated use

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example performance optimization:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Less efficient \PYGZhy{} computes centrality multiple times}
\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{threshold} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{3}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{7}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{execute\PYGZus{}query}\PYG{p}{(}
        \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,}
        \PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{SELECT nodes WHERE degree \PYGZgt{} }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{threshold}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{ COMPUTE betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}
    \PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} More efficient \PYGZhy{} compute once, filter in post\PYGZhy{}processing}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{execute\PYGZus{}query}\PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{SELECT nodes COMPUTE betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}
\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{centralities} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{result}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{computed}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}

\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{threshold} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{3}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{7}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{:}

                  \PYG{k}{if} \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{core\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{degree}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}} \PYG{n}{threshold}\PYG{p}{]}

\subsubsection{Overview}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/graph_ops:overview}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Py3plex provides a dplyr\sphinxhyphen{}style, fluent method\sphinxhyphen{}chaining interface for working with nodes
and edges in multilayer networks. This API is inspired by R’s dplyr package and provides
verbs like \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{filter}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{select}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mutate}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{arrange}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{group\_by}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{summarise}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The API enables you to express complex data manipulations as readable chains of operations:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{graph\PYGZus{}ops}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{edges}
\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{numpy}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{as}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{np}

\PYG{n}{df} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{layers}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ppi}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{filter}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{lambda} \PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}} \PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{mutate}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{k}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k}{lambda} \PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{/} \PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{weight}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{+} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{group\PYGZus{}by}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{layer}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{summarise}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{avg\PYGZus{}degree}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{np}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{mean}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}pandas}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The graph\_ops module is particularly useful for:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Fluent data manipulation}: Chain operations naturally without intermediate variables

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Aggregation and summarization}: Group data and compute statistics

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Integration with pandas}: Export results directly to DataFrames

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Filtering and transformation}: Apply complex logic to nodes and edges

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Key Concepts}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/graph_ops:key-concepts}}

\paragraph{NodeFrame and EdgeFrame}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/graph_ops:nodeframe-and-edgeframe}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The two main “frame” types wrap collections of nodes or edges:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{NodeFrame}: A chainable view over a collection of nodes

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{EdgeFrame}: A chainable view over a collection of edges

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Both wrap:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A reference to the underlying py3plex graph object (multinet)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A current selection of nodes or edges (as a list of dicts)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
All verbs return a new NodeFrame/EdgeFrame, enabling method chaining.


\paragraph{Top\sphinxhyphen{}level Helpers}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/graph_ops:top-level-helpers}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{nodes()}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{edges()}} functions to create frames:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{graph\PYGZus{}ops}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{edges}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Get all nodes from the network}
\PYG{n}{node\PYGZus{}frame} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Get nodes from specific layers}
\PYG{n}{node\PYGZus{}frame} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{layers}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{layer1}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{layer2}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Get all edges}
\PYG{n}{edge\PYGZus{}frame} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{edges}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Get edges from specific layers}
\PYG{n}{edge\PYGZus{}frame} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{edges}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{layers}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ppi}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{Quick Start Example}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/graph_ops:quick-start-example}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Here’s a complete working example:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\paragraph{Example 1: Hub Identification}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/graph_ops:example-1-hub-identification}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Find and analyze hub nodes across layers:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{core}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{multinet}
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{graph\PYGZus{}ops}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{nodes}
\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{numpy}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{as}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{np}

\PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{directed}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{False}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} ... add nodes and edges ...}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Find high\PYGZhy{}degree nodes (hubs) in each layer}
\PYG{n}{hub\PYGZus{}summary} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{filter}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{lambda} \PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{o}{=} \PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{)}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Only high\PYGZhy{}degree nodes}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{group\PYGZus{}by}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{layer}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{summarise}\PYG{p}{(}
        \PYG{n}{hub\PYGZus{}count}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{id}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}
        \PYG{n}{avg\PYGZus{}hub\PYGZus{}degree}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{np}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{mean}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}
        \PYG{n}{max\PYGZus{}degree}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n+nb}{max}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{arrange}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{hub\PYGZus{}count}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{reverse}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{True}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}pandas}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{hub\PYGZus{}summary}\PYG{p}{)}

\subsubsection{Best Practices}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/graph_ops:best-practices}}\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Start simple}: Begin with basic filters and add complexity incrementally

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Use method chaining}: Chain operations for readable, fluent code

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Handle missing values}: Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.get()}} for optional attributes:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{frame}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{mutate}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{x}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k}{lambda} \PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{n}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{weight}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Export early for debugging}: Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.to\_pandas()}} to inspect intermediate results

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Filter before grouping}: Reduce data volume before aggregation for better performance

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Name aggregations clearly}: Use descriptive names in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{summarise()}}

\end{enumerate}

\paragraph{When to Use Which}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/graph_ops:when-to-use-which}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Use DSL when:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
You need quick, exploratory queries

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
You want SQL\sphinxhyphen{}like syntax for familiar, readable code

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
You’re doing simple filtering and centrality computation

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
You need to quickly prototype an analysis

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Use graph\_ops when:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
You need complex data transformations with custom logic

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
You want full type hints and IDE autocompletion

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
You’re building reusable analysis pipelines

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
You need grouping and aggregation operations

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
You’re integrating with pandas workflows

\end{itemize}

\subsection{Analysis Recipes \& Workflows}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/recipes_and_workflows:analysis-recipes-workflows}}\label{\detokenize{user_guide/recipes_and_workflows:recipes}}\label{\detokenize{user_guide/recipes_and_workflows::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This guide provides \sphinxstylestrong{practical recipes} for \sphinxstylestrong{common analysis workflows} in py3plex.
Each recipe is a \sphinxstylestrong{complete, ready\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}use solution} for a real\sphinxhyphen{}world task.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{DSL for Rapid Analysis}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Many recipes can be expressed concisely using the DSL:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{dsl}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{L}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Quick hub identification}
\PYG{n}{hubs} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{where}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{degree\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}gt}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{compute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{order\PYGZus{}by}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZhy{}betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{limit}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Multi\PYGZhy{}layer comparison}
\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{layer\PYGZus{}name} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{social}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{work}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{family}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
        \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
         \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{from\PYGZus{}layers}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{L}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{layer\PYGZus{}name}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
         \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{compute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{clustering}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
         \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{layer\PYGZus{}name}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{count}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ nodes}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\paragraph{Recipe 1: Load Network from Multiple File Formats}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/recipes_and_workflows:recipe-1-load-network-from-multiple-file-formats}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Task:} Load \sphinxstylestrong{multilayer networks} from various \sphinxstylestrong{file formats} (edgelist, GraphML, CSV).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Script:} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{examples/io\_and\_data/example\_IO.py}}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{core}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{multinet}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} From multiedgelist (node1, layer1, node2, layer2, weight)}
\PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{load\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{data/network.txt}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{multiedgelist}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{n}{directed}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{False}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} From GraphML}
\PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{load\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{data/network.graphml}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{graphml}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} From edges list programmatically}
\PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{load\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}

\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Check which nodes are in largest community}

                      \PYG{k}{if} \PYG{n}{comm} \PYG{o}{==} \PYG{n}{largest\PYGZus{}comm}\PYG{p}{]}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}n}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Nodes in largest community: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{largest\PYGZus{}comm\PYGZus{}nodes}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{...}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Task:} Process large multilayer networks without running out of memory.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\subsubsection{Tips \& Best Practices}

\paragraph{General Tips}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/recipes_and_workflows:general-tips}}\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Always set random seeds} for reproducibility:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\item {}

\sphinxstylestrong{Save intermediate results} for long analyses:

\begin{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar

\paragraph{Performance Tips}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/recipes_and_workflows:performance-tips}}\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{For large networks}, process layers independently

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\paragraph{Visualization Tips}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/recipes_and_workflows:visualization-tips}}\begin{enumerate}

\item {}

\begin{itemize}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\end{enumerate}


\paragraph{Community Detection Tips}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/recipes_and_workflows:community-detection-tips}}\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Tune resolution parameter} (gamma):
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Higher gamma \(\rightarrow\) more, smaller communities

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Lower gamma \(\rightarrow\) fewer, larger communities

\end{itemize}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Tune coupling parameter} (omega) for multilayer:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Higher omega \(\rightarrow\) communities span layers

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Lower omega \(\rightarrow\) layer\sphinxhyphen{}specific communities

\end{itemize}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Run multiple times} with different random seeds to check stability

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Compare multiple algorithms} to validate findings

\end{enumerate}

\PYG{p}{)}

     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{compute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{clustering}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{limit}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{20}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{export\PYGZus{}csv}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{top\PYGZus{}hubs.csv}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Display results}

         \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{compute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{pagerank}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
         \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{order\PYGZus{}by}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZhy{}betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
         \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{limit}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{top\PYGZus{}n}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Use the template with different parameters}

\PYG{p}{)}

\paragraph{Recipe 22: DSL with EXPLAIN Mode}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/recipes_and_workflows:recipe-22-dsl-with-explain-mode}}

\sphinxstylestrong{Task:} Optimize queries before execution on large networks.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{DSL Example: Query Optimization}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{dsl}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{L}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Build a potentially expensive query}
\PYG{n}{query} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{compute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} O(n\(\sp{\text{3}}\)) operation!}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{order\PYGZus{}by}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZhy{}betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{limit}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Check the execution plan first}
\PYG{n}{plan} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{query}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{explain}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Query Execution Plan:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{step} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{plan}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{steps}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZhy{} }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{step}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{description}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{  Complexity: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{step}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{estimated\PYGZus{}complexity}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Check for warnings}
\PYG{k}{if} \PYG{n}{plan}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{warnings}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}n}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Warnings:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{warning} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{plan}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{warnings}\PYG{p}{:}
        \PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{⚠️  }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{warning}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Optimized version: filter first to reduce computation}
\PYG{n}{optimized\PYGZus{}query} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{where}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{degree\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}gt}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{)}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Pre\PYGZhy{}filter to reduce nodes}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{compute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{order\PYGZus{}by}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZhy{}betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{limit}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Execute the optimized query}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{optimized\PYGZus{}query}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}

\subsubsection{Why Case Studies Matter}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/case_studies:why-case-studies-matter}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Reading about algorithms is one thing. Applying them to real problems is another entirely.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The case studies in this chapter come from real research domains where multilayer network analysis has proven valuable. They’re not toy examples—they represent the kinds of questions that researchers and practitioners actually ask:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
How do we identify proteins that are likely to be functionally important?

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Which social media influencers are genuinely cross\sphinxhyphen{}platform celebrities versus one\sphinxhyphen{}hit wonders?

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
What happens to urban mobility when a major transit hub fails?

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Which academic researchers are likely to collaborate based on their publication patterns?

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Each case study walks through the complete analysis workflow, from problem formulation through data modeling, analysis, and interpretation. Pay attention not just to the code, but to the reasoning behind each decision.


\subsubsection{Lessons from the Field}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/case_studies:lessons-from-the-field}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Before diving into specific cases, here are some lessons learned from applying multilayer network analysis to real problems:

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Modeling decisions matter more than algorithm choice.} Whether you use Louvain or Infomap for community detection is less important than whether you’ve correctly identified what should be a layer, what should be a node, and how layers should be coupled. Spend your time on modeling.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Start simple, add complexity as needed.} It’s tempting to immediately build a network with ten layers, weighted edges, temporal dynamics, and inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer dependencies. Resist this urge. Start with the simplest model that might answer your question, and add complexity only when you can demonstrate it improves your analysis.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Validate with domain knowledge.} Network analysis can reveal surprising patterns—but it can also reveal artifacts of your modeling choices. Always sanity\sphinxhyphen{}check results against what domain experts know. If your community detection puts obviously unrelated entities in the same cluster, you have a modeling problem.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Document your decisions.} When you return to an analysis six months later, you won’t remember why you chose certain parameters. Write down your reasoning. Future\sphinxhyphen{}you will thank present\sphinxhyphen{}you.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsubsection{Case Study 1: Biological Network Analysis}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/case_studies:case-study-1-biological-network-analysis}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Identifying high\sphinxhyphen{}confidence protein interactions and functional modules}


\paragraph{Real\sphinxhyphen{}World Impact}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/case_studies:real-world-impact}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Protein\sphinxhyphen{}protein interaction (PPI) networks are foundational to understanding cellular function. The proteins in your body don’t work alone—they form complexes, signaling cascades, and metabolic pathways. Knowing which proteins interact helps researchers:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Understand disease mechanisms:} Many diseases result from disrupted protein interactions

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Identify drug targets:} Proteins central to disease networks are potential therapeutic targets

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Predict protein function:} A protein’s interactors suggest its biological role

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The challenge? PPI data comes from multiple experimental methods, each with different biases and error rates. High\sphinxhyphen{}throughput screens find many interactions quickly but include false positives. Literature curation is accurate but incomplete. How do you combine these sources intelligently?

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{This is exactly what multilayer network analysis is for.}


\paragraph{Multilayer Protein\sphinxhyphen{}Protein Interaction Network}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/case_studies:multilayer-protein-protein-interaction-network}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Problem Context:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
You’re a computational biologist studying protein interactions in yeast. You have PPI data from three experimental sources with different reliability levels:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Yeast two\sphinxhyphen{}hybrid (Y2H):} High\sphinxhyphen{}throughput but many false positives

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Affinity purification mass spectrometry (AP\sphinxhyphen{}MS):} More reliable but biased toward stable complexes

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Literature curated:} Highly reliable but incomplete

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
You want to:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Find functional modules (groups of proteins that work together)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Identify proteins that are central across evidence types (likely real interactions)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Discover proteins that bridge different functional modules

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Data Modeling Decisions:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Node type:} Proteins (same set across layers for multiplex analysis)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Layers:} One per evidence type (Y2H, AP\sphinxhyphen{}MS, Literature)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Edges:} Physical protein\sphinxhyphen{}protein interactions

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Network type:} Multiplex (same proteins, different interaction evidence)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Complete Code:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{core}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{multinet}
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{algorithms}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{statistics}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{multilayer\PYGZus{}statistics} \PYG{k}{as} \PYG{n}{mls}
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{algorithms}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{community\PYGZus{}detection}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{multilayer\PYGZus{}modularity}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{louvain\PYGZus{}multilayer}
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{collections}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{Counter}
\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{numpy}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{as}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{np}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} === 1. Create the network ===}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} In practice, you\PYGZsq{}d load from files; here we create a toy example}
\PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{multiplex}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Simulated PPI data (protein pairs by evidence type)}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Replace with your actual data loading}

The analysis reveals several insights:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{High\sphinxhyphen{}confidence interactions} (CDC28\sphinxhyphen{}CLB2, ACT1\sphinxhyphen{}TPM1) appear in all three evidence types, making them likely true interactions suitable for downstream analysis.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Functional modules} correspond to known protein complexes:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Cell cycle regulators (CDC28, CLB2, CLB5, CKS1, SIC1)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Actin cytoskeleton (ACT1, MYO2, TPM1, ABP1)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
DNA replication origin complex (CDC6, ORC1, ORC2, ORC3)

\end{itemize}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Bridge proteins} with high versatility may connect different functional modules and could be interesting drug targets or key regulators.

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Adapting to Your Data:}
\begin{enumerate}

Replace the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ppi\_data}} dictionary with your actual data loading code

\sphinxAtStartPar
Add Gene Ontology enrichment analysis to validate that communities match known functional annotations

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Consider edge weights based on evidence quality (e.g., literature = 3.0, APMS = 2.0, Y2H = 1.0)

\end{enumerate}


\subsubsection{Case Study 2: Multi\sphinxhyphen{}Platform Social Network Analysis}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/case_studies:case-study-2-multi-platform-social-network-analysis}}

\paragraph{Cross\sphinxhyphen{}Platform Influence Analysis}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/case_studies:cross-platform-influence-analysis}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Problem Context:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
You’re a social media researcher studying how influencers operate across platforms. You have data from three platforms:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Twitter/X:} Public follower/following relationships

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{YouTube:} Subscription relationships

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Instagram:} Follow relationships

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
You want to:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Identify influencers who are successful across platforms (vs. platform\sphinxhyphen{}specific)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Understand how different platforms are related (do the same people follow each other?)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Find communities that span platforms

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Data Modeling Decisions:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Node type:} Users (mapped across platforms using verified identities)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Layers:} One per platform (Twitter, YouTube, Instagram)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Edges:} Follow/subscribe relationships (directed in reality, undirected for this analysis)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Network type:} Multiplex (same users, different platforms)

\end{itemize}

\subsubsection{Case Study 3: Multi\sphinxhyphen{}Modal Transportation Analysis}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/case_studies:case-study-3-multi-modal-transportation-analysis}}

\paragraph{Urban Mobility and Resilience}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/case_studies:urban-mobility-and-resilience}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Problem Context:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
You’re an urban transportation analyst studying a city’s public transit system. You have network data for:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Metro/Subway:} High\sphinxhyphen{}capacity, fixed routes

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Bus:} Lower capacity, more flexible routes

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Bike\sphinxhyphen{}share:} Individual, first/last mile connections

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
You want to:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Identify multimodal hubs (stations serving multiple transport modes)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Analyze network resilience (what happens if a metro station closes?)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Find communities (“travel basins”) that span transport modes

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Data Modeling Decisions:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Node type:} Stations/stops (with geographic coordinates)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Layers:} One per transport mode (Metro, Bus, Bikeshare)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Edges:} Direct connections between stops (can walk/transfer)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Network type:} Multiplex with geographic coupling (same location = same node)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxstylestrong{Adapting to Your Data:}

\paragraph{General Adaptation Process}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/case_studies:general-adaptation-process}}\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Identify your entities} \(\rightarrow\) These become node types or layers

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Identify your relationships} \(\rightarrow\) These become edges

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Decide multiplex vs. heterogeneous:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Same entities, different relationship types \(\rightarrow\) Multiplex

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Different entity types \(\rightarrow\) Heterogeneous

\end{itemize}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Map identifiers} \(\rightarrow\) Ensure same entity has same ID across layers

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Choose appropriate metrics} based on your research questions

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Validate with domain knowledge} \(\rightarrow\) Do results match expectations?

\end{enumerate}

\subsubsection{Conclusion: Patterns Across Domains}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/case_studies:conclusion-patterns-across-domains}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Looking across these case studies, several patterns emerge:

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Multilayer structure reveals what single\sphinxhyphen{}layer analysis misses.} In the PPI network, interactions confirmed by multiple evidence types are more reliable—information you lose if you flatten into a single network. In the social network, cross\sphinxhyphen{}platform influencers are fundamentally different from single\sphinxhyphen{}platform celebrities. In transportation, failure cascades depend on inter\sphinxhyphen{}modal connections.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{The coupling parameter matters.} Lower coupling (omega \textless{} 1) finds layer\sphinxhyphen{}specific communities; higher coupling (omega \textgreater{} 1) finds cross\sphinxhyphen{}layer communities. The right choice depends on your question. If you expect the same underlying structure across layers, use higher coupling. If layers represent truly different phenomena, use lower coupling.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Validation requires domain expertise.} Network analysis can find structure, but whether that structure is meaningful requires interpretation. Do the detected communities correspond to known functional categories? Do the identified hubs match known influential entities? Ground your analysis in domain knowledge.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Start simple.} Each case study could be made more complex—weighted edges, temporal dynamics, more layers, heterogeneous node types. But starting simple lets you understand what’s happening and catch errors before the analysis becomes opaque.


\paragraph{The Meta\sphinxhyphen{}Lesson}
\label{\detokenize{user_guide/case_studies:the-meta-lesson}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
These case studies demonstrate a workflow pattern:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Formulate your question} in terms of network structure

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Model your data} as nodes, edges, and layers

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Apply appropriate algorithms} based on your question

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Interpret results} using domain knowledge

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Iterate} as you learn what works

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This pattern applies regardless of domain. The specific proteins, users, or stations change; the analytical approach remains similar.

\subsubsection{Quick Start}
\label{\detokenize{deployment/cli_and_docker:quick-start}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The fastest way to get started with Py3plex using Docker:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Clone the repository}
git\PYG{+w}{ }clone\PYG{+w}{ }https://github.com/SkBlaz/py3plex.git
\PYG{n+nb}{cd}\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Build the Docker image}
docker\PYG{+w}{ }build\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}t\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex:latest\PYG{+w}{ }.

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Run a self\PYGZhy{}test to verify installation}
docker\PYG{+w}{ }run\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}rm\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex:latest\PYG{+w}{ }selftest

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Display help}
docker\PYG{+w}{ }run\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}rm\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex:latest\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{help}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Show version}
docker\PYG{+w}{ }run\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}rm\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex:latest\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}version

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Run self\PYGZhy{}test}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Show help}
docker\PYG{+w}{ }run\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}rm\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex:latest\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{help}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Show help for a specific command}

\label{\detokenize{deployment/cli_and_docker:id1}}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Show help}
docker\PYGZhy{}compose\PYG{+w}{ }run\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}rm\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{help}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} \PYGZhy{} Volume mounting}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Usage examples:}
