\subsubsection{Docker Configuration Files}
\label{\detokenize{deployment/cli_and_docker:docker-configuration-files}}

\paragraph{.dockerignore}
\label{\detokenize{deployment/cli_and_docker:dockerignore}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.dockerignore}} file controls which files are excluded from the Docker build context:

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Key exclusions:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Git and version control}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.git/}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.github/}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.gitignore}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Python artifacts}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\_\_pycache\_\_/}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*.pyc}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dist/}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{build/}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Virtual environments}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{venv/}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{env/}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Testing and coverage}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.pytest\_cache/}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{htmlcov/}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{coverage.*}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Documentation builds}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{docs/\_build/}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{docfiles/}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Examples and datasets}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{examples/}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{datasets/}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{multilayer\_datasets/}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Development files}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tests/}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{run\_tests.py}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{validate\_*.py}}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Why this matters:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Faster builds}: Smaller build context means faster Docker builds

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Smaller images}: Excludes unnecessary files from the final image

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Security}: Prevents accidental inclusion of sensitive files

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Efficiency}: Only includes files needed to run py3plex

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.dockerignore}} file is located in the repository root.

\sphinxAtStartPar
To verify your Docker setup is working correctly, use the included test script:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Run the test script}
./test\PYGZhy{}docker\PYGZhy{}setup.sh
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This script will:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Check Docker installation

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Verify all Docker\sphinxhyphen{}related files exist

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Build the Docker image

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Run basic py3plex commands (\textendash{}version, help, selftest)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Test volume mounting and file creation

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Clean up test artifacts

\end{itemize}


\paragraph{Permission Issues}
\label{\detokenize{deployment/cli_and_docker:permission-issues}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If you encounter permission issues with mounted volumes:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} On Linux, you might need to run with your user ID}

\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Container Not Found}
\label{\detokenize{deployment/cli_and_docker:container-not-found}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If the image isn’t found:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} List available images}
docker\PYG{+w}{ }images\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{|}\PYG{+w}{ }grep\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Rebuild if necessary}
docker\PYG{+w}{ }build\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}t\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex:latest\PYG{+w}{ }.
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Network Issues During Build}
\label{\detokenize{deployment/cli_and_docker:network-issues-during-build}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If you encounter network timeouts during build:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Increase timeout}
docker\PYG{+w}{ }build\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}build\PYGZhy{}arg\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{PIP\PYGZus{}DEFAULT\PYGZus{}TIMEOUT}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m}{300}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}t\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex:latest\PYG{+w}{ }.

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Or use a different PyPI mirror}
docker\PYG{+w}{ }build\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}build\PYGZhy{}arg\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{PIP\PYGZus{}INDEX\PYGZus{}URL}\PYG{o}{=}https://pypi.tuna.tsinghua.edu.cn/simple\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}t\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex:latest\PYG{+w}{ }.
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Out of Disk Space}
\label{\detokenize{deployment/cli_and_docker:out-of-disk-space}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Clean up unused Docker resources:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Remove unused images}
docker\PYG{+w}{ }image\PYG{+w}{ }prune\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}a

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Remove all stopped containers, unused networks, and dangling images}
docker\PYG{+w}{ }system\PYG{+w}{ }prune\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}a
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Debugging Build Issues}
\label{\detokenize{deployment/cli_and_docker:debugging-build-issues}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Build with verbose output:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
docker\PYG{+w}{ }build\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}progress\PYG{o}{=}plain\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}no\PYGZhy{}cache\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}t\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex:latest\PYG{+w}{ }.
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{Best Practices}
\label{\detokenize{deployment/cli_and_docker:best-practices}}\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Use Volume Mounts}: Always mount volumes for input/output files

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Use \textendash{}rm Flag}: Remove containers after execution with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}rm}} to save space

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Tag Images}: Use specific tags (e.g., \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{py3plex:0.95a}}) for reproducibility

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Keep Data Separate}: Store network files in the mounted \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{data}} directory

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Use Docker Compose}: For repeated operations, docker\sphinxhyphen{}compose simplifies commands

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Regular Updates}: Rebuild the image periodically to get latest py3plex updates

\end{enumerate}

\subsubsection{Sparse Matrix Backend}
\label{\detokenize{deployment/performance_scalability:sparse-matrix-backend}}

\paragraph{Why Sparse Matrices?}
\label{\detokenize{deployment/performance_scalability:why-sparse-matrices}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Most real\sphinxhyphen{}world networks are \sphinxstylestrong{sparse} (few edges compared to possible edges). Sparse matrices:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Reduce memory usage} by 10\sphinxhyphen{}100x for typical networks

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Speed up} matrix operations (multiplication, inversion)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Enable} analysis of larger networks

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Example:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{numpy}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{as}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{np}
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{scipy}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{sparse}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{csr\PYGZus{}matrix}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Dense representation (10k × 10k network)}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Memory: 10,000\PYGZca{}2 × 8 bytes = 800 MB}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Sparse representation (with 1\PYGZpc{} density)}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Memory: \PYGZti{}8 MB (100x reduction!)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Automatic Sparse Matrix Usage}
\label{\detokenize{deployment/performance_scalability:automatic-sparse-matrix-usage}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Py3plex \sphinxstylestrong{automatically uses sparse matrices} for:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Supra\sphinxhyphen{}adjacency matrix operations

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Large network storage (\textgreater{}1000 nodes)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Matrix\sphinxhyphen{}based algorithms (PageRank, spectral methods)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Verify sparse usage:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{core}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{multinet}

\PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{load\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{large\PYGZus{}network.csv}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{multiedgelist}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Get sparse adjacency matrix}
\PYG{n}{adj\PYGZus{}sparse} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}sparse\PYGZus{}adjacency\PYGZus{}matrix}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Matrix size: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{adj\PYGZus{}sparse}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{shape}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Non\PYGZhy{}zero entries: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{adj\PYGZus{}sparse}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nnz}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Sparsity: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{adj\PYGZus{}sparse}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nnz}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{adj\PYGZus{}sparse}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{shape}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{.2\PYGZpc{}}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Force Sparse Operations}
\label{\detokenize{deployment/performance_scalability:force-sparse-operations}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For custom algorithms, explicitly use sparse operations:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{scipy}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{sparse}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{csr\PYGZus{}matrix}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{lil\PYGZus{}matrix}
\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{numpy}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{as}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{np}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Create sparse adjacency matrix}
\PYG{n}{adj} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{lil\PYGZus{}matrix}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{n\PYGZus{}nodes}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{n\PYGZus{}nodes}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{u}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{v} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{core\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{edges}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n}{i}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{j} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{node\PYGZus{}to\PYGZus{}idx}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{u}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{node\PYGZus{}to\PYGZus{}idx}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{v}\PYG{p}{]}
    \PYG{n}{adj}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{i}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{j}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}
    \PYG{n}{adj}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{j}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{i}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Undirected}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Convert to efficient format for operations}
\PYG{n}{adj\PYGZus{}csr} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{adj}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{tocsr}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Sparse matrix operations are MUCH faster}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{adj\PYGZus{}csr} \PYG{o}{@} \PYG{n}{adj\PYGZus{}csr}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Matrix multiplication}

\sphinxAtStartPar

\end{itemize}

\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{os}

\PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Memory after loading: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}memory\PYGZus{}usage}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{.1f}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ MB}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{gc}

    \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{load\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{file}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{multiedgelist}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Compute statistics}

    \PYG{n}{results}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{append}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{result}\PYG{p}{)}

    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Free memory}

\subsubsection{Alternative Tools for Scale}
\label{\detokenize{deployment/performance_scalability:alternative-tools-for-scale}}

\paragraph{When Py3plex Isn’t Enough}
\label{\detokenize{deployment/performance_scalability:when-py3plex-isn-t-enough}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For networks \textgreater{}100k nodes, consider:

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{igraph} (C\sphinxhyphen{}based, very fast):

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{igraph}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{as}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{ig}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} 10\PYGZhy{}100x faster for large networks}
\PYG{n}{g} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{ig}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{Graph}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{Read\PYGZus{}GraphML}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{large\PYGZus{}network.graphml}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{communities} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{g}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{community\PYGZus{}multilevel}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Export back to Py3plex if needed}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} (via GraphML or edge list)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{graph\sphinxhyphen{}tool} (C++, fastest):

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{graph\PYGZus{}tool}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{all}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{as}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{gt}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Fastest for \PYGZgt{}1M edges}
\PYG{n}{g} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{gt}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{load\PYGZus{}graph}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{large\PYGZus{}network.graphml}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{communities} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{gt}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{community\PYGZus{}structure}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{minimize\PYGZus{}blockmodel\PYGZus{}dl}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{g}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{NetworKit} (C++, parallel):

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{networkit}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{as}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{nk}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Excellent for parallel algorithms}
\PYG{n}{G} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{nk}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{readGraph}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{large\PYGZus{}network.edgelist}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{nk}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{Format}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{EdgeList}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{communities} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{nk}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{community}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{detectCommunities}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{G}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{Quick Performance Checklist}
\label{\detokenize{deployment/performance_scalability:quick-performance-checklist}}

\paragraph{Before Running on Large Network}
\label{\detokenize{deployment/performance_scalability:before-running-on-large-network}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
[ ] Enable sparse matrices (automatic for most ops)
[ ] Sample network if \PYGZgt{}10k nodes
[ ] Choose efficient algorithms (degree \PYGZgt{} betweenness)
[ ] Limit visualization detail
[ ] Monitor memory usage
[ ] Use batch processing for multiple networks
[ ] Consider alternative tools if \PYGZgt{}100k nodes
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Optimization Order}
\label{\detokenize{deployment/performance_scalability:optimization-order}}\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Use sparse matrices} (biggest impact, usually automatic)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Sample network} (if \textgreater{}10k nodes)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Choose efficient algorithms} (avoid O(n\(\sp{\text{3}}\)) operations)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Parallelize} (if multi\sphinxhyphen{}core available)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{GPU acceleration} (only if CUDA GPU available)

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The py3plex GUI provides a web\sphinxhyphen{}based interface for interactive multilayer network exploration.

\sphinxAtStartPar

cp\PYG{+w}{ }.env.example\PYG{+w}{ }.env

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Open in browser}

\subsubsection{Architecture}
\label{\detokenize{gui/gui_user_guide:architecture}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                     Nginx (Port 8080)                        │
│  Reverse Proxy + Static Serving                             │
└───────┬────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────┘
        │                        │
        ▼                        ▼
┌──────────────┐         ┌──────────────────────┐
│   Frontend   │         │      FastAPI         │
│ React + Vite │         │  (Port 8000)         │
│   (Dev HMR)  │         │  py3plex wrapper     │
└──────────────┘         └──────────┬───────────┘
                                    │
                    ┌───────────────┴────────────────┐
                    ▼                                ▼
            ┌──────────────┐                ┌──────────────┐
            │    Redis     │                │    Celery    │
            │  (Port 6379) │◄──────────────│    Worker    │
            │    Broker    │                │  + Flower    │
            └──────────────┘                └──────────────┘
                    │
                    ▼
            ┌──────────────────────────────────┐
            │  Shared Volume: /data            │
            │  \PYGZhy{} uploads/                      │
            │  \PYGZhy{} artifacts/                    │
            │  \PYGZhy{} workspaces/                   │
            └──────────────────────────────────┘
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Key Components:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Frontend}: React 18 + Vite + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{API}: FastAPI (Python 3.12) with py3plex integration

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Worker}: Celery for long\sphinxhyphen{}running analysis jobs

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Broker}: Redis for job queue

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Proxy}: Nginx for unified access

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Monitoring}: Flower dashboard for job inspection

\end{itemize}

\paragraph{Local Development Against py3plex}
\label{\detokenize{gui/gui_user_guide:local-development-against-py3plex}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The py3plex repository root is bind\sphinxhyphen{}mounted read\sphinxhyphen{}only into containers at \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{/workspace}}:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c}{\PYGZsh{} In Dockerfile.api}
\PYG{k}{ARG}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{PY3PLEX\PYGZus{}PATH}\PYG{o}{=}/workspace
\PYG{k}{RUN}\PYG{+w}{ }pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}e\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZdl{}\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nv}{PY3PLEX\PYGZus{}PATH}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Benefits:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Changes to py3plex core reflect immediately (no rebuild)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Editable install for development

\sphinxAtStartPar
Isolated GUI code under \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{gui/}}

\end{itemize}

\subsubsection{Production Deployment}
\label{\detokenize{gui/gui_user_guide:production-deployment}}

\paragraph{Static Build (Recommended)}
\label{\detokenize{gui/gui_user_guide:static-build-recommended}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For production, serve pre\sphinxhyphen{}built frontend assets:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c}{\PYGZsh{} Modify Dockerfile.frontend to use multi\PYGZhy{}stage build}
\PYG{k}{FROM}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{node:20\PYGZhy{}alpine}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{AS}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{builder}
\PYG{k}{WORKDIR}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{/app}
\PYG{k}{COPY}\PYG{+w}{ }frontend/\PYG{+w}{ }.
\PYG{k}{RUN}\PYG{+w}{ }npm\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }npm\PYG{+w}{ }run\PYG{+w}{ }build

\PYG{k}{FROM}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{nginx:alpine}
\PYG{k}{COPY}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}from\PYG{o}{=}builder\PYG{+w}{ }/app/dist\PYG{+w}{ }/usr/share/nginx/html
\PYG{k}{COPY}\PYG{+w}{ }nginx/nginx.conf\PYG{+w}{ }/etc/nginx/nginx.conf
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Update \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{docker\sphinxhyphen{}compose.yml}}:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n+nt}{frontend}\PYG{p}{:}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n+nt}{build}\PYG{p}{:}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n+nt}{context}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+lScalar+lScalarPlain}{.}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n+nt}{dockerfile}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+lScalar+lScalarPlain}{Dockerfile.frontend.prod}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Remove dev server volume mounts}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Security Considerations}
\label{\detokenize{gui/gui_user_guide:security-considerations}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Set \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{CORS allow\_origins}} to specific domains (not \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*}})

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Add authentication/authorization middleware

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use HTTPS (add TLS termination in Nginx)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Validate file uploads strictly

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Set resource limits per user/job

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Enable Celery task rate limiting

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Current Status}: Development mode \sphinxhyphen{} suitable for local use only. Do not expose to public internet without proper security hardening.

\subsection{GUI Deployment Guide}
\label{\detokenize{gui/gui_deployment:gui-deployment-guide}}\label{\detokenize{gui/gui_deployment::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This guide covers deploying the py3plex web interface for production use.


\subsubsection{Overview}
\label{\detokenize{gui/gui_deployment:overview}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The py3plex GUI can be deployed in several ways:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Local Development} \sphinxhyphen{} Run directly on your machine

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Docker Container} \sphinxhyphen{} Isolated, reproducible environment

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Production Server} \sphinxhyphen{} Behind reverse proxy with TLS

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Cloud Deployment} \sphinxhyphen{} AWS, Azure, GCP, etc.

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See {\hyperref[\detokenize{gui/gui_user_guide::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Py3plex GUI}}}} for basic usage and {\hyperref[\detokenize{gui/gui_architecture::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Py3plex GUI Architecture}}}} for technical details.


\subsubsection{Local Development Setup}
\label{\detokenize{gui/gui_deployment:local-development-setup}}

\paragraph{Quick Start}
\label{\detokenize{gui/gui_deployment:quick-start}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Clone repository}
git\PYG{+w}{ }clone\PYG{+w}{ }https://github.com/SkBlaz/py3plex.git
\PYG{n+nb}{cd}\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Install with GUI dependencies}
pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}e\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}.[gui]\PYGZdq{}}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Start development server}
python\PYG{+w}{ }gui/app.py
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The GUI will be available at \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{http://localhost:5000}}.


\paragraph{Configuration}
\label{\detokenize{gui/gui_deployment:configuration}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Create a configuration file \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{gui/config.py}}:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Development configuration}
\PYG{n}{DEBUG} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{k+kc}{True}
\PYG{n}{HOST} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{0.0.0.0}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}
\PYG{n}{PORT} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{l+m+mi}{5000}
\PYG{n}{SECRET\PYGZus{}KEY} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{dev\PYGZhy{}secret\PYGZhy{}key\PYGZhy{}change\PYGZhy{}in\PYGZhy{}production}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Upload settings}
\PYG{n}{UPLOAD\PYGZus{}FOLDER} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{./uploads}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}
\PYG{n}{MAX\PYGZus{}CONTENT\PYGZus{}LENGTH} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{l+m+mi}{100} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1024} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1024}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} 100 MB max file size}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Allowed file extensions}
\PYG{n}{ALLOWED\PYGZus{}EXTENSIONS} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{txt}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{edgelist}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{graphml}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{gml}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{json}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{arrow}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{Docker Deployment}
\label{\detokenize{gui/gui_deployment:docker-deployment}}

\paragraph{Basic Docker Setup}
\label{\detokenize{gui/gui_deployment:basic-docker-setup}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The repository includes a Dockerfile for the GUI:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Build image}
docker\PYG{+w}{ }build\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}t\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex\PYGZhy{}gui:latest\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}f\PYG{+w}{ }gui/Dockerfile\PYG{+w}{ }.

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Run container}
docker\PYG{+w}{ }run\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}d\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYGZhy{}p\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5000}:5000\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYGZhy{}v\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{\PYGZdl{}(}\PYG{n+nb}{pwd}\PYG{k}{)}/data:/app/data\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}name\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex\PYGZhy{}gui\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }py3plex\PYGZhy{}gui:latest
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The GUI will be available at \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{http://localhost:5000}}.


\paragraph{Docker Compose}
\label{\detokenize{gui/gui_deployment:docker-compose}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Create \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{docker\sphinxhyphen{}compose.yml}}:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n+nt}{version}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s}{3.8}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZsq{}}

\PYG{n+nt}{services}\PYG{p}{:}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n+nt}{gui}\PYG{p}{:}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n+nt}{build}\PYG{p}{:}
\PYG{+w}{      }\PYG{n+nt}{context}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+lScalar+lScalarPlain}{.}
\PYG{+w}{      }\PYG{n+nt}{dockerfile}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+lScalar+lScalarPlain}{gui/Dockerfile}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n+nt}{ports}\PYG{p}{:}
\PYG{+w}{      }\PYG{p+pIndicator}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{5000:5000}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n+nt}{volumes}\PYG{p}{:}
\PYG{+w}{      }\PYG{p+pIndicator}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+lScalar+lScalarPlain}{./data:/app/data}
\PYG{+w}{      }\PYG{p+pIndicator}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+lScalar+lScalarPlain}{./uploads:/app/uploads}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n+nt}{environment}\PYG{p}{:}
\PYG{+w}{      }\PYG{p+pIndicator}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+lScalar+lScalarPlain}{FLASK\PYGZus{}ENV=production}
\PYG{+w}{      }\PYG{p+pIndicator}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+lScalar+lScalarPlain}{SECRET\PYGZus{}KEY=\PYGZdl{}\PYGZob{}SECRET\PYGZus{}KEY\PYGZcb{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n+nt}{restart}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+lScalar+lScalarPlain}{unless\PYGZhy{}stopped}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n+nt}{healthcheck}\PYG{p}{:}
\PYG{+w}{      }\PYG{n+nt}{test}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p+pIndicator}{[}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{CMD}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p+pIndicator}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{curl}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p+pIndicator}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZhy{}f}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p+pIndicator}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{http://localhost:5000/health}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p+pIndicator}{]}
\PYG{+w}{      }\PYG{n+nt}{interval}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+lScalar+lScalarPlain}{30s}
\PYG{+w}{      }\PYG{n+nt}{timeout}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+lScalar+lScalarPlain}{10s}
\PYG{+w}{      }\PYG{n+nt}{retries}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+lScalar+lScalarPlain}{3}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Set secret key}
\PYG{n+nb}{export}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{SECRET\PYGZus{}KEY}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k}{\PYGZdl{}(}python\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}c\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}import secrets; print(secrets.token\PYGZus{}hex(32))\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{k}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Start services}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Check logs}

\subsubsection{Production Deployment}
\label{\detokenize{gui/gui_deployment:production-deployment}}

\paragraph{Using Gunicorn}
\label{\detokenize{gui/gui_deployment:using-gunicorn}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For production, use a production WSGI server like Gunicorn:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Install Gunicorn}
pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }gunicorn

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Run with Gunicorn}
gunicorn\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}bind\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}.0.0.0:5000\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}workers\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}timeout\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{120}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}access\PYGZhy{}logfile\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}error\PYGZhy{}logfile\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }gui.app:app
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Supervisor Configuration}
\label{\detokenize{gui/gui_deployment:supervisor-configuration}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use Supervisor to manage the GUI process:

\sphinxAtStartPar
Create \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{/etc/supervisor/conf.d/py3plex\sphinxhyphen{}gui.conf}}:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{[program:py3plex\PYGZhy{}gui]}
\PYG{n+na}{command}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s}{/path/to/venv/bin/gunicorn \PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}bind 127.0.0.1:5000 \PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}workers 4 gui.app:app}
\PYG{n+na}{directory}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s}{/path/to/py3plex}
\PYG{n+na}{user}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s}{www\PYGZhy{}data}
\PYG{n+na}{autostart}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s}{true}
\PYG{n+na}{autorestart}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s}{true}
\PYG{n+na}{redirect\PYGZus{}stderr}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s}{true}
\PYG{n+na}{stdout\PYGZus{}logfile}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s}{/var/log/py3plex\PYGZhy{}gui.log}
\PYG{n+na}{environment=FLASK\PYGZus{}ENV}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{production}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{n+na}{,SECRET\PYGZus{}KEY}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{your\PYGZhy{}secret\PYGZhy{}key}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Start with:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
sudo\PYG{+w}{ }supervisorctl\PYG{+w}{ }reread
sudo\PYG{+w}{ }supervisorctl\PYG{+w}{ }update
sudo\PYG{+w}{ }supervisorctl\PYG{+w}{ }start\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex\PYGZhy{}gui
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Systemd Service}
\label{\detokenize{gui/gui_deployment:systemd-service}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Alternative: use systemd:

\sphinxAtStartPar
Create \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{/etc/systemd/system/py3plex\sphinxhyphen{}gui.service}}:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{[Unit]}
\PYG{n+na}{Description}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s}{Py3plex GUI}
\PYG{n+na}{After}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s}{network.target}

\PYG{k}{[Service]}
\PYG{n+na}{Type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s}{notify}
\PYG{n+na}{User}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s}{www\PYGZhy{}data}
\PYG{n+na}{WorkingDirectory}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s}{/path/to/py3plex}
\PYG{n+na}{Environment}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{FLASK\PYGZus{}ENV=production}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{n+na}{Environment}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{SECRET\PYGZus{}KEY=your\PYGZhy{}secret\PYGZhy{}key}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{n+na}{ExecStart}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s}{/path/to/venv/bin/gunicorn \PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}bind 127.0.0.1:5000 \PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}workers 4 gui.app:app}
\PYG{n+na}{ExecReload}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s}{/bin/kill \PYGZhy{}s HUP \PYGZdl{}MAINPID}
\PYG{n+na}{KillMode}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s}{mixed}
\PYG{n+na}{TimeoutStopSec}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s}{5}
\PYG{n+na}{PrivateTmp}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s}{true}

\PYG{k}{[Install]}
\PYG{n+na}{WantedBy}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s}{multi\PYGZhy{}user.target}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Enable and start:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
sudo\PYG{+w}{ }systemctl\PYG{+w}{ }daemon\PYGZhy{}reload
sudo\PYG{+w}{ }systemctl\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{enable}\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex\PYGZhy{}gui
sudo\PYG{+w}{ }systemctl\PYG{+w}{ }start\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex\PYGZhy{}gui
sudo\PYG{+w}{ }systemctl\PYG{+w}{ }status\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex\PYGZhy{}gui
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{Reverse Proxy Setup}

\sphinxAtStartPar

Create \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{/etc/nginx/sites\sphinxhyphen{}available/py3plex\sphinxhyphen{}gui}}:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{server}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{k+kn}{listen}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{80}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{k+kn}{server\PYGZus{}name}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{py3plex.yourdomain.com}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Redirect to HTTPS}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{k+kn}{return}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{301}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{https://}\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}server\PYGZus{}name\PYGZdl{}request\PYGZus{}uri}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}

\PYG{k}{server}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{k+kn}{listen}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{443}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{ssl}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{http2}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{k+kn}{server\PYGZus{}name}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{py3plex.yourdomain.com}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} SSL certificates (use Let\PYGZsq{}s Encrypt)}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{k+kn}{ssl\PYGZus{}certificate}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{/etc/letsencrypt/live/py3plex.yourdomain.com/fullchain.pem}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{k+kn}{ssl\PYGZus{}certificate\PYGZus{}key}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{/etc/letsencrypt/live/py3plex.yourdomain.com/privkey.pem}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Security headers}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{k+kn}{add\PYGZus{}header}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{X\PYGZhy{}Frame\PYGZhy{}Options}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}SAMEORIGIN\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{always}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{k+kn}{add\PYGZus{}header}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{X\PYGZhy{}Content\PYGZhy{}Type\PYGZhy{}Options}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}nosniff\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{always}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{k+kn}{add\PYGZus{}header}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{X\PYGZhy{}XSS\PYGZhy{}Protection}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}1}\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{mode=block\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{always}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Upload size limit}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{k+kn}{client\PYGZus{}max\PYGZus{}body\PYGZus{}size}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{100M}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{k+kn}{location}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{/}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{        }\PYG{k+kn}{proxy\PYGZus{}pass}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{http://127.0.0.1:5000}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{        }\PYG{k+kn}{proxy\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}header}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{Host}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}host}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{        }\PYG{k+kn}{proxy\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}header}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{X\PYGZhy{}Real\PYGZhy{}IP}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}remote\PYGZus{}addr}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{        }\PYG{k+kn}{proxy\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}header}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{X\PYGZhy{}Forwarded\PYGZhy{}For}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}proxy\PYGZus{}add\PYGZus{}x\PYGZus{}forwarded\PYGZus{}for}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{        }\PYG{k+kn}{proxy\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}header}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{X\PYGZhy{}Forwarded\PYGZhy{}Proto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}scheme}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}

\paragraph{Apache Configuration}

\sphinxAtStartPar

\PYG{n+nt}{\PYGZlt{}VirtualHost}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{*:80}\PYG{n+nt}{\PYGZgt{}}

\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n+nb}{Header}\PYG{+w}{ }always\PYG{+w}{ }set\PYG{+w}{ }X\PYGZhy{}Content\PYGZhy{}Type\PYGZhy{}Options\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}nosniff\PYGZdq{}}

\paragraph{SSL/TLS with Let’s Encrypt}
\label{\detokenize{gui/gui_deployment:ssl-tls-with-let-s-encrypt}}

\paragraph{Automated Backups}
\label{\detokenize{gui/gui_deployment:automated-backups}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+ch}{\PYGZsh{}!/bin/bash}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} backup.sh}

\PYG{n+nv}{BACKUP\PYGZus{}DIR}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}/backups/py3plex\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{n+nv}{DATE}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k}{\PYGZdl{}(}date\PYG{+w}{ }+\PYGZpc{}Y\PYGZpc{}m\PYGZpc{}d\PYGZus{}\PYGZpc{}H\PYGZpc{}M\PYGZpc{}S\PYG{k}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Backup uploads}
tar\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}czf\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}BACKUP\PYGZus{}DIR}\PYG{l+s+s2}{/uploads\PYGZus{}}\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}DATE}\PYG{l+s+s2}{.tar.gz}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }/path/to/uploads

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Backup database (if using one)}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} pg\PYGZus{}dump py3plex \PYGZgt{} \PYGZdq{}\PYGZdl{}BACKUP\PYGZus{}DIR/db\PYGZus{}\PYGZdl{}DATE.sql\PYGZdq{}}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Cleanup old backups (keep last 7 days)}
find\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}BACKUP\PYGZus{}DIR}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}type\PYG{+w}{ }f\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}mtime\PYG{+w}{ }+7\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}delete
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\PYG{l+m}{0}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }*\PYG{+w}{ }*\PYG{+w}{ }*\PYG{+w}{ }/path/to/backup.sh

\subsubsection{Rate Limits}
\label{\detokenize{gui/gui_api_reference:rate-limits}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Default rate limits (configurable):
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
200 requests per day per IP

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
50 requests per hour per IP

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
10 uploads per hour per IP

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Rate limit headers in responses:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
X\PYGZhy{}RateLimit\PYGZhy{}Limit: 50
X\PYGZhy{}RateLimit\PYGZhy{}Remaining: 45
X\PYGZhy{}RateLimit\PYGZhy{}Reset: 1674480000
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\subsubsection{Data Flow}
\label{\detokenize{gui/gui_architecture:data-flow}}

\paragraph{Upload \& Parse Flow}
\label{\detokenize{gui/gui_architecture:upload-parse-flow}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
User \(\rightarrow\) Frontend \(\rightarrow\) API /upload \(\rightarrow\) io.save\PYGZus{}upload()
                                      ↓
                              io.load\PYGZus{}graph\PYGZus{}from\PYGZus{}file()
                                      ↓
                              NetworkX graph loaded
                                      ↓
                              Stored in GRAPH\PYGZus{}REGISTRY
                                      ↓
                              Return graph\PYGZus{}id to frontend
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Analysis Job Flow}
\label{\detokenize{gui/gui_architecture:analysis-job-flow}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
User \(\rightarrow\) Frontend \(\rightarrow\) API /analysis/centrality
                        ↓
                  Create Celery task
                        ↓
                  Return job\PYGZus{}id
                        ↓
                  Task queued in Redis
                        ↓
                  Worker picks up task
                        ↓
              task.update\PYGZus{}state(progress=30)
                        ↓
              services.metrics.compute\PYGZus{}centrality()
                        ↓
              Save results to /data/artifacts/
                        ↓
              task.update\PYGZus{}state(progress=100, result=\PYGZob{}...\PYGZcb{})
                        ↓
User ← Frontend ← API /jobs/\PYGZob{}job\PYGZus{}id\PYGZcb{} ← Redis result backend
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\subsubsection{System Overview}
\label{\detokenize{dev/code_architecture:system-overview}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
py3plex is built as a \sphinxstylestrong{modular, layered architecture} with clear separation of concerns:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│          High\PYGZhy{}Level Interfaces (Wrappers)           │
│  node2vec\PYGZus{}embedding, benchmark\PYGZus{}nodes                │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                        ↓
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│              Algorithms Layer                        │
│  ┌──────────────┬───────────────┬─────────────────┐ │
│  │  Community   │  Statistics   │  Multilayer     │ │
│  │  Detection   │               │  Algorithms     │ │
│  └──────────────┴───────────────┴─────────────────┘ │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                        ↓
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│            Visualization Layer                       │
│  ┌──────────────┬───────────────┬─────────────────┐ │
│  │  Multilayer  │  Drawing      │  Layout         │ │
│  │  Plots       │  Machinery    │  Algorithms     │ │
│  └──────────────┴───────────────┴─────────────────┘ │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                        ↓
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                Core Layer                            │
│  ┌──────────────┬───────────────┬─────────────────┐ │
│  │  multinet    │  Parsers      │  Converters     │ │
│  │  (MultiLayer │               │                 │ │
│  │   Network)   │               │                 │ │
│  └──────────────┴───────────────┴─────────────────┘ │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                        ↓
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│           NetworkX Foundation                        │
│  MultiDiGraph, MultiGraph, Algorithms                │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Encoding Scheme:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Nodes are encoded as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"\{node\_id\}\{delimiter\}\{layer\_id\}"}}

\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxAtStartPar
This allows NetworkX to handle multilayer structure transparently.

\subsubsection{Coding Standards}
\label{\detokenize{dev/contributing:coding-standards}}

\paragraph{Code Style}
\label{\detokenize{dev/contributing:code-style}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
We follow PEP 8 with these specifics:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Line length: 100 characters (not 80)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Indentation: 4 spaces (no tabs)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
String quotes: Single quotes preferred (‘text’ not “text”)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Imports: Grouped and sorted (using isort)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Auto\sphinxhyphen{}format your code:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
make\PYG{+w}{ }format
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This runs:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{isort}} \sphinxhyphen{} Sort and organize imports

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{black}} \sphinxhyphen{} Format code consistently

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ruff \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}fix}} \sphinxhyphen{} Auto\sphinxhyphen{}fix linting issues

\end{itemize}


\paragraph{Naming Conventions}
\label{\detokenize{dev/contributing:naming-conventions}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Functions/variables: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{snake\_case}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Classes: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PascalCase}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Constants: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{UPPER\_SNAKE\_CASE}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Private members: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\_leading\_underscore}}

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Good}
\PYG{k}{def}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{compute\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{node\PYGZus{}id}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}

    \PYG{n}{centrality\PYGZus{}scores} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}
    \PYG{k}{return} \PYG{n}{centrality\PYGZus{}scores}

\PYG{k}{class}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nc}{MultilayerNetwork}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{k}{def}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf+fm}{\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}init\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n+nb+bp}{self}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use pytest for testing:

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} tests/test\PYGZus{}my\PYGZus{}feature.py}
\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{pytest}

\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{algorithms}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{statistics}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{multilayer\PYGZus{}statistics} \PYG{k}{as} \PYG{n}{mls}

\PYG{k}{def}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{test\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}density}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{l+s+sd}{\PYGZdq{}\PYGZdq{}\PYGZdq{}Test layer density calculation.\PYGZdq{}\PYGZdq{}\PYGZdq{}}
    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Setup}
    \PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}edges}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}
        \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{A}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{L1}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{B}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{L1}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
        \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{B}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{L1}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{C}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{L1}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{list}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Execute}
    \PYG{n}{density} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{mls}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{layer\PYGZus{}density}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{L1}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Assert}
    \PYG{k}{assert} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0} \PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{density} \PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{=} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}
    \PYG{k}{assert} \PYG{n}{density} \PYG{o}{==} \PYG{n}{pytest}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{approx}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.333}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n+nb}{abs}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.01}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{k}{def}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{test\PYGZus{}invalid\PYGZus{}layer}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{l+s+sd}{\PYGZdq{}\PYGZdq{}\PYGZdq{}Test error handling for invalid layer.\PYGZdq{}\PYGZdq{}\PYGZdq{}}
    \PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

    \PYG{k}{with} \PYG{n}{pytest}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{raises}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n+ne}{ValueError}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
        \PYG{n}{mls}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{layer\PYGZus{}density}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{nonexistent}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

Bases: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{object}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Main class for multilayer network analysis and manipulation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This class provides a comprehensive toolkit for creating, analyzing, and
visualizing multilayer networks where nodes can exist in multiple layers
and edges can connect nodes within or across layers.
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Supported Network Types (network\_type parameter):}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{multilayer} (default): General multilayer networks with arbitrary
layer structure. Each layer can have a different set of nodes.
Suitable for heterogeneous networks (e.g., authors\sphinxhyphen{}papers\sphinxhyphen{}venues)
or networks where nodes naturally appear in only some layers.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{multiplex}: Special case where all layers share the same node set
but with different edge types. After loading a network, automatic
coupling edges are created between each node and its counterparts
in other layers. Suitable for social networks with multiple
relationship types (e.g., friend, colleague, family layers).

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Choosing the Right Network Type:}
\sphinxlineitem{Key Features:}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Dict\sphinxhyphen{}based API for adding nodes and edges (see add\_nodes() and add\_edges())

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
NetworkX interoperability via to\_networkx() and from\_networkx()

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Multiple I/O formats (edgelist, GML, GraphML, gpickle, etc.)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Visualization methods for multilayer layouts

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Community detection and centrality analysis

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Random walk and embedding generation

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Hypergraph Support:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This class does NOT natively support true hypergraphs (edges connecting
more than two nodes). For hypergraph\sphinxhyphen{}like structures, consider:
\sphinxhyphen{} Using bipartite projections (nodes and hyperedges as separate node types)
\sphinxhyphen{} The incidence gadget encoding via to\_homogeneous\_hypergraph()
\sphinxhyphen{} External hypergraph libraries with conversion utilities

\end{description}
\subsubsection*{Notes}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Nodes in multilayer networks are represented as (node\_id, layer) tuples

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use add\_nodes() and add\_edges() with dict format for easiest interaction

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
See examples/ directory for usage patterns and best practices

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Add edges to the multilayer network.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This method supports multiple input formats for specifying edges between nodes
in different layers. The most common format is dict\sphinxhyphen{}based.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{edge\_dict\_list}} \textendash{} Edge data in one of the supported formats (see below)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{input\_type}} \textendash{} Format of edge data (‘dict’, ‘list’, or ‘px\_edge’)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns self for method chaining

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
self

\end{description}\end{quote}
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Supported Formats:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Dict format (recommended):}
{\color{red}\bfseries{}\textasciigrave{}\textasciigrave{}}{\color{red}\bfseries{}\textasciigrave{}}python
\{
\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
‘source’: ‘node1’,          \# Source node ID
‘target’: ‘node2’,          \# Target node ID
‘source\_type’: ‘layer1’,    \# Source layer name
‘target\_type’: ‘layer2’,    \# Target layer name (can be same as source)
‘weight’: 1.0,              \# Optional: edge weight
‘type’: ‘interaction’       \# Optional: edge type/label
\end{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{List format:}
\sphinxtitleref{{[}node1, layer1, node2, layer2{]}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{px\_edge format:}
\sphinxtitleref{((node1, layer1), (node2, layer2), \{‘weight’: 1.0\})}

\end{description}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Add nodes to the multilayer network.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Nodes in a multilayer network are identified by both their ID and the layer
they belong to. This method adds nodes using a dict\sphinxhyphen{}based format.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{node\_dict\_list}} \textendash{} Node data as a dict or list of dicts (see format below)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{input\_type}} \textendash{} Format of node data (currently only ‘dict’ is supported)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns self for method chaining

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
self

\end{description}\end{quote}
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Dict Format:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\color{red}\bfseries{}\textasciigrave{}\textasciigrave{}}{\color{red}\bfseries{}\textasciigrave{}}python
\{
\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
‘source’: ‘node\_id’,    \# Node identifier (can be string or number)
‘type’: ‘layer\_name’,   \# Layer this node belongs to

\# … any other node attributes

\end{description}

\subsubsection*{Notes}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The same node ID can exist in multiple layers

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Each (node\_id, layer) combination is treated as a unique node

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Additional attributes beyond ‘source’ and ‘type’ are preserved

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Nodes must be added before edges referencing them

\end{itemize}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

{{ $\rightarrow$ Dict\DUrole{p}{{[}}str\DUrole{p}{,}\DUrole{w}{ }Any\DUrole{p}{{]}}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute Ollivier\sphinxhyphen{}Ricci curvature on the multilayer network.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This method provides flexible computation of Ollivier\sphinxhyphen{}Ricci curvature
at different levels of the multilayer network:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{core mode}: Compute curvature on the aggregated (flattened) network

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{layers mode}: Compute curvature separately for each layer

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{supra mode}: Compute curvature on the full supra\sphinxhyphen{}graph including
both intra\sphinxhyphen{}layer and inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer edges

\end{itemize}
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{mode}} \textendash{} Scope of computation. Options: “core”, “layers”, “supra”.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{layers}} \textendash{} List of layer identifiers to process (only for mode=”layers”).
If None, all layers are processed.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{alpha}} \textendash{} Ollivier\sphinxhyphen{}Ricci parameter in {[}0, 1{]} controlling the mass
distribution. Default: 0.5.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{weight\_attr}} \textendash{} Name of edge attribute containing weights. Default: “weight”.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{curvature\_attr}} \textendash{} Name of edge attribute to store curvature values.
Default: “ricciCurvature”.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{verbose}} \textendash{} Verbosity level. Options: “INFO”, “DEBUG”, “ERROR”. Default: “ERROR”.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{backend\_kwargs}} \textendash{} Additional keyword arguments for OllivierRicci constructor.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{inplace}} \textendash{} If True, update internal graphs. If False, return new graphs
without modifying the network. Default: True.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{interlayer\_weight}} \textendash{} Weight for inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer coupling edges (only for
mode=”supra”). Default: 1.0.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Dictionary mapping scope identifiers to NetworkX graphs with computed
curvatures:
\sphinxhyphen{} mode=”core”: \{“core”: graph\_with\_curvature\}
\sphinxhyphen{} mode=”layers”: \{layer\_id: graph\_with\_curvature, …\}
\sphinxhyphen{} mode=”supra”: \{“supra”: supra\_graph\_with\_curvature\}

\sphinxlineitem{Raises}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{RicciBackendNotAvailable}} \textendash{} If GraphRicciCurvature is not installed.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{ValueError}} \textendash{} If mode is invalid or layers contains invalid identifiers.

\end{itemize}

\end{description}\end{quote}

\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute Ollivier\sphinxhyphen{}Ricci flow on the multilayer network.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Ricci flow iteratively adjusts edge weights based on their Ricci curvature,
effectively revealing and enhancing community structure. After Ricci flow,
edges with negative curvature (community boundaries) have reduced weights,
while edges with positive curvature have increased weights.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{mode}} \textendash{} Scope of computation. Options: “core”, “layers”, “supra”.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{layers}} \textendash{} List of layer identifiers to process (only for mode=”layers”).
If None, all layers are processed.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{alpha}} \textendash{} Ollivier\sphinxhyphen{}Ricci parameter in {[}0, 1{]}. Default: 0.5.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{iterations}} \textendash{} Number of Ricci flow iterations. Default: 10.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{method}} \textendash{} Ricci flow method. Options: “OTD” (Optimal Transport Distance,
recommended), “ATD” (Average Transport Distance). Default: “OTD”.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{weight\_attr}} \textendash{} Name of edge attribute containing weights. After Ricci flow,
these weights are updated to reflect the flow metric.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{curvature\_attr}} \textendash{} Name of edge attribute for curvature values.
Default: “ricciCurvature”.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{verbose}} \textendash{} Verbosity level. Options: “INFO”, “DEBUG”, “ERROR”. Default: “ERROR”.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{backend\_kwargs}} \textendash{} Additional keyword arguments for OllivierRicci constructor.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{inplace}} \textendash{} If True, update internal graphs. If False, return new graphs.
Default: True.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{interlayer\_weight}} \textendash{} Weight for inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer coupling edges (only for
mode=”supra”). Default: 1.0.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Dictionary mapping scope identifiers to NetworkX graphs with Ricci flow
applied:
\sphinxhyphen{} mode=”core”: \{“core”: graph\_with\_flow\}
\sphinxhyphen{} mode=”layers”: \{layer\_id: graph\_with\_flow, …\}
\sphinxhyphen{} mode=”supra”: \{“supra”: supra\_graph\_with\_flow\}

\sphinxlineitem{Raises}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{RicciBackendNotAvailable}} \textendash{} If GraphRicciCurvature is not installed.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{ValueError}} \textendash{} If mode is invalid or layers contains invalid identifiers.

\end{itemize}

\end{description}\end{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Convert a temporal edge DataFrame to edge tuple list.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Extracts edges from a pandas DataFrame with temporal/activity information
and converts them to a list of edge tuples suitable for network construction.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{edge\_df}} \textendash{} pandas DataFrame with columns:
\sphinxhyphen{} node\_first: Source node identifier
\sphinxhyphen{} node\_second: Target node identifier
\sphinxhyphen{} layer\_name: Layer identifier

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{List of edge tuples in format:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
(node\_first, node\_second, layer\_first, layer\_second, weight)
where weight is always 1

\end{description}


\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
list

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Notes}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
All values are converted to strings

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
All edges are assigned weight=1

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Both source and target are assumed to be in the same layer

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Execute a DSL query on this multilayer network.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is a convenience method that provides first\sphinxhyphen{}class access to the
py3plex DSL (Domain\sphinxhyphen{}Specific Language) for querying multilayer networks.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Supports both SELECT and MATCH queries:
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{SELECT queries:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
net.execute\_query(‘SELECT nodes WHERE layer=”transport”’)
net.execute\_query(‘SELECT * FROM nodes IN LAYER “ppi” WHERE degree \textgreater{} 10’)

\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxAtStartPar
Fill temporary layer graphs with edges from a DataFrame.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Populates the emptied layer graphs (created by remove\_layer\_edges) with
edges from a temporal/activity DataFrame. Useful for temporal network
analysis where edge sets change over time.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{edge\_df}} \textendash{} pandas DataFrame with columns:
\sphinxhyphen{} node\_first: Source node identifier
\sphinxhyphen{} node\_second: Target node identifier
\sphinxhyphen{} layer\_name: Layer identifier

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Notes}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Requires remove\_layer\_edges() to be called first

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Edges are grouped by layer

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Modifies self.tmp\_layers in place

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Each edge is stored as ((node\_first, layer), (node\_second, layer))

\end{itemize}
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Raises}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{AttributeError}} \textendash{} If self.tmp\_layers doesn’t exist (call remove\_layer\_edges first)

the original layers based on cycle lengths (prime numbers).

Create a multi\_layer\_network from a NetworkX graph.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This class method converts a NetworkX graph into a py3plex multi\_layer\_network.
For multilayer networks, nodes should be tuples of (node\_id, layer).

\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{network\_type}} \textendash{} Type of network (‘multilayer’ or ‘multiplex’)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{directed}} \textendash{} Whether to treat the network as directed. If None, inferred from G.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A new multi\_layer\_network instance

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.core.multinet.multi_layer_network}]{\sphinxcrossref{multi\_layer\_network}}}

\index{get\_edges() (py3plex.core.multinet.multi\_layer\_network method)@\spxentry{get\_edges()}\spxextra{py3plex.core.multinet.multi\_layer\_network method}}

\begin{savenotes}\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.core.multinet.multi_layer_network.get_edges}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret
{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{get\_edges}}}
{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{data}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{bool}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{False}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{multiplex\_edges}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{bool}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{False}}}
{{ $\rightarrow$ Any}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Iterate over edges in the network.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This method behaves differently based on the network\_type:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{multilayer}: Returns all edges without filtering.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{multiplex}: By default, filters out coupling edges (auto\sphinxhyphen{}generated
inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer edges connecting each node to itself in other layers).
Set multiplex\_edges=True to include coupling edges.

\end{itemize}
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{data}} \textendash{} If True, return edge data along with edge tuples

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{multiplex\_edges}} \textendash{} If True, include coupling edges in multiplex networks.
Only relevant when network\_type=’multiplex’. Coupling edges are
automatically added to connect each node to its counterparts
in other layers.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Yields}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Edge tuples, optionally with data. For multiplex networks with
multiplex\_edges=False, coupling edges are excluded.

\sphinxlineitem{Raises}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{ValueError}} \textendash{} If network\_type is not ‘multilayer’ or ‘multiplex’.

\end{description}\end{quote}

\index{load\_network() (py3plex.core.multinet.multi\_layer\_network method)@\spxentry{load\_network()}\spxextra{py3plex.core.multinet.multi\_layer\_network method}}

\begin{savenotes}\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.core.multinet.multi_layer_network.load_network}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret
{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_network}}}
{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{input\_file}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{str\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{p}{|}\DUrole{w}{ }None}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{None}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{directed}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{bool}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{False}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{input\_type}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{str}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{\textquotesingle{}gml\textquotesingle{}}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{label\_delimiter}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{str}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{\textquotesingle{}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}\textquotesingle{}}}}
{{ $\rightarrow$ {\hyperref[\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.core.multinet.multi_layer_network}]{\sphinxcrossref{multi\_layer\_network}}}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Load a network from file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This method loads and prepares a given network. The behavior depends on
the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{network\_type}} set during initialization:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{multilayer}: Network is loaded as\sphinxhyphen{}is. No automatic edges are added.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{multiplex}: After loading, coupling edges are automatically created
between each node and its counterparts in other layers. These edges
have type=’coupling’ and can be filtered via get\_edges().

\end{itemize}
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{input\_file}} \textendash{} Path to the network file to load

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{directed}} \textendash{} Whether the network is directed

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{input\_type}} \textendash{} Format of the input file. Supported values:
\sphinxhyphen{} ‘gml’: Graph Modeling Language format
\sphinxhyphen{} ‘graphml’: GraphML XML format
\sphinxhyphen{} ‘edgelist’: Simple edge list (source target {[}weight{]})
\sphinxhyphen{} ‘multiedgelist’: Multilayer edge list (node1 layer1 node2 layer2 weight)
\sphinxhyphen{} ‘multiplex\_edges’: Multiplex format (layer node1 node2 weight)
\sphinxhyphen{} ‘multiplex\_folder’: Folder with layer files
\sphinxhyphen{} ‘gpickle’: Python pickle format
\sphinxhyphen{} ‘nx’: NetworkX graph object
\sphinxhyphen{} ‘sparse’: Sparse matrix format

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{label\_delimiter}} \textendash{} Delimiter used to separate layer names in node labels

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self for method chaining. Populates self.core\_network, self.labels,
and self.activity.

\end{description}\end{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For multiplex networks, use input\_type=’multiplex\_edges’ or
‘multiplex\_folder’ with network\_type=’multiplex’ to get automatic
coupling edges.
\end{sphinxadmonition}
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Load multilayer network (no automatic coupling)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{net} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{multilayer}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{net}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{load\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{data.gml}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{gml}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}  
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Load multiplex network (automatic coupling edges)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{net} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{multiplex}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{net}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{load\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{data.edges}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{multiplex\PYGZus{}edges}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}  
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Remove all edges from separate layer graphs while keeping nodes.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This method creates empty copies of each layer graph with all nodes intact
but no edges. Useful for reconstructing networks with different edge sets
or for temporal network analysis.
\subsubsection*{Notes}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Requires split\_to\_layers() to be called first

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Stores empty layer graphs in self.tmp\_layers

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Original graphs in self.separate\_layers remain unchanged

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
All nodes and their attributes are preserved

\end{itemize}
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Raises}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{RuntimeError}} \textendash{} If split\_to\_layers() hasn’t been called yet

\end{description}\end{quote}


\begin{sphinxseealso}{See also:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
split\_to\_layers: Must be called before this method
fill\_tmp\_with\_edges: Add edges back to emptied layers


\end{sphinxseealso}


\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Save the network to a file in various formats.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This method exports the multilayer network to different file formats
for persistence, sharing, or use with other tools.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{output\_file}} \textendash{} Path where the network should be saved

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{output\_type}} \textendash{} Format for saving (‘edgelist’, ‘multiedgelist’,
‘multiedgelist\_encoded’, or ‘gpickle’)

\end{itemize}

\end{description}\end{quote}
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Supported Formats:}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
‘edgelist’: Simple edge list format (standard NetworkX)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
‘multiedgelist’: Multilayer edge list with layer information

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
‘multiedgelist\_encoded’: Multilayer edge list with integer encoding

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
‘gpickle’: Python pickle format (preserves all attributes)

\end{itemize}

\end{description}
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{net} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{net}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{source}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{A}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{type}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{layer1}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{net}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}edges}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{source}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{A}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{target}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{B}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{g+gp}{... }                \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{source\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{layer1}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{target\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{layer1}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{net}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{save\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{network.txt}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{output\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{multiedgelist}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} For faster I/O with all metadata preserved}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{net}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{save\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{network.gpickle}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{output\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{gpickle}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\subsubsection*{Notes}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
‘gpickle’ format preserves all node/edge attributes

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
‘multiedgelist\_encoded’ creates node\_map and layer\_map attributes

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Edge weights and types are preserved in supported formats

\end{itemize}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\index{serialize\_to\_edgelist() (py3plex.core.multinet.multi\_layer\_network method)@\spxentry{serialize\_to\_edgelist()}\spxextra{py3plex.core.multinet.multi\_layer\_network method}}

\begin{savenotes}\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.core.multinet.multi_layer_network.serialize_to_edgelist}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret
{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{serialize\_to\_edgelist}}}
{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{edgelist\_file}\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{default_value}{\textquotesingle{}./tmp/tmpedgelist.txt\textquotesingle{}}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{tmp\_folder}\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{default_value}{\textquotesingle{}tmp\textquotesingle{}}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{out\_folder}\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{default_value}{\textquotesingle{}out\textquotesingle{}}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{multiplex}\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{default_value}{False}}}
{}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Serialize the multilayer network to an edgelist file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Converts the network to a numeric edgelist format suitable for external tools
and algorithms that require integer node/layer identifiers.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{edgelist\_file}} \textendash{} Path to output edgelist file (default: “./tmp/tmpedgelist.txt”)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{tmp\_folder}} \textendash{} Temporary folder for intermediate files (default: “tmp”)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{out\_folder}} \textendash{} Output folder for results (default: “out”)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{multiplex}} \textendash{} If True, use multiplex format (node layer node layer weight)
If False, use simple edgelist format (node1 node2 weight)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Inverse node mapping (numeric\_id \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} original\_node\_tuple)}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use this to decode results from external algorithms

\end{description}


\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
dict

\end{description}\end{quote}
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{File Formats:}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Multiplex format: node1\_id layer1\_id node2\_id layer2\_id weight

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Simple format: node1\_id node2\_id weight

\end{itemize}

\end{description}
\subsubsection*{Notes}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Creates tmp\_folder and out\_folder if they don’t exist

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Nodes are mapped to sequential integers starting from 0

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Layers are mapped to sequential integers starting from 0 (multiplex mode)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
All edges have weight 1 unless explicitly specified

\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example requires file output \sphinxhyphen{} for illustration only.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{net} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}  
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} ... build network ...}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{node\PYGZus{}mapping} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{net}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{serialize\PYGZus{}to\PYGZus{}edgelist}\PYG{p}{(}  
\PYG{g+gp}{... }    \PYG{n}{edgelist\PYGZus{}file}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{network.txt}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{g+gp}{... }    \PYG{n}{multiplex}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{True}
\PYG{g+gp}{... }\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Use node\PYGZus{}mapping to decode results}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{original\PYGZus{}node} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{node\PYGZus{}mapping}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{]}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Get original node for id 0  }

\begin{savenotes}\begin{fulllineitems}
