pₙ = proportion of inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer edges incident to node n
Total over all nodes connecting the two layers

\end{description}
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{network}} \textendash{} py3plex multi\_layer\_network object

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{layer\_i}} \textendash{} First layer identifier

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{layer\_j}} \textendash{} Second layer identifier

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Entropy value in bits

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{entropy} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{inter\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}dependence\PYGZus{}entropy}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{L1}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{L2}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Inter\PYGZhy{}layer dependence entropy: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{entropy}\PYG{l+s+si}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{.3f}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Reference:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
De Domenico et al. (2015), “Ranking in interconnected multilayer networks”

\index{interdependence() (in module py3plex.algorithms.statistics.multilayer\_statistics)@\spxentry{interdependence()}\spxextra{in module py3plex.algorithms.statistics.multilayer\_statistics}}

\begin{savenotes}\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.algorithms.statistics.multilayer_statistics.interdependence}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret
{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{py3plex.algorithms.statistics.multilayer\_statistics.}}\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{interdependence}}}
{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{network}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{Any}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{sample\_size}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{int}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{100}}}
{{ $\rightarrow$ float}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Calculate interdependence (λ).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Formula: λ = ⟨dᴹᴸ⟩ / ⟨dᵃᵛᵍ⟩

\sphinxAtStartPar
Quantifies how much shortest\sphinxhyphen{}path communication depends on inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer connections.
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Variables:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
dᵢⱼᴹᴸ = shortest path from node i to node j in the full multilayer network
dᵢⱼᵃᵛᵍ = (1/L) Σₐ dᵢⱼᵅ is the average shortest path across individual layers
⟨·⟩ = average over sampled node pairs

\sphinxlineitem{Interpretation:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
λ \textless{} 1: multilayer connectivity reduces path lengths (positive interdependence)
λ ≈ 1: inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer connections provide little benefit
λ \textgreater{} 1: multilayer structure increases path lengths (rare)

\end{description}
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{network}} \textendash{} py3plex multi\_layer\_network object

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{sample\_size}} \textendash{} Number of node pairs to sample for estimation

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Interdependence ratio

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{interdep} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{interdependence}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{sample\PYGZus{}size}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{50}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Reference:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Gomez et al. (2013), Buldyrev et al. (2010)

\end{description}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\index{interlayer\_degree\_correlation\_matrix() (in module py3plex.algorithms.statistics.multilayer\_statistics)@\spxentry{interlayer\_degree\_correlation\_matrix()}\spxextra{in module py3plex.algorithms.statistics.multilayer\_statistics}}

\begin{savenotes}\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.algorithms.statistics.multilayer_statistics.interlayer_degree_correlation_matrix}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret
{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{py3plex.algorithms.statistics.multilayer\_statistics.}}\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{interlayer\_degree\_correlation\_matrix}}}
{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{network}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{Any}}}
{{ $\rightarrow$ Tuple\DUrole{p}{{[}}ndarray\DUrole{p}{,}\DUrole{w}{ }list\DUrole{p}{{]}}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Calculate inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer degree correlation matrix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Computes Pearson correlation coefficients for node degrees between all
pairs of layers, organized as a symmetric correlation matrix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Formula: Matrix{[}α,β{]} = r\textasciicircum{}αβ = corr(k\textasciicircum{}α, k\textasciicircum{}β)

\sphinxAtStartPar
where k\textasciicircum{}α and k\textasciicircum{}β are degree vectors for layers α and β over common nodes.
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Properties:}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Diagonal elements are 1.0 (self\sphinxhyphen{}correlation)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Off\sphinxhyphen{}diagonal elements in {[}\sphinxhyphen{}1, 1{]}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Symmetric matrix

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Positive values indicate positive degree correlation

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Negative values indicate negative degree correlation

\end{itemize}

\end{description}
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{network}} \textendash{} py3plex multi\_layer\_network object

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
correlation\_matrix: 2D numpy array of shape (num\_layers, num\_layers)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
layer\_labels: List of layer names corresponding to matrix indices

\sphinxAtStartPar
Calculate entropy of layer connectivity (H\_connectivity).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Formula: H\_c = \sphinxhyphen{}Σᵢ (kᵢ/Σⱼkⱼ) log\(\sb{\text{2}}\)(kᵢ/Σⱼkⱼ)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Shannon entropy of degree distribution within a layer; measures
heterogeneity of node connectivity patterns.
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Variables:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
kᵢ = degree of node i in the layer
Σⱼkⱼ = sum of all degrees (2 * edges for undirected)

\sphinxlineitem{Properties:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
H\_c = 0 when all nodes have the same degree (uniform distribution)
H\_c is maximized when degree distribution is highly uneven

\end{description}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{network}} \textendash{} py3plex multi\_layer\_network object

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{layer}} \textendash{} Layer identifier

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Entropy value in bits

{{ $\rightarrow$ float}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Calculate layer influence centrality (Iᵅ).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Formula (coupling): Iᵅ = Σᵦ≠ᵅ C\textasciicircum{}αβ / (L\sphinxhyphen{}1)
Formula (flow): Iᵅ = Σᵦ≠ᵅ F\textasciicircum{}αβ / (L\sphinxhyphen{}1)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Quantifies how much a layer influences other layers through inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer
connections (coupling method) or information flow (flow method).
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Variables:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
C\textasciicircum{}αβ = inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer coupling strength between layers α and β
F\textasciicircum{}αβ = flow from layer α to layer β (random walk transition probability)
L = total number of layers

\sphinxlineitem{Properties:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Higher values indicate layers that strongly influence others
Useful for identifying critical layers in the multilayer structure

\end{description}
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{network}} \textendash{} py3plex multi\_layer\_network object

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{layer}} \textendash{} Layer identifier

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{method}} \textendash{} ‘coupling’ for structural influence, ‘flow’ for dynamic influence

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{sample\_size}} \textendash{} Number of random walk steps for flow simulation

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Influence centrality value

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{influence} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{layer\PYGZus{}influence\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{L1}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{method}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{coupling}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Reference:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Cozzo et al. (2013), “Mathematical formulation of multilayer networks”
De Domenico et al. (2014), “Identifying modular flows”

{{ $\rightarrow$ float}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Calculate layer redundancy coefficient.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Measures the proportion of edges in one layer that are redundant
(also present) in another layer. Values close to 1 indicate high
redundancy, while values close to 0 indicate complementary layers.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Formula: Rᵅᵝ = {\color{red}\bfseries{}|Eᵅ ∩ Eᵝ|} / {\color{red}\bfseries{}|Eᵅ|}

\sphinxAtStartPar
where Eᵅ and Eᵝ are edge sets of layers α and β.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{network}} \textendash{} py3plex multi\_layer\_network object

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{layer\_i}} \textendash{} First layer identifier

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{layer\_j}} \textendash{} Second layer identifier

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Redundancy coefficient between 0 and 1

\end{description}\end{quote}

\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Redundancy: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{redundancy}\PYG{l+s+si}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{.2\PYGZpc{}}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

{{ $\rightarrow$ float}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Calculate layer similarity (S\textasciicircum{}αβ).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Formula: S\textasciicircum{}αβ = ⟨Aₐ, Aᵦ⟩ / (‖Aₐ‖ ‖Aᵦ‖) = Σᵢⱼ AᵢⱼᵅAᵢⱼᵝ / √(Σᵢⱼ(Aᵢⱼᵅ)\(\sp{\text{2}}\)) √(Σᵢⱼ(Aᵢⱼᵝ)\(\sp{\text{2}}\))

\sphinxAtStartPar
Cosine or Jaccard similarity between adjacency matrices of two layers.
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Variables:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Aₐ, Aᵦ = adjacency matrices for layers α and β
⟨·,·⟩ = Frobenius inner product
‖·‖ = Frobenius norm

\end{description}
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{network}} \textendash{} py3plex multi\_layer\_network object

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{layer\_i}} \textendash{} First layer identifier (α)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{layer\_j}} \textendash{} Second layer identifier (β)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{method}} \textendash{} ‘cosine’ or ‘jaccard’

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Similarity value between 0 and 1

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Calculate multilayer betweenness surface (tensor representation).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Computes betweenness centrality for each node\sphinxhyphen{}layer pair and organizes
the results as a 2D array (nodes × layers) that can be visualized as
a heatmap or surface plot.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Formula: Surface{[}i,α{]} = Bᵢᵅ

\sphinxAtStartPar
where Bᵢᵅ is the betweenness centrality of node i in layer α.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{normalized}} \textendash{} Whether to normalize betweenness values

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{weight}} \textendash{} Edge weight attribute name (None for unweighted)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
2D numpy array of shape (num\_nodes, num\_layers) containing betweenness values.
Also returns tuple of (node\_labels, layer\_labels) for axis labeling.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Calculate multilayer clustering coefficient (Cᴹ).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Formula: Cᵢᴹ = Tᵢ / Tᵢᵐᵃˣ

\sphinxAtStartPar
Extends transitivity to account for triangles that span multiple layers.
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Variables:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Tᵢ = number of closed triplets (triangles) involving node i across all layers
Tᵢᵐᵃˣ = maximum possible triplets = Σₐ kᵢᵅ(kᵢᵅ \sphinxhyphen{} 1)/2 for undirected networks
Average over all nodes: Cᴹ = (1/N) Σᵢ Cᵢᴹ

\end{description}
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{network}} \textendash{} py3plex multi\_layer\_network object

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{node}} \textendash{} If specified, compute for single node; otherwise compute for all

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Clustering coefficient value or dict of values per node

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{clustering} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multilayer\PYGZus{}clustering\PYGZus{}coefficient}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{node\PYGZus{}clustering} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multilayer\PYGZus{}clustering\PYGZus{}coefficient}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{node}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{A}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

{{ $\rightarrow$ float}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Calculate multilayer modularity (Qᴹᴸ).

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is a wrapper for the existing multilayer\_modularity implementation
in py3plex.algorithms.community\_detection.multilayer\_modularity.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Formula: Qᴹᴸ = (1/2μ) Σᵢⱼₐᵦ {[}(Aᵢⱼᵅ \sphinxhyphen{} γₐPᵢⱼᵅ)δₐᵦ + ωₐᵦδᵢⱼ{]} δ(gᵢᵅ, gⱼᵝ)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Extension of Newman\sphinxhyphen{}Girvan modularity to multiplex networks (Mucha et al., 2010).
Measures community quality across layers.
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Variables:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
μ = total edge weight in supra\sphinxhyphen{}network
Aᵢⱼᵅ = adjacency matrix element for layer α
Pᵢⱼᵅ = kᵢᵅkⱼᵅ/(2mₐ) is the null model (configuration model)
γₐ = resolution parameter for layer α
ωₐᵦ = inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer coupling strength
δₐᵦ = Kronecker delta (1 if α=β, 0 otherwise)
δᵢⱼ = Kronecker delta (1 if i=j, 0 otherwise)
δ(gᵢᵅ, gⱼᵝ) = 1 if node i in layer α and node j in layer β are in same community

\end{description}
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{network}} \textendash{} py3plex multi\_layer\_network object

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{communities}} \textendash{} Dictionary mapping (node, layer) tuples to community IDs

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{gamma}} \textendash{} Resolution parameter(s)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{omega}} \textendash{} Inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer coupling strength

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{weight}} \textendash{} Edge weight attribute

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Modularity value Q

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{communities} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{A}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{L1}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{B}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{L1}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{C}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{L1}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{Q} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multilayer\PYGZus{}modularity}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{communities}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Reference:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Mucha et al. (2010), Science 328(5980), 876\sphinxhyphen{}878

\end{description}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Calculate multiplex betweenness centrality.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Computes betweenness centrality on the supra\sphinxhyphen{}graph, accounting for paths
that traverse inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer couplings. This extends the standard betweenness
definition to multiplex networks where paths can cross layers.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Formula: Bᵢᵅ = Σₛ≠ᵢ≠ₜ (σₛₜ(iα) / σₛₜ)

\sphinxAtStartPar
where σₛₜ is the total number of shortest paths from s to t, and
σₛₜ(iα) is the number of those paths passing through node i in layer α.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{network}} \textendash{} py3plex multi\_layer\_network object

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{normalized}} \textendash{} Whether to normalize by the number of node pairs

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{weight}} \textendash{} Edge weight attribute name (None for unweighted)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Dictionary mapping (node, layer) tuples to betweenness centrality values

\index{multiplex\_closeness\_centrality() (in module py3plex.algorithms.statistics.multilayer\_statistics)@\spxentry{multiplex\_closeness\_centrality()}\spxextra{in module py3plex.algorithms.statistics.multilayer\_statistics}}

\begin{savenotes}\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.algorithms.statistics.multilayer_statistics.multiplex_closeness_centrality}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret
{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{py3plex.algorithms.statistics.multilayer\_statistics.}}\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{multiplex\_closeness\_centrality}}}
{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{network}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{Any}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{normalized}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{bool}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{True}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{weight}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{str\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{p}{|}\DUrole{w}{ }None}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{None}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{variant}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{str}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{\textquotesingle{}standard\textquotesingle{}}}}
{{ $\rightarrow$ Dict\DUrole{p}{{[}}Tuple\DUrole{p}{{[}}Any\DUrole{p}{,}\DUrole{w}{ }Any\DUrole{p}{{]}}\DUrole{p}{,}\DUrole{w}{ }float\DUrole{p}{{]}}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Calculate multiplex closeness centrality.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Computes closeness centrality on the supra\sphinxhyphen{}graph, where shortest paths
can traverse inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer edges. This captures how quickly a node\sphinxhyphen{}layer
can reach all other node\sphinxhyphen{}layers in the multiplex network.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Standard closeness formula: Cᵢᵅ = (N*L \sphinxhyphen{} 1) / Σⱼᵝ≠ᵢᵅ d(iα, jβ)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Harmonic closeness formula: HCᵢᵅ = Σⱼᵝ≠ᵢᵅ 1/d(iα, jβ)

\sphinxAtStartPar
where d(iα, jβ) is the shortest path distance from node i in layer α
to node j in layer β, and N*L is the total number of node\sphinxhyphen{}layer pairs.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{network}} \textendash{} py3plex multi\_layer\_network object

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{normalized}} \textendash{} Whether to normalize by network size

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{weight}} \textendash{} Edge weight attribute name (None for unweighted)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{variant}} \textendash{} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Closeness variant to use. Options:
\sphinxhyphen{} ‘standard’: Classic closeness (reciprocal of sum of distances).
\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Can produce biased values for nodes in disconnected components.
\end{quote}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
’harmonic’: Harmonic closeness (sum of reciprocal distances).
Recommended for disconnected multilayer networks.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
’auto’: Automatically selects ‘harmonic’ if the network has
multiple connected components, otherwise uses ‘standard’.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Default is ‘standard’ for backward compatibility.


\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Dictionary mapping (node, layer) tuples to closeness centrality values

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{closeness} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multiplex\PYGZus{}closeness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{central\PYGZus{}nodes} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{k}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{v} \PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{k}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{v} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{closeness}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{items}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{k}{if} \PYG{n}{v} \PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}} \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.5}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} For disconnected networks, use harmonic variant}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{closeness} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multiplex\PYGZus{}closeness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{variant}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{harmonic}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Reference:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
De Domenico et al. (2015), “Structural reducibility of multilayer networks”
Boldi, P., \& Vigna, S. (2014). Axioms for Centrality. Internet Math.

\end{description}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\index{multiplex\_rich\_club\_coefficient() (in module py3plex.algorithms.statistics.multilayer\_statistics)@\spxentry{multiplex\_rich\_club\_coefficient()}\spxextra{in module py3plex.algorithms.statistics.multilayer\_statistics}}

\begin{savenotes}\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.algorithms.statistics.multilayer_statistics.multiplex_rich_club_coefficient}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret
{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{py3plex.algorithms.statistics.multilayer\_statistics.}}\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{multiplex\_rich\_club\_coefficient}}}
{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{network}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{Any}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{k}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{int}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{normalized}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{bool}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{True}}}
{{ $\rightarrow$ float}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Calculate multiplex rich\sphinxhyphen{}club coefficient.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Measures the tendency of high\sphinxhyphen{}degree nodes to be more densely connected
to each other than expected by chance, accounting for the multiplex structure.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Formula: φᴹ(k) = Eᴹ(\textgreater{}k) / (Nᴹ(\textgreater{}k) * (Nᴹ(\textgreater{}k)\sphinxhyphen{}1) / 2)

\sphinxAtStartPar
where Eᴹ(\textgreater{}k) is the number of edges among nodes with overlapping degree \textgreater{} k,
and Nᴹ(\textgreater{}k) is the number of such nodes.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{network}} \textendash{} py3plex multi\_layer\_network object

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{k}} \textendash{} Degree threshold

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{normalized}} \textendash{} Whether to normalize by random expectation

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Rich\sphinxhyphen{}club coefficient value

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{rich\PYGZus{}club} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multiplex\PYGZus{}rich\PYGZus{}club\PYGZus{}coefficient}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{k}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Rich\PYGZhy{}club coefficient: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{rich\PYGZus{}club}\PYG{l+s+si}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{.3f}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Reference:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Alstott et al. (2014), “powerlaw: A Python Package for Analysis of Heavy\sphinxhyphen{}Tailed Distributions”
Extended to multiplex networks

\end{description}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

Activity value between 0 and 1

\index{resilience() (in module py3plex.algorithms.statistics.multilayer\_statistics)@\spxentry{resilience()}\spxextra{in module py3plex.algorithms.statistics.multilayer\_statistics}}

\begin{savenotes}\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.algorithms.statistics.multilayer_statistics.resilience}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret
{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{py3plex.algorithms.statistics.multilayer\_statistics.}}\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{resilience}}}
{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{network}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{Any}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{perturbation\_type}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{str}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{\textquotesingle{}layer\_removal\textquotesingle{}}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{perturbation\_param}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{str\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{p}{|}\DUrole{w}{ }float\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{p}{|}\DUrole{w}{ }None}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{None}}}
{{ $\rightarrow$ float}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Calculate resilience (R).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Formula: R = S’ / S\(\sb{\text{0}}\)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Ratio of largest connected component after perturbation to original size.
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Variables:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
S\(\sb{\text{0}}\) = size of largest connected component in original network
S’ = size of largest connected component after perturbation

\sphinxlineitem{Perturbation types:}\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Layer removal: Remove all nodes/edges in a specific layer

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Coupling removal: Remove a fraction of inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer edges

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxlineitem{Properties:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
R = 1 indicates full resilience (no impact from perturbation)
R = 0 indicates complete fragmentation
0 \textless{} R \textless{} 1 indicates partial resilience

\end{description}
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{network}} \textendash{} py3plex multi\_layer\_network object

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{perturbation\_type}} \textendash{} ‘layer\_removal’ or ‘coupling\_removal’

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{perturbation\_param}} \textendash{} Layer to remove or fraction of inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer edges

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Resilience ratio between 0 and 1

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{r} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{resilience}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{layer\PYGZus{}removal}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{perturbation\PYGZus{}param}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{L1}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{r} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{resilience}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{coupling\PYGZus{}removal}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{perturbation\PYGZus{}param}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.5}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Reference:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Buldyrev et al. (2010), Nature 464, 1025\sphinxhyphen{}1028

\end{description}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\index{supra\_laplacian\_spectrum() (in module py3plex.algorithms.statistics.multilayer\_statistics)@\spxentry{supra\_laplacian\_spectrum()}\spxextra{in module py3plex.algorithms.statistics.multilayer\_statistics}}

\begin{savenotes}\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.algorithms.statistics.multilayer_statistics.supra_laplacian_spectrum}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret
{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{py3plex.algorithms.statistics.multilayer\_statistics.}}\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{supra\_laplacian\_spectrum}}}
{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{network}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{Any}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{k}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{int}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{10}}}
{{ $\rightarrow$ ndarray}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Calculate supra\sphinxhyphen{}Laplacian spectrum (Λ).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Formula: ℒ = 𝒟 \sphinxhyphen{} 𝒜

\sphinxAtStartPar
Eigenvalue spectrum of the supra\sphinxhyphen{}Laplacian matrix; captures diffusion properties.
Uses sparse eigenvalue computation when beneficial.
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Variables:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
𝒜 = supra\sphinxhyphen{}adjacency matrix (NL × NL block matrix containing all layers and inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer couplings)
𝒟 = supra\sphinxhyphen{}degree matrix (diagonal matrix with row sums of 𝒜)
ℒ = supra\sphinxhyphen{}Laplacian matrix
Λ = \{λ\(\sb{\text{0}}\), λ\(\sb{\text{1}}\), …, λₙₗ₋\(\sb{\text{1}}\)\} with 0 = λ\(\sb{\text{0}}\) ≤ λ\(\sb{\text{1}}\) ≤ … ≤ λₙₗ₋\(\sb{\text{1}}\)

\end{description}
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{network}} \textendash{} py3plex multi\_layer\_network object

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{k}} \textendash{} Number of smallest eigenvalues to compute

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Array of k smallest eigenvalues

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{spectrum} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{supra\PYGZus{}laplacian\PYGZus{}spectrum}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{k}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Reference:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
De Domenico et al. (2013), Gomez et al. (2013)

\end{description}
\subsubsection*{Notes}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Uses sparse eigsh() for sparse matrices (more efficient)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Falls back to dense computation for small matrices (n \textless{} 100) or when k is large relative to n

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Laplacian is always symmetric for undirected graphs (PSD with smallest eigenvalue = 0)

\end{itemize}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\pysigstartsignatures

{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{network}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{Any}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{centrality\_type}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{str}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{\textquotesingle{}degree\textquotesingle{}}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{alpha}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{Dict\DUrole{p}{{[}}str\DUrole{p}{,}\DUrole{w}{ }float\DUrole{p}{{]}}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{p}{|}\DUrole{w}{ }None}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{None}}}
{{ $\rightarrow$ Dict\DUrole{p}{{[}}Any\DUrole{p}{,}\DUrole{w}{ }float\DUrole{p}{{]}}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Calculate versatility centrality (Vᵢ).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Formula: Vᵢ = Σₐ wₐ Cᵢᵅ

\sphinxAtStartPar
Weighted combination of node centrality values across layers; measures overall influence.
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Variables:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
wₐ = weight for layer α (typically 1/L for uniform weighting, Σₐ wₐ = 1)
Cᵢᵅ = centrality of node i in layer α (can be degree, betweenness, closeness, etc.)

\end{description}
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{network}} \textendash{} py3plex multi\_layer\_network object

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{centrality\_type}} \textendash{} Type of centrality (‘degree’, ‘betweenness’, ‘closeness’)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{alpha}} \textendash{} Layer weights (default: uniform weights)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Dictionary mapping nodes to versatility centrality values

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{versatility} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{versatility\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{centrality\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Reference:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
De Domenico et al. (2015), Nature Communications 6, 6868

\end{description}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\paragraph{Multilayer Algorithms}
\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:module-py3plex.algorithms.multilayer_algorithms.centrality}}\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:multilayer-algorithms}}\index{module@\spxentry{module}!py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.centrality@\spxentry{py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.centrality}}\index{py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.centrality@\spxentry{py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.centrality}!module@\spxentry{module}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Multilayer/Multiplex Network Centrality Measures

\sphinxAtStartPar
This module implements various centrality measures for multilayer and multiplex networks,
following standard definitions from multilayer network analysis literature.


\subparagraph{Weight Handling Notes:}
\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:weight-handling-notes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For path\sphinxhyphen{}based centralities (betweenness, closeness):
\sphinxhyphen{} Edge weights from the supra\sphinxhyphen{}adjacency matrix are converted to distances (inverse of weight)
\sphinxhyphen{} NetworkX algorithms use these distances for shortest path computation
\sphinxhyphen{} betweenness\_centrality: weight parameter specifies the edge attribute for path computation
\sphinxhyphen{} closeness\_centrality: distance parameter specifies the edge attribute for path computation

\sphinxAtStartPar
For disconnected graphs:
\sphinxhyphen{} closeness\_centrality uses wf\_improved parameter (Wasserman\sphinxhyphen{}Faust scaling) by default
\sphinxhyphen{} When wf\_improved=True, scores are normalized by reachable nodes only
\sphinxhyphen{} When wf\_improved=False, unreachable nodes contribute infinite distance

\sphinxAtStartPar
Weight Constraints:
\sphinxhyphen{} Weights should be positive (\textgreater{} 0) for shortest path algorithms
\sphinxhyphen{} Zero or negative weights will cause undefined behavior
\sphinxhyphen{} For unweighted analysis, use weighted=False parameters

\sphinxAtStartPar
Authors: py3plex contributors
Date: 2025

Class for computing centrality measures on multilayer networks.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This class provides implementations of various centrality measures
specifically designed for multilayer/multiplex networks, including
degree\sphinxhyphen{}based, eigenvector\sphinxhyphen{}based, and path\sphinxhyphen{}based measures.
\index{accessibility\_centrality() (py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.centrality.MultilayerCentrality method)@\spxentry{accessibility\_centrality()}\spxextra{py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.centrality.MultilayerCentrality method}}

\begin{savenotes}\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.algorithms.multilayer_algorithms.centrality.MultilayerCentrality.accessibility_centrality}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret
{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{accessibility\_centrality}}}
{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{h}\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{default_value}{2}}}
{}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute accessibility centrality (entropy\sphinxhyphen{}based reach within h steps).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Accessibility measures the diversity of nodes reachable within h steps
using entropy of the probability distribution.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Access\_r = exp(H\_r) where H\_r is the entropy of the h\sphinxhyphen{}step distribution
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{h}} \textendash{} Number of steps (default: 2)

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\{(node, layer): accessibility\}

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
dict

\end{description}\end{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Accessibility is measured as the effective number of h\sphinxhyphen{}step destinations,
using the entropy of the random walk distribution.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Dangling Node Handling: For nodes with no outgoing edges (dangling nodes),
this implementation uses uniform teleportation to all nodes. This differs
from the original Travencolo\sphinxhyphen{}Costa definition which does not include
teleportation. The teleportation ensures a well\sphinxhyphen{}defined random walk
distribution but may affect accessibility values for nodes near dangling
nodes compared to implementations that handle dangling nodes differently.
\end{sphinxadmonition}
\subsubsection*{References}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Travencolo, B. A. N., \& Costa, L. D. F. (2008). Accessibility in complex
networks. Physics Letters A, 373(1), 89\sphinxhyphen{}95.

\end{itemize}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\index{bridging\_centrality() (py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.centrality.MultilayerCentrality method)@\spxentry{bridging\_centrality()}\spxextra{py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.centrality.MultilayerCentrality method}}

\begin{savenotes}\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.algorithms.multilayer_algorithms.centrality.MultilayerCentrality.bridging_centrality}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret
{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{bridging\_centrality}}}
{}
{}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute bridging centrality for nodes in the supra\sphinxhyphen{}graph.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Bridging centrality combines betweenness with the bridging coefficient,
which measures how much a node connects sparse regions of the network.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Bridging(u) = B(u) * BCoeff(u)
where BCoeff(u) = (1 / k\_u) * sum\_\{v in N(u)\} {[}1 / k\_v{]}
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\{(node, layer): bridging\_centrality\}

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
dict

\end{description}\end{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Nodes with higher bridging centrality act as important bridges
connecting different parts of the network.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\index{collective\_influence() (py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.centrality.MultilayerCentrality method)@\spxentry{collective\_influence()}\spxextra{py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.centrality.MultilayerCentrality method}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute collective influence (CI\_ℓ) for multiplex networks.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Collective influence identifies influential spreaders by considering
not just immediate neighbors but also nodes at distance ℓ.

\sphinxAtStartPar
CI\_ℓ(u) = (k\_u \sphinxhyphen{} 1) * sum\_\{v in ∂Ball\_ℓ(u)\} (k\_v \sphinxhyphen{} 1)
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{radius}} \textendash{} Radius ℓ for the ball boundary (default: 2)

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\{(node, layer): collective\_influence\}

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
dict

\end{description}\end{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Uses overlapping degree across all layers for each physical node.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\index{communicability\_betweenness\_centrality() (py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.centrality.MultilayerCentrality method)@\spxentry{communicability\_betweenness\_centrality()}\spxextra{py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.centrality.MultilayerCentrality method}}

\begin{savenotes}\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.algorithms.multilayer_algorithms.centrality.MultilayerCentrality.communicability_betweenness_centrality}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret
{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{communicability\_betweenness\_centrality}}}
{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{normalized}\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{default_value}{True}}}
{}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute communicability betweenness centrality on the supra\sphinxhyphen{}graph.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This measure quantifies how much a node contributes to the communicability
between other pairs of nodes. It uses the matrix exponential to account
for all walks between nodes.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{normalized}} \textendash{} If True (default), normalize scores by dividing by the
maximum value (min\sphinxhyphen{}max scaling to {[}0, 1{]} range). Note that
this is simple rescaling, not the theoretical Estrada\sphinxhyphen{}Hatano
normalization from the original literature.

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\{(node, layer): communicability\_betweenness\}

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
dict

\end{description}\end{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This implementation uses NetworkX’s communicability\_betweenness\_centrality,
which operates on unweighted graphs. Edge weights from the supra\sphinxhyphen{}adjacency
matrix are used only to determine edge existence (weight \textgreater{} 0), not for
weighted communicability computation. For truly weighted communicability
analysis, a custom implementation using the weighted matrix exponential
would be required.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is computationally expensive as it requires computing the matrix
exponential multiple times. For large networks, this may take significant time.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\index{flow\_betweenness\_centrality() (py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.centrality.MultilayerCentrality method)@\spxentry{flow\_betweenness\_centrality()}\spxextra{py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.centrality.MultilayerCentrality method}}

\begin{savenotes}\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.algorithms.multilayer_algorithms.centrality.MultilayerCentrality.flow_betweenness_centrality}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret
{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{flow\_betweenness\_centrality}}}
{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{samples}\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{default_value}{100}}}
{}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute flow betweenness based on maximum flow sampling.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Flow betweenness measures how much flow passes through a node when
maximizing flow between randomly sampled source\sphinxhyphen{}target pairs.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{samples}} \textendash{} Number of source\sphinxhyphen{}target pairs to sample (default: 100)

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\{(node, layer): flow\_betweenness\}

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
dict

\end{description}\end{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This is a sampling\sphinxhyphen{}based approximation of flow betweenness. The
implementation samples random pairs of supra\sphinxhyphen{}graph nodes and computes
the maximum flow through each intermediate node.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Unlike classical Freeman flow betweenness which uses a normalization
factor based on the number of nodes, this implementation returns the
average flow per sampled pair without additional normalization. For
multilayer networks, the number of supra\sphinxhyphen{}graph nodes (N * L for N
physical nodes and L layers) affects the raw values.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For large networks, this sampling approach is more computationally
feasible than computing exact flow betweenness for all pairs.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\index{harmonic\_closeness\_centrality() (py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.centrality.MultilayerCentrality method)@\spxentry{harmonic\_closeness\_centrality()}\spxextra{py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.centrality.MultilayerCentrality method}}

\begin{savenotes}\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.algorithms.multilayer_algorithms.centrality.MultilayerCentrality.harmonic_closeness_centrality}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret
{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{harmonic\_closeness\_centrality}}}
{}
{}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute harmonic closeness centrality on the supra\sphinxhyphen{}graph.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Harmonic closeness handles disconnected graphs better than standard closeness
by summing the reciprocals of distances instead of taking reciprocal of sum.

\sphinxAtStartPar
HC(u) = sum\_\{v≠u\} (1 / d(u,v)) for finite distances
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\{(node, layer): harmonic\_closeness\}

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
dict

\end{description}\end{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This measure naturally handles disconnected components as unreachable
nodes contribute 0 (instead of infinity) to the sum.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Weight Interpretation: Edge weights from the supra\sphinxhyphen{}adjacency matrix
are interpreted as connection strengths (larger weight = stronger
connection = shorter distance). They are converted to distances via
1/weight for shortest path computation. If your edge weights already
represent distances, do not use this function directly—you would need
to invert them first or use the distance values directly in a custom
computation.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\begin{savenotes}\begin{fulllineitems}

\index{information\_centrality() (py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.centrality.MultilayerCentrality method)@\spxentry{information\_centrality()}\spxextra{py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.centrality.MultilayerCentrality method}}

\begin{savenotes}\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.algorithms.multilayer_algorithms.centrality.MultilayerCentrality.information_centrality}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret
{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{information\_centrality}}}
{}
{}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute Information Centrality (Stephenson\sphinxhyphen{}Zelen style) on the supra\sphinxhyphen{}graph.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Information centrality measures the importance of a node based on the
information flow through the network. It uses the inverse of a modified
Laplacian matrix.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\{(node, layer): information\_centrality\}

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
dict

\end{description}\end{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This implementation returns values for each node\sphinxhyphen{}layer pair in the
supra\sphinxhyphen{}graph, not aggregated physical node values. To obtain physical
node\sphinxhyphen{}level information centrality, use the aggregate\_to\_node\_level()
method on the returned dictionary.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The implementation uses NetworkX’s information\_centrality for computation.
Falls back to harmonic closeness if information centrality computation fails.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Information centrality is defined only for undirected graphs. For directed
networks, the graph is symmetrized with a warning.
\end{sphinxadmonition}
\subsubsection*{References}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Stephenson, K., \& Zelen, M. (1989). Rethinking centrality: Methods and
examples. Social Networks, 11(1), 1\sphinxhyphen{}37.

\end{itemize}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute Katz\sphinxhyphen{}Bonacich centrality on the supra\sphinxhyphen{}graph.

z = Σ\_\{t=0\}\textasciicircum{}\(\infty\) α\textasciicircum{}t M\textasciicircum{}t b = (I \sphinxhyphen{} αM)\textasciicircum{}\{\sphinxhyphen{}1\} b

\index{load\_centrality() (py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.centrality.MultilayerCentrality method)@\spxentry{load\_centrality()}\spxextra{py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.centrality.MultilayerCentrality method}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute load centrality (shortest\sphinxhyphen{}path load).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Load centrality measures the fraction of shortest paths that pass
through each node, counting all paths (not just unique pairs).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Load{[}k{]} = sum over all (s,t) pairs of {[}number of shortest paths through k / total shortest paths{]}
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\{(node, layer): load\_centrality\}

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
dict

\end{description}\end{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This is similar to betweenness but counts all paths rather than
normalizing by the number of node pairs.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\index{local\_efficiency\_centrality() (py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.centrality.MultilayerCentrality method)@\spxentry{local\_efficiency\_centrality()}\spxextra{py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.centrality.MultilayerCentrality method}}

\begin{savenotes}\begin{fulllineitems}

{}
{}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute local efficiency centrality.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Local efficiency measures how efficiently information is exchanged among
a node’s neighbors when the node is removed. It quantifies the fault
tolerance of the network.

\sphinxAtStartPar
LE(u) = (1 / ({\color{red}\bfseries{}|N\_u|*(|N\_u|}\sphinxhyphen{}1))) * sum\_\{i≠j in N\_u\} {[}1 / d(i,j){]}
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\{(node, layer): local\_efficiency\}

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
dict

\end{description}\end{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For nodes with less than 2 neighbors, local efficiency is 0.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\index{lp\_aggregated\_centrality() (py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.centrality.MultilayerCentrality method)@\spxentry{lp\_aggregated\_centrality()}\spxextra{py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.centrality.MultilayerCentrality method}}

\begin{savenotes}\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.algorithms.multilayer_algorithms.centrality.MultilayerCentrality.lp_aggregated_centrality}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret
{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{lp\_aggregated\_centrality}}}
{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{layer\_centralities}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{p}\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{default_value}{2}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{weights}\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{default_value}{None}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{exclude\_missing}\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{default_value}{True}}}
{}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute Lp\sphinxhyphen{}aggregated per\sphinxhyphen{}layer centrality.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Aggregates per\sphinxhyphen{}layer centrality values using Lp norm.

\sphinxAtStartPar
C\_i = (sum\_\{ℓ in L\_i\} w\_ℓ * {\color{red}\bfseries{}|c\textasciicircum{}ℓ{[}i{]}|\textasciicircum{}p)\textasciicircum{}\{1/p\}  for p \textless{} \(\infty\)
C\_i = max\_\{ℓ in L\_i\} (w\_ℓ * |c\textasciicircum{}ℓ{[}i{]}|})          for p = \(\infty\)

\sphinxAtStartPar
where L\_i is the set of layers where node i exists.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{layer\_centralities}} \textendash{} dict of \{layer: \{node: centrality\}\} or
\{(node, layer): centrality\}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{p}} \textendash{} Lp norm parameter (default: 2). Use float(‘inf’) for L\sphinxhyphen{}infinity norm.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{weights}} \textendash{} dict of \{layer: weight\}. If None, uniform weights are used.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{exclude\_missing}} \textendash{} If True (default), only aggregate over layers where
the node exists (has a centrality value). If False,
treat nodes absent from a layer as having zero centrality,
which may bias scores for nodes with sparse layer
participation.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\{node: aggregated\_centrality\}

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
dict

\end{description}\end{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This is a framework for aggregating any per\sphinxhyphen{}layer centrality measure.
Input can be degree, PageRank, eigenvector, etc.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Sparse Layer Participation: When exclude\_missing=True (default), nodes
that only appear in a subset of layers are aggregated only over those
layers where they exist. This prevents bias against nodes with sparse
layer participation. When exclude\_missing=False, missing layers contribute
zero to the aggregation, which may penalize nodes that don’t appear in
all layers.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\index{multilayer\_betweenness\_centrality() (py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.centrality.MultilayerCentrality method)@\spxentry{multilayer\_betweenness\_centrality()}\spxextra{py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.centrality.MultilayerCentrality method}}

\begin{savenotes}\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.algorithms.multilayer_algorithms.centrality.MultilayerCentrality.multilayer_betweenness_centrality}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret
{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{multilayer\_betweenness\_centrality}}}
{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{normalized}\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{default_value}{True}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{endpoints}\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{default_value}{False}}}
{}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute betweenness centrality on the supra\sphinxhyphen{}graph.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For each node\sphinxhyphen{}layer pair (i,α), computes the fraction of shortest
paths between all pairs of nodes that pass through (i,α).
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{normalized}} \textendash{} Whether to normalize the betweenness values.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{endpoints}} \textendash{} Whether to include endpoints in path counts.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\{(node, layer): betweenness\_centrality\}

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
dict

\end{description}\end{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This is computationally expensive for large networks as it
requires computing shortest paths between all pairs of nodes.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Weight handling: Edge weights from the supra\sphinxhyphen{}adjacency matrix are
converted to distances (1/weight) for shortest path computation.
Weights must be positive (\textgreater{} 0). Zero or negative weights will
cause undefined behavior.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\index{multilayer\_closeness\_centrality() (py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.centrality.MultilayerCentrality method)@\spxentry{multilayer\_closeness\_centrality()}\spxextra{py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.centrality.MultilayerCentrality method}}

\begin{savenotes}\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.algorithms.multilayer_algorithms.centrality.MultilayerCentrality.multilayer_closeness_centrality}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret
{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{multilayer\_closeness\_centrality}}}
{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{normalized}\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{default_value}{True}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{wf\_improved}\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{default_value}{True}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{variant}\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{default_value}{\textquotesingle{}standard\textquotesingle{}}}}
{}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute closeness centrality on the supra\sphinxhyphen{}graph.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For each node\sphinxhyphen{}layer pair (i,α), computes:
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Standard closeness:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
C\_c(i,α) = (n\sphinxhyphen{}1) / Σ\_\{(j,β)\} d((i,α), (j,β))

\sphinxlineitem{Harmonic closeness (recommended for disconnected networks):}
\sphinxAtStartPar
HC(i,α) = Σ\_\{(j,β)≠(i,α)\} 1/d((i,α), (j,β))

\end{description}

\sphinxAtStartPar
where d((i,α), (j,β)) is the shortest path distance in the supra\sphinxhyphen{}graph.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{normalized}} \textendash{} This parameter is kept for API compatibility but has no effect.
Standard closeness is always normalized by (n\sphinxhyphen{}1) per the
NetworkX implementation. Harmonic closeness returns unnormalized
sums of reciprocal distances by definition.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{wf\_improved}} \textendash{} If True, use Wasserman\sphinxhyphen{}Faust improved closeness scaling
for disconnected graphs. Default is True. This affects
the magnitude and ordering of scores in graphs with
multiple components (e.g., low interlayer coupling).
See NetworkX documentation for details. Only used when
variant=’standard’.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{variant}} \textendash{} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Closeness variant to use. Options:
\sphinxhyphen{} ‘standard’: Classic closeness (reciprocal of sum of distances).
\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For disconnected graphs, uses Wasserman\sphinxhyphen{}Faust scaling if
wf\_improved=True. Can produce biased values for nodes in
small or disconnected components.
\end{quote}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
’harmonic’: Harmonic closeness (sum of reciprocal distances).
Mathematically well\sphinxhyphen{}defined for disconnected networks:
unreachable nodes contribute 0 instead of infinity.
Recommended for disconnected multilayer networks.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
’auto’: Automatically selects ‘harmonic’ if the supra\sphinxhyphen{}graph
has multiple connected components, otherwise uses ‘standard’.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Default is ‘standard’ for backward compatibility.


\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\{(node, layer): closeness\_centrality\}

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
dict

\end{description}\end{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This implementation uses NetworkX’s shortest path algorithms on
the supra\sphinxhyphen{}graph representation. For large networks, this can be
computationally expensive.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For disconnected multilayer graphs (e.g., layers with no inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer
coupling, or networks with isolated components), use variant=’harmonic’
or variant=’auto’ to get mathematically consistent closeness values.
The harmonic variant naturally handles unreachable nodes by summing
1/d for finite distances only (infinite distances contribute 0).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Weight Interpretation: Edge weights from the supra\sphinxhyphen{}adjacency matrix
are interpreted as connection strengths (larger weight = stronger
connection). They are converted to distances via 1/weight for
shortest path computation. If your edge weights already represent
distances, use them directly without this function’s weight inversion.
\end{sphinxadmonition}
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} For connected networks, standard closeness works well}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{closeness} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{calc}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multilayer\PYGZus{}closeness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{variant}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{standard}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} For potentially disconnected networks, use harmonic}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{closeness} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{calc}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multilayer\PYGZus{}closeness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{variant}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{harmonic}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Let the algorithm decide based on connectivity}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{closeness} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{calc}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multilayer\PYGZus{}closeness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{variant}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{auto}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

Compute PageRank centrality on the supra\sphinxhyphen{}graph.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Uses the standard PageRank algorithm on the supra\sphinxhyphen{}adjacency matrix
representing the multilayer network. Properly handles dangling nodes
(nodes with no outgoing edges) via teleportation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This implementation preserves sparsity when possible for memory efficiency.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{damping}} \textendash{} Damping parameter (typically 0.85).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{max\_iter}} \textendash{} Maximum number of iterations.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{tol}} \textendash{} Tolerance for convergence.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\{(node, layer): centrality\_value\}

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
dict

\end{description}\end{quote}
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Mathematical Invariants:}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
PageRank values sum to 1.0 (within tol=1e\sphinxhyphen{}6)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
All values are non\sphinxhyphen{}negative

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Converges for strongly connected components or with teleportation

\end{itemize}

\end{description}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\index{percolation\_centrality() (py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.centrality.MultilayerCentrality method)@\spxentry{percolation\_centrality()}\spxextra{py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.centrality.MultilayerCentrality method}}

\begin{savenotes}\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.algorithms.multilayer_algorithms.centrality.MultilayerCentrality.percolation_centrality}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret
{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{percolation\_centrality}}}
{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{edge\_activation\_prob}\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{default_value}{0.5}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{trials}\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{default_value}{100}}}
{}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute percolation centrality using bond percolation Monte Carlo simulation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This implementation measures the average relative component size that a node
belongs to across multiple bond percolation realizations, providing an estimate
of a node’s importance for network connectivity under random edge failures.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{edge\_activation\_prob}} \textendash{} Probability that an edge is active (default: 0.5)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{trials}} \textendash{} Number of Monte Carlo trials (default: 100)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\{(node, layer): percolation\_centrality\}

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
dict

\end{description}\end{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This is a component\sphinxhyphen{}size\sphinxhyphen{}based percolation measure, not the path\sphinxhyphen{}based
percolation betweenness from the original Piraveenan et al. literature,
which requires recomputing betweenness on each percolated realization.
The original percolation centrality is computationally expensive (O(n\(\sp{\text{3}}\))
per trial), so this implementation provides a more efficient alternative
that captures related connectivity information.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Values are normalized to {[}0, 1{]} range where higher values indicate nodes
that tend to belong to larger connected components across percolation
realizations.
\end{sphinxadmonition}
\subsubsection*{References}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Piraveenan, M., Prokopenko, M., \& Hossain, L. (2013). Percolation
centrality: Quantifying graph\sphinxhyphen{}theoretic impact of nodes during
percolation in networks. PloS one, 8(1), e53095.

\end{itemize}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\index{spreading\_centrality() (py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.centrality.MultilayerCentrality method)@\spxentry{spreading\_centrality()}\spxextra{py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.centrality.MultilayerCentrality method}}

\begin{savenotes}\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.algorithms.multilayer_algorithms.centrality.MultilayerCentrality.spreading_centrality}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret
{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{spreading\_centrality}}}
{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{beta}\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{default_value}{0.2}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{mu}\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{default_value}{0.1}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{trials}\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{default_value}{50}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{steps}\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{default_value}{100}}}
{}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute spreading (epidemic) centrality using SIR model.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Spreading centrality measures how influential a node is in spreading
information or disease through the network, based on Monte Carlo
simulations of discrete\sphinxhyphen{}time SIR dynamics.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{beta}} \textendash{} Infection rate per edge per time step (default: 0.2)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{mu}} \textendash{} Recovery rate per time step (default: 0.1)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{trials}} \textendash{} Number of simulation trials per node (default: 50)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{steps}} \textendash{} Maximum simulation steps (default: 100)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\{(node, layer): spreading\_centrality\}

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
dict

\end{description}\end{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This measures the average outbreak size (fraction of nodes ever infected)
when seeding the epidemic from each node. Values are normalized by the
total number of nodes, producing scores in the range {[}1/n, 1{]} where n is
the number of supra\sphinxhyphen{}graph nodes.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is an empirical simulation\sphinxhyphen{}based measure, not normalized by
theoretical epidemic threshold or branching factor as in some literature
definitions. The normalization allows comparison of relative spreading
power within the network but may not be directly comparable across
networks of different sizes or structures.
\end{sphinxadmonition}
\subsubsection*{References}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Kitsak, M., et al. (2010). Identification of influential spreaders
in complex networks. Nature physics, 6(11), 888\sphinxhyphen{}893.

\end{itemize}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{supra\_matrix}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{spmatrix}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{normalize}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{bool}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{True}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{use\_sparse}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{bool}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{True}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{max\_iter}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{int}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{100}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{tol}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{float}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{1e\sphinxhyphen{}06}}}
{{ $\rightarrow$ ndarray}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute communicability centrality for each node\sphinxhyphen{}layer pair.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Communicability centrality measures the weighted sum of all walks between
nodes, with exponentially decaying weights for longer walks. It is computed
as the row sum of the matrix exponential:
\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
c\_i = sum\_j (exp(A))\_ij
\end{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This implementation uses scipy.sparse.linalg.expm\_multiply for efficient
sparse matrix exponential computation.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{supra\_matrix}} \textendash{} Sparse supra\sphinxhyphen{}adjacency matrix (n x n).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{normalize}} \textendash{} If True, normalize output to sum to 1.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{use\_sparse}} \textendash{} If True, use sparse matrix operations. Falls back to dense
for matrices smaller than 10000 elements.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{max\_iter}} \textendash{} Maximum number of iterations for sparse approximation (currently unused).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{tol}} \textendash{} Tolerance for convergence (currently unused).

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Communicability centrality scores for each node\sphinxhyphen{}layer pair (n,).

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
np.ndarray

\sphinxlineitem{Raises}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.exceptions.Py3plexMatrixError}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{Py3plexMatrixError}}}}} \textendash{} If matrix is invalid (non\sphinxhyphen{}square, empty, etc.).

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Example}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{core}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{random\PYGZus{}generators}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{net} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{random\PYGZus{}generators}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{random\PYGZus{}multiplex\PYGZus{}ER}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{50}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{3}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.1}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{A} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{net}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}supra\PYGZus{}adjacency\PYGZus{}matrix}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{comm} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{communicability\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{A}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Communicability centrality computed for }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{comm}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ node\PYGZhy{}layer pairs}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

{}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute all available centrality measures for a multilayer network.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{network}} \textendash{} py3plex multi\_layer\_network object

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{include\_path\_based}} \textendash{} Whether to include computationally expensive path\sphinxhyphen{}based measures
(betweenness, closeness). Default: False

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{include\_advanced}} \textendash{} Whether to include advanced measures (HITS, current\sphinxhyphen{}flow,
communicability, k\sphinxhyphen{}core). Default: False

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{include\_extended}} \textendash{} Whether to include extended measures (information, accessibility,
percolation, spreading, collective influence, load, flow betweenness,
harmonic, bridging, local efficiency). Default: False

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{preset}} \textendash{} Convenience parameter to set all inclusion flags at once. Options:
\sphinxhyphen{} ‘basic’: Only degree and eigenvector\sphinxhyphen{}based measures (default behavior)
\sphinxhyphen{} ‘standard’: Includes path\sphinxhyphen{}based measures
\sphinxhyphen{} ‘advanced’: Includes path\sphinxhyphen{}based and advanced measures
\sphinxhyphen{} ‘all’: Includes all measures (path\sphinxhyphen{}based, advanced, and extended)
\sphinxhyphen{} None: Use individual flags (default)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{wf\_improved}} \textendash{} If True, use Wasserman\sphinxhyphen{}Faust improved scaling for closeness
centrality in disconnected graphs. Default: True. Only used when
closeness\_variant=’standard’.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{closeness\_variant}} \textendash{} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Variant of closeness centrality to use. Options:
\sphinxhyphen{} ‘standard’: Classic closeness (reciprocal of sum of distances).
\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Uses Wasserman\sphinxhyphen{}Faust scaling if wf\_improved=True.
\end{quote}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
’harmonic’: Harmonic closeness (sum of reciprocal distances).
Recommended for disconnected multilayer networks.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
’auto’: Automatically selects ‘harmonic’ if the network has
disconnected components, otherwise uses ‘standard’.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Default: ‘standard’ for backward compatibility.


\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Dictionary containing all computed centrality measures with keys:}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Degree\sphinxhyphen{}based: “layer\_degree”, “layer\_strength”, “supra\_degree”,
“supra\_strength”, “overlapping\_degree”, “overlapping\_strength”,
“participation\_coefficient”, “participation\_coefficient\_strength”

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Eigenvector\sphinxhyphen{}based: “multiplex\_eigenvector”, “eigenvector\_versatility”,
“katz\_bonacich”, “pagerank”

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Path\sphinxhyphen{}based (if include\_path\_based=True): “closeness”, “betweenness”

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Advanced (if include\_advanced=True): “hits”, “current\_flow\_closeness”,
“current\_flow\_betweenness”, “subgraph\_centrality”,
“total\_communicability”, “multiplex\_k\_core”

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Extended (if include\_extended=True): “information”, “communicability\_betweenness”,
“accessibility”, “harmonic\_closeness”, “local\_efficiency”, “edge\_betweenness”,
“bridging”, “percolation”, “spreading”, “collective\_influence”, “load”,
“flow\_betweenness”

\end{itemize}

\end{description}


\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
dict

\end{description}\end{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Path\sphinxhyphen{}based, advanced, and extended measures are computationally expensive for large
networks. Use flags or presets to control which measures are computed.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For disconnected multilayer graphs (e.g., networks without inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer coupling,
or with isolated components), use closeness\_variant=’harmonic’ or ‘auto’ to
get mathematically consistent closeness values.
\end{sphinxadmonition}
