\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret
{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.centrality.}}\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{katz\_centrality}}}
{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{supra\_matrix}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{spmatrix}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{alpha}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{float\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{p}{|}\DUrole{w}{ }None}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{None}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{beta}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{float}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{1.0}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{tol}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{float}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{1e\sphinxhyphen{}06}}}
{{ $\rightarrow$ ndarray}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute Katz centrality for each node\sphinxhyphen{}layer pair.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Katz centrality measures node influence by accounting for all paths with
exponentially decaying weights. It is computed as:
\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
x = (I \sphinxhyphen{} alpha * A)\textasciicircum{}\{\sphinxhyphen{}1\} * beta * 1
\end{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
where alpha \textless{} 1/lambda\_max(A) to ensure convergence. If alpha is not
provided, it defaults to 0.85 / lambda\_max(A).
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{supra\_matrix}} \textendash{} Sparse supra\sphinxhyphen{}adjacency matrix (n x n).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{alpha}} \textendash{} Attenuation parameter. Must be less than 1/spectral\_radius(A).
If None, defaults to 0.85 / lambda\_max(A).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{beta}} \textendash{} Weight of exogenous influence (typically 1.0).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{tol}} \textendash{} Tolerance for eigenvalue computation.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Katz centrality scores for each node\sphinxhyphen{}layer pair (n,).}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Normalized to sum to 1.

\end{description}


\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
np.ndarray

\sphinxlineitem{Raises}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.exceptions.Py3plexMatrixError}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{Py3plexMatrixError}}}}} \textendash{} If matrix is invalid or alpha is out of valid range.

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Example}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{core}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{random\PYGZus{}generators}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{net} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{random\PYGZus{}generators}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{random\PYGZus{}multiplex\PYGZus{}ER}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{50}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{3}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.1}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{A} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{net}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}supra\PYGZus{}adjacency\PYGZus{}matrix}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{katz} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{katz\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{A}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Katz centrality computed for }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{katz}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ node\PYGZhy{}layer pairs}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} With custom alpha}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{katz\PYGZus{}custom} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{katz\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{A}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{alpha}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.05}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\index{module@\spxentry{module}!py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.multixrank@\spxentry{py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.multixrank}}\index{py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.multixrank@\spxentry{py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.multixrank}!module@\spxentry{module}}\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:module-py3plex.algorithms.multilayer_algorithms.multixrank}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
MultiXRank: Random Walk with Restart on Universal Multilayer Networks

\sphinxAtStartPar
This module implements the MultiXRank algorithm described in:
Baptista et al. (2022), “Universal multilayer network exploration by random walk
with restart”, Communications Physics, 5, 170.

\sphinxAtStartPar
MultiXRank performs random walk with restart (RWR) on a supra\sphinxhyphen{}heterogeneous
adjacency matrix built from multiple multiplexes connected by bipartite blocks.

Bases: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{object}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
MultiXRank: Universal multilayer network exploration by random walk with restart.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This class implements the MultiXRank algorithm for node prioritization and
ranking in universal multilayer networks. It builds a supra\sphinxhyphen{}heterogeneous
adjacency matrix from multiple multiplexes and bipartite inter\sphinxhyphen{}multiplex
connections, then performs random walk with restart.

\sphinxhyphen{} ‘ignore’: Leave as zero (not recommended for RWR)

\index{module@\spxentry{module}!py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.supra\_matrix\_function\_centrality@\spxentry{py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.supra\_matrix\_function\_centrality}}\index{py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.supra\_matrix\_function\_centrality@\spxentry{py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.supra\_matrix\_function\_centrality}!module@\spxentry{module}}\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:module-py3plex.algorithms.multilayer_algorithms.supra_matrix_function_centrality}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Supra Matrix Function Centralities for Multilayer Networks.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This module implements centrality measures based on matrix functions of the
supra\sphinxhyphen{}adjacency matrix, including:
\sphinxhyphen{} Communicability Centrality (Estrada \& Hatano, 2008)
\sphinxhyphen{} Katz Centrality (Katz, 1953)

\sphinxAtStartPar
These measures operate directly on the sparse supra\sphinxhyphen{}adjacency matrix obtained
from multi\_layer\_network.get\_supra\_adjacency\_matrix().
\subsubsection*{References}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Estrada, E., \& Hatano, N. (2008). Communicability in complex networks.
Physical Review E, 77(3), 036111.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Katz, L. (1953). A new status index derived from sociometric analysis.
Psychometrika, 18(1), 39\sphinxhyphen{}43.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Authors: py3plex contributors
Date: October 2025 (Phase II)
\index{communicability\_centrality() (in module py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.supra\_matrix\_function\_centrality)@\spxentry{communicability\_centrality()}\spxextra{in module py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.supra\_matrix\_function\_centrality}}

\begin{savenotes}\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.algorithms.multilayer_algorithms.supra_matrix_function_centrality.communicability_centrality}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret
{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.supra\_matrix\_function\_centrality.}}\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{communicability\_centrality}}}
{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{supra\_matrix}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{spmatrix}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{normalize}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{bool}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{True}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{use\_sparse}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{bool}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{True}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{max\_iter}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{int}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{100}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{tol}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{float}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{1e\sphinxhyphen{}06}}}
{{ $\rightarrow$ ndarray}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute communicability centrality for each node\sphinxhyphen{}layer pair.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Communicability centrality measures the weighted sum of all walks between
nodes, with exponentially decaying weights for longer walks. It is computed
as the row sum of the matrix exponential:
\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
c\_i = sum\_j (exp(A))\_ij
\end{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This implementation uses scipy.sparse.linalg.expm\_multiply for efficient
sparse matrix exponential computation.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{supra\_matrix}} \textendash{} Sparse supra\sphinxhyphen{}adjacency matrix (n x n).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{normalize}} \textendash{} If True, normalize output to sum to 1.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{use\_sparse}} \textendash{} If True, use sparse matrix operations. Falls back to dense
for matrices smaller than 10000 elements.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{max\_iter}} \textendash{} Maximum number of iterations for sparse approximation (currently unused).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{tol}} \textendash{} Tolerance for convergence (currently unused).

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Communicability centrality scores for each node\sphinxhyphen{}layer pair (n,).

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
np.ndarray

\sphinxlineitem{Raises}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.exceptions.Py3plexMatrixError}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{Py3plexMatrixError}}}}} \textendash{} If matrix is invalid (non\sphinxhyphen{}square, empty, etc.).

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Example}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{core}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{random\PYGZus{}generators}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{net} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{random\PYGZus{}generators}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{random\PYGZus{}multiplex\PYGZus{}ER}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{50}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{3}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.1}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{A} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{net}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}supra\PYGZus{}adjacency\PYGZus{}matrix}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{comm} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{communicability\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{A}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Communicability centrality computed for }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{comm}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ node\PYGZhy{}layer pairs}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\index{katz\_centrality() (in module py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.supra\_matrix\_function\_centrality)@\spxentry{katz\_centrality()}\spxextra{in module py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.supra\_matrix\_function\_centrality}}

\begin{savenotes}\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.algorithms.multilayer_algorithms.supra_matrix_function_centrality.katz_centrality}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret
{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{py3plex.algorithms.multilayer\_algorithms.supra\_matrix\_function\_centrality.}}\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{katz\_centrality}}}
{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{supra\_matrix}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{spmatrix}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{alpha}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{float\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{p}{|}\DUrole{w}{ }None}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{None}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{beta}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{float}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{1.0}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{tol}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{float}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{1e\sphinxhyphen{}06}}}
{{ $\rightarrow$ ndarray}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute Katz centrality for each node\sphinxhyphen{}layer pair.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Katz centrality measures node influence by accounting for all paths with
exponentially decaying weights. It is computed as:
\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
x = (I \sphinxhyphen{} alpha * A)\textasciicircum{}\{\sphinxhyphen{}1\} * beta * 1
\end{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
where alpha \textless{} 1/lambda\_max(A) to ensure convergence. If alpha is not
provided, it defaults to 0.85 / lambda\_max(A).
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{supra\_matrix}} \textendash{} Sparse supra\sphinxhyphen{}adjacency matrix (n x n).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{alpha}} \textendash{} Attenuation parameter. Must be less than 1/spectral\_radius(A).
If None, defaults to 0.85 / lambda\_max(A).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{beta}} \textendash{} Weight of exogenous influence (typically 1.0).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{tol}} \textendash{} Tolerance for eigenvalue computation.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Katz centrality scores for each node\sphinxhyphen{}layer pair (n,).}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Normalized to sum to 1.

\end{description}


\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
np.ndarray

\sphinxlineitem{Raises}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.exceptions.Py3plexMatrixError}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{Py3plexMatrixError}}}}} \textendash{} If matrix is invalid or alpha is out of valid range.

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Example}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{core}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{random\PYGZus{}generators}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{net} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{random\PYGZus{}generators}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{random\PYGZus{}multiplex\PYGZus{}ER}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{50}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{3}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.1}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{A} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{net}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}supra\PYGZus{}adjacency\PYGZus{}matrix}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{katz} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{katz\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{A}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Katz centrality computed for }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{katz}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ node\PYGZhy{}layer pairs}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} With custom alpha}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{katz\PYGZus{}custom} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{katz\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{A}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{alpha}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.05}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Multiplex Participation Coefficient (MPC) for multiplex networks.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This module implements the Multiplex Participation Coefficient metric for
multiplex networks (networks with identical node sets across all layers).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Authors: py3plex contributors
Date: 2025

\index{multiplex\_participation\_coefficient() (in module py3plex.algorithms.multicentrality)@\spxentry{multiplex\_participation\_coefficient()}\spxextra{in module py3plex.algorithms.multicentrality}}

\begin{savenotes}\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.algorithms.multicentrality.multiplex_participation_coefficient}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret
{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{py3plex.algorithms.multicentrality.}}\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{multiplex\_participation\_coefficient}}}
{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{multinet}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{Any}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{normalized}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{bool}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{True}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{check\_multiplex}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{bool}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{True}}}
{{ $\rightarrow$ Dict\DUrole{p}{{[}}Any\DUrole{p}{,}\DUrole{w}{ }float\DUrole{p}{{]}}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute the Multiplex Participation Coefficient (MPC) for multiplex networks.
MPC measures how evenly a node participates across layers.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{multinet}} ({\hyperref[\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.core.multinet.multi_layer_network}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{py3plex.core.multinet.multi\_layer\_network}}}}}) \textendash{} Multiplex network object (same node set across layers).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{normalized}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{bool}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{optional}}) \textendash{} Whether to normalize MPC to {[}0,1{]}. Default: True.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{check\_multiplex}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{bool}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{optional}}) \textendash{} Validate that all layers share the same node set.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Node \(\rightarrow\) MPC value mapping.

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
dict

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Notes}
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{The MPC is computed as:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
MPC(i) = 1 \sphinxhyphen{} sum\_α (k\_i\textasciicircum{}α / k\_i\textasciicircum{}total)\textasciicircum{}2

\end{description}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Where:
\sphinxhyphen{} k\_i\textasciicircum{}α is the degree of node i in layer α
\sphinxhyphen{} k\_i\textasciicircum{}total is the total degree of node i across all layers

\sphinxAtStartPar
When normalized=True, the result is multiplied by L/(L\sphinxhyphen{}1) to normalize
to {[}0,1{]} range, where L is the number of layers.
\subsubsection*{References}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Battiston, F., et al. (2014). “Structural measures for multiplex networks.”
Physical Review E, 89(3), 032804.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
De Domenico, M., et al. (2015). “Identifying modular flows on multilayer networks
reveals highly overlapping organization in interconnected systems.”
Physical Review X, 5(1), 011027.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Harooni, M., et al. (2025). “Centrality in Multilayer Networks: Accurate
Measurements with MultiNetPy.” The Journal of Supercomputing, 81(1), 92.
DOI: 10.1007/s11227\sphinxhyphen{}025\sphinxhyphen{}07197\sphinxhyphen{}8

\end{itemize}
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Contracts:}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Precondition: multinet must not be None

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Precondition: normalized and check\_multiplex must be booleans

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Postcondition: returns a dictionary with numeric values

\end{itemize}

\end{description}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\paragraph{General Algorithms}
\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:module-py3plex.algorithms.general.walkers}}\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:general-algorithms}}\index{module@\spxentry{module}!py3plex.algorithms.general.walkers@\spxentry{py3plex.algorithms.general.walkers}}\index{py3plex.algorithms.general.walkers@\spxentry{py3plex.algorithms.general.walkers}!module@\spxentry{module}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Random walk primitives for graph\sphinxhyphen{}based algorithms.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This module provides foundation for higher\sphinxhyphen{}level algorithms like Node2Vec,
DeepWalk, and diffusion processes. Implements both basic and second\sphinxhyphen{}order
(biased) random walks with proper edge weight handling and multilayer support.
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Key Features:}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Basic random walks with weighted edge sampling

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Second\sphinxhyphen{}order (Node2Vec\sphinxhyphen{}style) biased random walks with p/q parameters

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Multiple simultaneous walks with deterministic reproducibility

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Support for directed, weighted, and multilayer networks

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Efficient sparse adjacency handling

\end{itemize}

\end{description}
\subsubsection*{References}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Grover, A., \& Leskovec, J. (2016). node2vec: Scalable feature learning for networks.
KDD ‘16. \sphinxurl{https://doi.org/10.1145/2939672.2939754}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Perozzi, B., Al\sphinxhyphen{}Rfou, R., \& Skiena, S. (2014). DeepWalk: Online learning of social
representations. KDD ‘14. \sphinxurl{https://doi.org/10.1145/2623330.2623732}

\end{itemize}

\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Perform a basic random walk on a graph with proper edge weight handling.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The next step is sampled proportionally to the normalized edge weights
of the current node. For unweighted graphs, transitions are uniform.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{G}} \textendash{} NetworkX graph (directed or undirected, weighted or unweighted)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{start\_node}} \textendash{} Node to start the walk from

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{walk\_length}} \textendash{} Number of steps in the walk

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{weighted}} \textendash{} Whether to use edge weights (default: True)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{seed}} \textendash{} Random seed for reproducibility (default: None)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
List of nodes representing the walk path (includes start\_node)

\sphinxlineitem{Raises}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{ValueError}} \textendash{} If start\_node not in graph or walk\_length \textless{} 1

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{G} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{nx}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{Graph}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{G}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}weighted\PYGZus{}edges\PYGZus{}from}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{2.0}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{3}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{walk} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{basic\PYGZus{}random\PYGZus{}walk}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{G}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{walk\PYGZus{}length}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{3}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{seed}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{42}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{walk}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+go}{4}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{walk}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{]}
\PYG{g+go}{0}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Handles disconnected nodes by terminating walk early

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Edge weights must be positive for weighted walks

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Sum of transition probabilities from any node equals 1.0

\end{itemize}
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Generate multiple random walks from specified or all nodes.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This interface supports multiple simultaneous walks with deterministic
reproducibility under fixed RNG seed. Can return either node sequences
or edge sequences.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{G}} \textendash{} NetworkX graph

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{num\_walks}} \textendash{} Number of walks to generate per start node

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{walk\_length}} \textendash{} Number of steps in each walk

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{start\_nodes}} \textendash{} Nodes to start walks from (if None, uses all nodes)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{p}} \textendash{} Return parameter for Node2Vec (1.0 = no bias)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{q}} \textendash{} In\sphinxhyphen{}out parameter for Node2Vec (1.0 = no bias)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{weighted}} \textendash{} Whether to use edge weights

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{return\_edges}} \textendash{} Return edge sequences instead of node sequences

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{seed}} \textendash{} Random seed for reproducibility

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
List of nodes (if return\_edges=False)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
List of edges as tuples (if return\_edges=True)

\end{itemize}


\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
List of walks, where each walk is either

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{G} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{nx}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{karate\PYGZus{}club\PYGZus{}graph}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Generate 10 walks from each node}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{walks} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{generate\PYGZus{}walks}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{G}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{num\PYGZus{}walks}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{walk\PYGZus{}length}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{seed}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{42}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{walks}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+go}{340}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Generate walks with Node2Vec bias}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{walks} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{generate\PYGZus{}walks}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{G}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{num\PYGZus{}walks}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{walk\PYGZus{}length}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{p}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.5}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{q}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{2.0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{seed}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{42}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Get edge sequences}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{edge\PYGZus{}walks} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{generate\PYGZus{}walks}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{G}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{num\PYGZus{}walks}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{3}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{walk\PYGZus{}length}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{return\PYGZus{}edges}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{True}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{seed}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{42}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
With same seed, generates identical walks across runs

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
If p == q == 1.0, uses basic random walk (faster)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Empty walks are included if node has no neighbors

\end{itemize}
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Perform random walk with layer constraints for multilayer networks.

\sphinxAtStartPar
In a multilayer network represented in py3plex format (where node names
include layer information), this function can constrain walks to specific
layers with occasional inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer transitions.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{G}} \textendash{} NetworkX graph (multilayer network in py3plex format)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{start\_node}} \textendash{} Node to start walk from (may include layer info)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{walk\_length}} \textendash{} Number of steps in the walk

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{layer}} \textendash{} Target layer to constrain walk to (None = no constraint)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{cross\_layer\_prob}} \textendash{} Probability of crossing to different layer (0\sphinxhyphen{}1)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{weighted}} \textendash{} Whether to use edge weights

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{seed}} \textendash{} Random seed for reproducibility

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
List of nodes representing the walk path

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Multilayer network with layer\PYGZhy{}specific walks}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{core}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{multinet}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}layer}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{social}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}layer}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{biological}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} ... add nodes and edges ...}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{walk} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{layer\PYGZus{}specific\PYGZus{}random\PYGZus{}walk}\PYG{p}{(}
\PYG{g+gp}{... }    \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{core\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{g+gp}{... }    \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{nodeA\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}social}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{g+gp}{... }    \PYG{n}{walk\PYGZus{}length}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{g+gp}{... }    \PYG{n}{layer}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{social}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{g+gp}{... }    \PYG{n}{cross\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}prob}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.1}
\PYG{g+gp}{... }\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}\begin{itemize}

\begin{savenotes}\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.algorithms.general.walkers.node2vec_walk}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret
{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{py3plex.algorithms.general.walkers.}}\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{node2vec\_walk}}}
{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{G}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{Graph}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{start\_node}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{int\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{p}{|}\DUrole{w}{ }str}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{walk\_length}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{int}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{p}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{float}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{1.0}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{q}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{float}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{1.0}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{weighted}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{bool}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{True}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{seed}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{int\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{p}{|}\DUrole{w}{ }None}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{None}}}
{{ $\rightarrow$ List\DUrole{p}{{[}}int\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{p}{|}\DUrole{w}{ }str\DUrole{p}{{]}}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Perform a second\sphinxhyphen{}order (biased) random walk following Node2Vec logic.

\sphinxAtStartPar
When transitioning from node t \(\rightarrow\) v \(\rightarrow\) x, the probability of choosing x
is biased by parameters p (return) and q (in\sphinxhyphen{}out):
\sphinxhyphen{} If x == t (return to previous): weight / p
\sphinxhyphen{} If x is neighbor of t (stay close): weight / 1
\sphinxhyphen{} If x is not neighbor of t (explore): weight / q
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{G}} \textendash{} NetworkX graph (directed or undirected, weighted or unweighted)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{start\_node}} \textendash{} Node to start the walk from

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{walk\_length}} \textendash{} Number of steps in the walk

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{p}} \textendash{} Return parameter (higher p = less likely to return to previous node)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{q}} \textendash{} In\sphinxhyphen{}out parameter (higher q = less likely to explore further)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{weighted}} \textendash{} Whether to use edge weights (default: True)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{seed}} \textendash{} Random seed for reproducibility (default: None)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
List of nodes representing the walk path (includes start\_node)

\sphinxlineitem{Raises}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{ValueError}} \textendash{} If p \textless{}= 0 or q \textless{}= 0 or start\_node not in graph

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{G} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{nx}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{Graph}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{G}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}edges\PYGZus{}from}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{3}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Low p, high q: tends to backtrack}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{walk} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{node2vec\PYGZus{}walk}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{G}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{walk\PYGZus{}length}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{p}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{q}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{10.0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{seed}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{42}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} High p, low q: tends to explore outward}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{walk2} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{node2vec\PYGZus{}walk}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{G}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{walk\PYGZus{}length}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{p}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{10.0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{q}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{seed}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{42}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
First step is always a basic random walk (no previous node)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Properly normalizes probabilities at each step

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Handles disconnected nodes by terminating early

\end{itemize}
\end{sphinxadmonition}
\subsubsection*{References}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Grover \& Leskovec (2016), node2vec: Scalable feature learning for networks

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

Draw edges connecting multiple layers.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Draws curved or straight edges that connect nodes across different layers
in a multilayer network visualization. Typically used after draw\_multilayer\_default
to add inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer connections.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{network\_list}} \textendash{} List of NetworkX graphs (layers) or dict of layer\_name \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} graph

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{multi\_edge\_tuple}} \textendash{} List of tuples specifying edges to draw, e.g. {[}(node1, node2), …{]}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{input\_type}} \textendash{} Type of input (“nodes” or other)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{linepoints}} \textendash{} Line style (e.g., “\sphinxhyphen{}.”, “\textendash{}”, “\sphinxhyphen{}“)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{alphachannel}} \textendash{} Transparency level (0.0 to 1.0)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{linecolor}} \textendash{} Color of the lines

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{curve\_height}} \textendash{} Height of curved edges

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{style}} \textendash{} Style of edges (“curve2\_bezier”, “line”, “curve3\_bezier”, “curve3\_fit”, “piramidal”)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{linewidth}} \textendash{} Width of lines

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{invert}} \textendash{} Whether to invert drawing direction

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{linmod}} \textendash{} Line modification mode

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{resolution}} \textendash{} Resolution for curve drawing

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxAtStartPar
Core multilayer drawing method.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Draws a diagonal multilayer network visualization where each layer is
offset to create a 3D\sphinxhyphen{}like effect. Nodes within each layer are drawn
with their positions, and background shapes indicate layer boundaries.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{network\_list}} \textendash{} List of NetworkX graphs to visualize (or dict of layer\_name \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} graph)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{display}} \textendash{} If True, calls plt.show() after drawing. Default is False
to let the caller control rendering.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{node\_size}} \textendash{} Base size of nodes

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{alphalevel}} \textendash{} Transparency level for background shapes

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{rectanglex}} \textendash{} Width of rectangular backgrounds

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{rectangley}} \textendash{} Height of rectangular backgrounds

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{background\_shape}} \textendash{} Background shape type (“circle” or “rectangle”)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{background\_color}} \textendash{} Background color scheme (“default”, “rainbow”, or None)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{networks\_color}} \textendash{} Network color scheme (“rainbow” or “black”)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{labels}} \textendash{} Layer labels to display

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{arrowsize}} \textendash{} Size of edge arrows

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{label\_position}} \textendash{} Position offset for layer labels

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{verbose}} \textendash{} Whether to log network information

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{remove\_isolated\_nodes}} \textendash{} Whether to remove isolated nodes

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{ax}} \textendash{} Matplotlib Axes to draw on. If None, uses current axes (plt.gca())

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{edge\_size}} \textendash{} Width of edges

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{node\_labels}} \textendash{} Whether to display node labels

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{node\_font\_size}} \textendash{} Font size for node labels

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{scale\_by\_size}} \textendash{} Whether to scale node size by degree

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{axis}} \textendash{} Deprecated. Use ax instead.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Matplotlib Axes object containing the visualization.

\end{description}\end{quote}

\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{matplotlib}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{pyplot}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{as}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{plt}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Draw multilayer network as layered flow visualization (alluvial\sphinxhyphen{}style).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Shows each layer as a horizontal band with nodes positioned along the x\sphinxhyphen{}axis.
Intra\sphinxhyphen{}layer activity is encoded as node color/size, and inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer edges are
shown as thick flow ribbons (Bezier curves) where width encodes edge weight.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{graphs}} \textendash{} List of NetworkX graphs, one per layer (from multi\_layer\_network.get\_layers())

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{multilinks}} \textendash{} Dictionary mapping edge\_type \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} list of multi\sphinxhyphen{}layer edges

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{labels}} \textendash{} Optional list of layer labels. If None, uses layer indices

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{node\_activity}} \textendash{} Optional dict mapping node\_id \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} activity value.
If None, computes intra\sphinxhyphen{}layer degree

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{ax}} \textendash{} Matplotlib axes to draw on. If None, creates new figure

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{display}} \textendash{} If True, calls plt.show() at the end

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{layer\_gap}} \textendash{} Vertical distance between layer bands

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{node\_size}} \textendash{} Base marker size for nodes

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{node\_cmap}} \textendash{} Matplotlib colormap name for node activity coloring

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{flow\_alpha}} \textendash{} Base transparency for flow ribbons

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{flow\_min\_width}} \textendash{} Minimum line width for flows

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{flow\_max\_width}} \textendash{} Maximum line width for flows

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{aggregate\_by}} \textendash{} Tuple of keys for aggregating flows (currently not used, for future extension)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{**kwargs}} \textendash{} Reserved for future extensions

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Matplotlib axes object

\end{description}\end{quote}

\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{load\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{data.txt}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{multiedgelist}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Draw a force\sphinxhyphen{}directed “hairball” visualization of a network.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Creates a force\sphinxhyphen{}directed layout visualization where nodes are colored by
type/layer and sized by degree. This is a common visualization for showing
the overall structure of a network.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{g}} \textendash{} NetworkX graph to visualize

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{color\_list}} \textendash{} List of colors for nodes. If None, colors are assigned
based on node types.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{display}} \textendash{} If True, calls plt.show() after drawing. Default is False
to let the caller control rendering.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{node\_size}} \textendash{} Base size of nodes

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{text\_color}} \textendash{} Color for node labels

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{node\_sizes}} \textendash{} Custom list of node sizes (overrides node\_size and scale\_by\_size)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{layout\_parameters}} \textendash{} Parameters for the layout algorithm (e.g., \{“pos”: \{…\}\})

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{legend}} \textendash{} If True, display a legend mapping colors to node types

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{scale\_by\_size}} \textendash{} If True, scale node sizes by log(degree)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{layout\_algorithm}} \textendash{} Layout algorithm to use. Options:
\sphinxhyphen{} “force”: Force\sphinxhyphen{}directed layout (spring layout)
\sphinxhyphen{} “random”: Random layout
\sphinxhyphen{} “custom\_coordinates”: Use positions from layout\_parameters{[}“pos”{]}
\sphinxhyphen{} “custom\_coordinates\_initial\_force”: Use custom positions as initial layout

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{edge\_width}} \textendash{} Width of edges

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{alpha\_channel}} \textendash{} Transparency level (0.0 to 1.0)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{labels}} \textendash{} List of node labels to display (None for no labels)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{draw}} \textendash{} If True, draw the network. If False, only compute layout and return data.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{label\_font\_size}} \textendash{} Font size for node labels

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{ax}} \textendash{} Matplotlib Axes to draw on. If None, uses current axes (plt.gca())

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Matplotlib Axes object containing the visualization
\sphinxhyphen{} If draw=False: Tuple of (graph, node\_sizes, color\_mapping, positions)

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
If draw=True

\end{itemize}


\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Example}

\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{matplotlib}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{pyplot}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{as}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{plt}

\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{ax} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{hairball\PYGZus{}plot}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{core\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{ax}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{ax}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{legend}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{True}\PYG{p}{)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Create an interactive 2.5D diagonal multilayer plot using Plotly.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This function creates an interactive version of the diagonal multilayer
visualization, mimicking the traditional 2D diagonal layout but in an
interactive 3D environment. Each layer is positioned diagonally with
clear visual separation, similar to the static diagonal visualization.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{network\_list}} \textendash{} List of NetworkX graphs (layers) or dict of layer\_name \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} graph

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{layer\_labels}} \textendash{} Optional labels for each layer

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{layout\_algorithm}} \textendash{} Layout algorithm for nodes (“force”, “circular”, “random”)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{layer\_gap}} \textendash{} Distance between layers in diagonal direction (default: 2.5)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{node\_size\_base}} \textendash{} Base size for nodes (default: 8)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{layer\_colors}} \textendash{} Optional list of colors for each layer (HTML color names or hex)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{show\_interlayer\_edges}} \textendash{} Whether to show inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer edges

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{interlayer\_edges}} \textendash{} List of tuples (node1, node2) for inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer connections

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
False if plotly not available, otherwise plotly figure object

\end{description}\end{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Create an aggregated projection where edge colors indicate layer membership.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This visualization projects all layers onto a single 2D graph, using edge colors
to distinguish which layer each edge belongs to. Useful for seeing the overall
structure while maintaining layer information.

\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{layout}} \textendash{} Layout algorithm to use (“spring”, “circular”, “random”, “kamada\_kawai”)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{node\_size}} \textendash{} Size of nodes

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{layer\_colors}} \textendash{} Optional dict mapping layer names to colors; if None, auto\sphinxhyphen{}generated

\item {}

\sphinxAtStartPar
High\sphinxhyphen{}level function to visualize multilayer networks with multiple visualization modes.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This function provides a unified interface for various multilayer network visualization
techniques, making it easy to switch between different visual representations.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{multilayer\_network}} \textendash{} A MultiLayerNetwork instance from py3plex.core.multinet

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{visualization\_type}} \textendash{} Type of visualization to use. Options:
\sphinxhyphen{} “diagonal”: Default layer\sphinxhyphen{}centric diagonal layout (existing behavior)
\sphinxhyphen{} “small\_multiples”: One subplot per layer with shared or independent layouts
\sphinxhyphen{} “edge\_colored\_projection”: Aggregate projection with edge colors by layer
\sphinxhyphen{} “supra\_adjacency\_heatmap”: Matrix representation of multilayer structure
\sphinxhyphen{} “radial\_layers”: Concentric circles for layers with radial inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer edges
\sphinxhyphen{} “ego\_multilayer”: Ego\sphinxhyphen{}centric view focused on a specific node

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{**kwargs}} \textendash{} Additional keyword arguments specific to each visualization type.
See individual plot functions for details.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The created figure object

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
matplotlib.figure.Figure

\sphinxlineitem{Raises}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{ValueError}} \textendash{} If visualization\_type is not recognized

\end{description}\end{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Draw the graph G with Matplotlib.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Draw the graph as a simple representation with no node
labels or edge labels and using the full Matplotlib figure area
and no axis labels by default.  See draw\_networkx() for more
full\sphinxhyphen{}featured drawing that allows title, axis labels etc.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{G}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{graph}}) \textendash{} A networkx graph

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{pos}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{dictionary}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{optional}}) \textendash{} A dictionary with nodes as keys and positions as values.
If not specified a spring layout positioning will be computed.
See \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{networkx.drawing.layout}} for functions that
compute node positions.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{ax}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{Matplotlib Axes object}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{optional}}) \textendash{} Draw the graph in specified Matplotlib axes.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{kwds}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{optional keywords}}) \textendash{} See networkx.draw\_networkx() for a description of optional keywords.

\end{itemize}

\end{description}\end{quote}

\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{G} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{nx}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{dodecahedral\PYGZus{}graph}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{nx}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{draw}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{G}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{pos}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{nx}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{spring\PYGZus{}layout}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{G}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} use spring layout}

\subsubsection*{Notes}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This function has the same name as pylab.draw and pyplot.draw
so beware when using

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{networkx}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{o}{*}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
since you might overwrite the pylab.draw function.

\sphinxAtStartPar
With pyplot use

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{matplotlib}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{pyplot}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{as}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{plt}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{networkx}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{as}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{nx}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{G} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{nx}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{dodecahedral\PYGZus{}graph}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{nx}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{draw}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{G}\PYG{p}{)}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} networkx draw()}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{plt}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{draw}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} pyplot draw()}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Also see the NetworkX drawing examples at
\sphinxurl{https://networkx.github.io/documentation/latest/auto\_examples/index.html}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{nodelist}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{list}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{optional}}) \textendash{} Draw only specified nodes (default G.nodes())

same length as nodelist.

\sphinxAtStartPar

or a  sequence of colors with the same length as nodelist.

colors using the cmap and vmin,vmax parameters.  See
matplotlib.scatter for more details.

Compute force\sphinxhyphen{}directed layout for a graph using ForceAtlas2 or NetworkX spring layout.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{gravity}} \textendash{} Attraction force towards the center (must be non\sphinxhyphen{}negative)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{edgeWeightInfluence}} \textendash{} Influence of edge weights on layout

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{scalingRatio}} \textendash{} Scaling factor for the layout (must be positive)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{forceImport}} \textendash{} Whether to use ForceAtlas2 (if available)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{seed}} \textendash{} Random seed for reproducibility in fallback spring layout

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Dictionary mapping nodes to 2D position arrays

\end{description}\end{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar

faster layouts (circular, random, spectral) or matrix visualization.
\end{sphinxadmonition}
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Contracts:}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Precondition: graph must not be None and be a NetworkX graph

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Precondition: graph must have at least one node

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Precondition: gravity must be non\sphinxhyphen{}negative

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Precondition: scalingRatio must be positive

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Postcondition: result is a dictionary

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Postcondition: result has positions for all nodes

\end{itemize}

\end{description}

\subsubsection{I/O Operations}
\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:i-o-operations}}
\sphinxAtStartPar

Aggregation and Network Operations
———————————\sphinxhyphen{}
\index{module@\spxentry{module}!py3plex.multinet.aggregation@\spxentry{py3plex.multinet.aggregation}}\index{py3plex.multinet.aggregation@\spxentry{py3plex.multinet.aggregation}!module@\spxentry{module}}\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:module-py3plex.multinet.aggregation}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Vectorized multiplex aggregation for multilayer networks.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This module provides optimized implementations for aggregating edges across
multiple layers using vectorized NumPy and SciPy sparse operations, replacing
slower Python loops with efficient matrix operations.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Performance targets:
\sphinxhyphen{} ≥3× speedup for 1M edges across 4 layers compared to legacy loop\sphinxhyphen{}based methods
\sphinxhyphen{} Memory\sphinxhyphen{}efficient sparse matrix output by default
\sphinxhyphen{} Float tolerance of 1e\sphinxhyphen{}6 for numerical equivalence with legacy methods

\sphinxAtStartPar
Author: py3plex development team
License: MIT
\index{aggregate\_layers() (in module py3plex.multinet.aggregation)@\spxentry{aggregate\_layers()}\spxextra{in module py3plex.multinet.aggregation}}

\begin{savenotes}\begin{fulllineitems}

\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Aggregate edge weights across multiple layers using vectorized operations.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This function replaces Python loops with efficient NumPy and SciPy sparse
matrix operations for superior performance on large multilayer networks.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Complexity}: O(E) where E is the number of edges
\sphinxstylestrong{Memory}: O(E) for sparse output, O(N\(\sp{\text{2}}\)) for dense output
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{edges}} \textendash{} Edge data as ndarray with shape (E, \textgreater{}=3) containing
(layer, src, dst, {[}weight{]}) columns. If no weight column,
assumes weight=1.0 for all edges. Can also accept list of lists.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{weight\_col}} \textendash{} Column name or index for weights (default “w”).
If edges is ndarray, must be int index (0\sphinxhyphen{}based).
Column 3 is used if it exists, else weights default to 1.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{reducer}} \textendash{} Aggregation method \sphinxhyphen{} one of:
\sphinxhyphen{} “sum”: Sum weights for edges appearing in multiple layers (default)
\sphinxhyphen{} “mean”: Average weights across layers
\sphinxhyphen{} “max”: Take maximum weight across layers

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{to\_sparse}} \textendash{} If True, return scipy.sparse.csr\_matrix (default, memory\sphinxhyphen{}efficient).
If False, return dense numpy.ndarray.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Aggregated adjacency matrix in requested format (sparse CSR or dense).
Shape is (N, N) where N is the maximum node ID + 1.

\sphinxlineitem{Raises}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{ValueError}} \textendash{} If edges array has wrong shape or reducer is invalid.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{TypeError}} \textendash{} If edges is not ndarray or list\sphinxhyphen{}like.

\end{itemize}

\end{description}\end{quote}

\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{edges} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{np}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{array}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}

\PYG{g+gp}{... }    \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{2.0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{g+gp}{... }    \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.5}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Same edge in layer 1}
\PYG{g+gp}{... }    \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{3}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{1.5}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{g+gp}{... }\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{mat} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{aggregate\PYGZus{}layers}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{edges}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{reducer}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{sum}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{g+go}{1.5}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} With mean aggregation}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{mat\PYGZus{}mean} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{aggregate\PYGZus{}layers}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{edges}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{reducer}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{mean}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}sparse}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{False}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{mat\PYGZus{}mean}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Average of 1.0 and 0.5}
\PYG{g+go}{0.75}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\subsubsection*{Notes}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Node IDs are assumed to be integers starting from 0

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self\sphinxhyphen{}loops are supported

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
For directed graphs, (i,j) and (j,i) are different edges

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Sparse output recommended for large networks (N \textgreater{} 1000)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Deterministic output for fixed input order

\end{itemize}
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Performance:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Achieves ≥3× speedup vs loop\sphinxhyphen{}based aggregation on 1M edges:
\sphinxhyphen{} Legacy loop: \textasciitilde{}2.5s for 1M edges, 4 layers
\sphinxhyphen{} Vectorized: \textasciitilde{}0.8s for same dataset (measured on standard hardware)

\end{description}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\subsubsection{Profiling Utilities}
\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:module-py3plex.profiling}}\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:profiling-utilities}}\index{module@\spxentry{module}!py3plex.profiling@\spxentry{py3plex.profiling}}\index{py3plex.profiling@\spxentry{py3plex.profiling}!module@\spxentry{module}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Performance profiling utilities for py3plex.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This module provides decorators and utilities for tracking function execution time,
memory usage, and performance metrics. These tools enable performance regression
detection and optimization efforts.
\subsubsection*{Example}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{profiling}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{profile\PYGZus{}performance}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n+nd}{@profile\PYGZus{}performance}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{k}{def}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{slow\PYGZus{}function}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
\PYG{g+gp}{... }    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} ... computation}
\PYG{g+gp}{... }    \PYG{k}{pass}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{slow\PYGZus{}function}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Logs execution time automatically}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Benchmark a function with multiple iterations.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Runs the function multiple times and collects statistics about execution time.
Includes a warmup phase to allow JIT compilation and caching.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{func}} \textendash{} Function to benchmark

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{iterations}} \textendash{} Number of iterations to run (default: 100)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{warmup}} \textendash{} Number of warmup iterations (default: 10)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{args}} \textendash{} Positional arguments for the function

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{kwargs}} \textendash{} Keyword arguments for the function

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
mean: Average execution time (seconds)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
median: Median execution time (seconds)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
min: Minimum execution time (seconds)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
max: Maximum execution time (seconds)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
std: Standard deviation (seconds)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
total: Total time for all iterations (seconds)

\end{itemize}


\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Dictionary containing benchmark statistics

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Example}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{profiling}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{benchmark}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{k}{def}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{my\PYGZus{}function}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}

{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{func}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{Callable\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{p}{|}\DUrole{w}{ }None}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{None}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{o}{*}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{log\_args}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{bool}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{False}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{track\_memory}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{bool}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{False}}}
{{ $\rightarrow$ Callable}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Decorator to track function execution time and optionally memory usage.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This decorator measures the wall\sphinxhyphen{}clock time taken by a function and logs it.
It can also track memory usage changes if requested. Performance metrics
are stored in the global performance monitor for later analysis.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{func}} \textendash{} Function to decorate (when used without arguments)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{log\_args}} \textendash{} If True, log function arguments (default: False)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{track\_memory}} \textendash{} If True, track memory usage (default: False)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Decorated function that logs execution time

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Basic usage:
\textgreater{}\textgreater{}\textgreater{} @profile\_performance
… def my\_function(x, y):
…     return x + y

\sphinxAtStartPar
With options:
\textgreater{}\textgreater{}\textgreater{} @profile\_performance(log\_args=True, track\_memory=True)
… def expensive\_function(data):
…     \# … expensive computation
…     return result

\sphinxAtStartPar
Manual wrapping:
\textgreater{}\textgreater{}\textgreater{} def my\_function():
…     pass
\textgreater{}\textgreater{}\textgreater{} profiled\_func = profile\_performance(my\_function)

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Memory tracking requires the tracemalloc module and adds overhead.
Use it only when investigating memory issues.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute the Heaviside step function.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The Heaviside function returns 1 for positive values, 0.5 for zero, and 0 for
negative values. This is used in signed\sphinxhyphen{}rank tests for Bayesian comparisons.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{X}} \textendash{} Input array or scalar

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Array with same shape as X containing:}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
1.0 where X \textgreater{} 0

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
0.5 where X == 0

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
0.0 where X \textless{} 0

\end{itemize}

\end{description}


\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
np.ndarray

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\PYG{g+go}{array([0. , 0.5, 1. , 1. ])}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Perform hierarchical Bayesian test for comparing algorithms across multiple datasets.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This test accounts for the hierarchical structure of the data (multiple datasets,
each with multiple folds) and correlations due to overlapping training sets.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{diff}} \textendash{} Array of differences between classifier scores

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{rope}} \textendash{} Width of the region of practical equivalence (ROPE)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{rho}} \textendash{} Correlation between folds (typically around 1/n\_folds)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{upperAlpha}} \textendash{} Upper bound for alpha parameter of Gamma prior (default: 2)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{lowerAlpha}} \textendash{} Lower bound for alpha parameter of Gamma prior (default: 1)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{lowerBeta}} \textendash{} Lower bound for beta parameter of Gamma prior (default: 0.01)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{upperBeta}} \textendash{} Upper bound for beta parameter of Gamma prior (default: 0.1)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{std\_upper\_bound}} \textendash{} Upper bound multiplier for standard deviation prior (default: 1000)
Posterior is insensitive to this if large enough (\textgreater{}100)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{verbose}} \textendash{} Whether to print probability results (default: False)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{names}} \textendash{} Tuple of classifier names for verbose output (default: (“C1”, “C2”))

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{(p\_left, p\_rope, p\_right)}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
p\_left: Probability that first classifier is worse

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
p\_rope: Probability that classifiers are practically equivalent

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
p\_right: Probability that first classifier is better

\end{itemize}

\end{description}


\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Tuple{[}float, float, float{]}

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Notes}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The Gamma distribution parameters control the prior on degrees of freedom

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The hierarchical structure models between\sphinxhyphen{}dataset and within\sphinxhyphen{}dataset variance

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use when comparing algorithms across multiple datasets with cross\sphinxhyphen{}validation

\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{References}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Benavoli, A., Corani, G., \& Mangili, F. (2016). Should we really use
post\sphinxhyphen{}hoc tests based on mean\sphinxhyphen{}ranks? The Journal of Machine Learning Research.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Monte Carlo sampling for hierarchical Bayesian test.

Generates Monte Carlo samples from the posterior distribution for hierarchical
comparison of algorithms across multiple datasets with cross\sphinxhyphen{}validation.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{rope}} \textendash{} Width of the region of practical equivalence (ROPE)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{rho}} \textendash{} Correlation between folds due to overlapping training sets

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{upperAlpha}} \textendash{} Upper bound for alpha parameter of Gamma prior (default: 2)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{lowerAlpha}} \textendash{} Lower bound for alpha parameter of Gamma prior (default: 1)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{lowerBeta}} \textendash{} Lower bound for beta parameter of Gamma prior (default: 0.01)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{upperBeta}} \textendash{} Upper bound for beta parameter of Gamma prior (default: 0.1)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{std\_upper\_bound}} \textendash{} Upper bound multiplier for standard deviation prior (default: 1000)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{names}} \textendash{} Tuple of classifier names for identification (default: (“C1”, “C2”))

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Monte Carlo samples with shape (n\_samples, 3)}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Each row contains {[}p\_left, p\_rope, p\_right{]} for one MC sample

\end{description}


\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
np.ndarray

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Notes}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Uses PyStan for Bayesian inference with hierarchical model

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Data is rescaled by mean standard deviation for numerical stability

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Hierarchical structure captures both within\sphinxhyphen{}dataset and between\sphinxhyphen{}dataset variance

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Requires pystan package to be installed

\end{itemize}
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Implementation:}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Uses Stan’s NUTS sampler with 4 chains

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Each chain runs 100 iterations (including warmup)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Total posterior samples: \textasciitilde{}200 after warmup

\end{itemize}

\end{description}

\sphinxAtStartPar
hierarchical: Main function that processes MC samples
correlated\_ttest\_MC: Simpler MC version for single dataset
